article.articleHeadline: Епидемията от ебола е убила над 5000 души в Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic has killed more than 5,000 people in Congo.
article.articleSummary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is facing a Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo strain, with over 5,000 deaths and more than 10,000 infections since May, making it the largest Congo Ebola outbreak to date. Deaths have risen by about 1,000 since early October. There are no approved treatments or vaccines for Bundibugyo. The outbreak spans eight of 26 provinces, and containment is hampered by attacks on health workers following misinformation that medical staff contaminate water sources; last week a nurse was killed and another health worker wounded. Cross-border concerns are rising as Nigeria reports a case, following Congo, Kenya and Uganda as the fourth African country affected. The Congo outbreak is the second-largest globally, behind the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone), which killed about 11,000 and infected 28,000. Source: Sky News, 2026-10-31.

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية.. "بونديبوغيو" يحصد أرواح أكثر من 5000 شخص
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo... Bundibugyo ebolavirus has claimed the lives of more than 5,000 people.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo ebolavirus is driving a devastating outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with government data showing more than 5,000 deaths and over 10,000 cases since May. The outbreak has reached eight of 26 provinces, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centers. It ranks as the second-largest Ebola surge globally, surpassed only by the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak that sickened about 28,600 and killed over 11,000 in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Nigeria reported infection last week, broadening the virus’s reach to West Africa; Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases. In May, the World Health Organization declared an international emergency over Bundibugyo Ebola in DRC and Uganda. There are no approved treatments or vaccines for this Bundibugyo strain; containment hinges on isolation and contact tracing, challenged by detection delays, community conflict, and weakened health systems.

article.articleHeadline: Baby Matthew critically ill with influenza A stranded in Hong Kong as family seeks private air transfer to UK
article.articleSummary: Baby Matthew, from Nottinghamshire, is critically ill in Hong Kong with influenza A after three cardiac arrests; he is ventilated and unable to travel home by commercial flight, prompting a private air transfer arranged by Lia's Wings. The family seeks a donated long-haul aircraft to fly to the UK for NHS tests and treatment; estimated cost up to £200,000 for a dedicated air ambulance, beyond family and charity means. A specialist team (two consultants and a paediatric nurse) and equipment to adapt the jet are on standby, with both Hong Kong and English clinicians agreeing on the plan. Without repatriation, Matthew faces gradual medical decline away from home support. Travel insurance excludes repatriation. Lia's Wings notes rising demand for pediatric international transfers, assisting 68 children in six months of 2026, and over 300 since 2010. Hong Kong health authorities had warned of rising seasonal influenza A activity and urged vigilance.

article.articleHeadline: Dấu hiệu cảnh báo đột quỵ, nhồi máu cơ tim ở người nhiễm cúm
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Warning signs of stroke and myocardial infarction in people infected with influenza.
article.articleSummary: Influenza infection elevates the risk of cardiovascular events, notably myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke, especially among the elderly and those with cardiovascular disease or chronic conditions. The inflammatory response from flu can destabilize atherosclerotic plaques, promote thrombosis, and increase myocardial oxygen demand, with pneumonia or respiratory failure reducing oxygen supply further increasing risk. Early after infection, studies show about a 6–10-fold rise in myocardial infarction risk and a 3–10-fold rise in stroke risk, based on specific studies. In Vietnam, a study of 598 elderly patients with coronary artery disease and/or heart failure followed for six months post-discharge found influenza vaccination reduced all-cause readmission (25.7% vs 41.2%), cardiovascular readmission (20.2% vs 35%), and all-cause mortality (1% vs 5.2%). Vaccination complements, not replaces, treatment; maintain blood pressure, lipids, and glucose control, and seek urgent care for chest pain, shortness of breath, fainting, or sudden weakness or speech difficulty. Emphasize vaccination and hygiene, especially for those 65+ and with chronic diseases.

article.articleHeadline: Hunger deepens for millions amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks - DRC Congo
article.articleSummary: DRC Congo faces a deepening hunger crisis amid conflict, a record Ebola outbreak and climate shocks. The IPC global food security monitor estimates 28.8 million people (23% of those analyzed) will experience high acute food insecurity (IPC Phase 3+) through December, with more than 3.6 million (3%) in IPC Phase 4 emergencies. The alert, covering September 2026 through June 2027, accompanies a near six-month Ebola outbreak now exceeding 10,000 cases. The outbreak began in Ituri and has spread to eight provinces, with North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri hardest-hit at 10.4 million Phase 3+; four territories—Djugu, Fizi, Shabunda, Walungu—in Phase 4. Ongoing conflict, displacement, rising prices, floods, and El Niño-driven impacts threaten livelihoods and market access. IPC projections for January–June 2027 show 30.3 million in Phase 3+ and 4.2 million in Phase 4, underscoring worsening conditions and waning humanitarian aid.

article.articleHeadline: Peralihan Musim Bikin Anak Rentan Terserang Batuk, Pilek hingga DBD
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Seasonal Changes Make Children Prone to Coughs, Colds, and Dengue Fever.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia, including Jakarta, faces higher risk of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) in children as the dry-to-rainy season shifts, with cough, runny nose, and influenza concerns, plus dengue fever (DBD). Dr. Aisya Fikritama Aditya, SpA, a pediatric specialist from UNS Solo, explains weather changes raise infection risk through temperature and humidity shifts, altered activity, and greater pathogen exposure, not direct causation. Diarrhea from contaminated food or water and dengue fever increase with standing water, while floods heighten leptospirosis risk for children in contact with water or soil contaminated with urine of infected animals. Early warning signs include fever, malaise, vomiting, sore throat, dehydration, or respiratory distress; seek care for shortness of breath, altered consciousness, seizures, or severe abdominal pain. BMKG forecasts rainy season starting November 2026, peaking December 2026 (185 zom, 24.66% land; 266 zom, 17.31% land); El Niño may delay onset.

article.articleHeadline: Bé trai nhiễm virus hợp bào hô hấp, bệnh tay chân miệng
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A boy infected with respiratory syncytial virus and hand, foot and mouth disease.
article.articleSummary: 9-month-old boy in Hanoi presents with hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) co-infected with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), causing acute bronchitis and acute nasopharyngitis. Rapid RSV test positive; chest X-ray shows bilateral peribronchial thickening. Diagnoses: HFMD grade 1, RSV-related acute bronchitis, and acute pharyngitis. He received oral antibiotics for a mild bacterial infection, plus supportive respiratory therapy, nebulization, and care of skin and oral lesions. After six days, fever resolved, child alert, vesicles dried, mouth ulcers improved, and he was discharged. HFMD typically presents vesicles on hands/feet with mouth ulcers; most cases are mild but can have neurological, cardiac, or respiratory complications. RSV can cause lower respiratory tract infection in young children, with cough, runny nose, fever, and may progress to bronchiolitis or pneumonia, with rapid breathing and wheeze. Transmission via contact with secretions, vesicle fluid, stool, or contaminated objects; caregivers should monitor feeding and urine output and practice hand hygiene and surface cleaning.

article.articleHeadline: El número de muertos por el brote de ébola en la República Democrática del Congo supera los 5.000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of deaths from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,000 deaths with more than 10,000 infections since its May declaration. The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which no approved vaccines or treatments exist. As of Oct 27, the National Institute of Public Health (INSP) reported a 48.7% case‑fatality rate. The epidemic spans 66 health zones across eight of the DRC's 26 provinces, with Ituri the hardest hit, accounting for 71.4% of confirmed cases and about six of ten new infections. It remains massive and has not peaked, making it the second deadliest Ebola outbreak globally. It has reached Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths; 15 imported from the DRC); linked cases have been detected in Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths) and Nigeria (1 case). Delays in detection, conflict, and overwhelmed health services have facilitated spread.

article.articleHeadline: Dodental ebola opgelopen tot boven de 5000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola death toll tops 5,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed more than 5,000 people, with official diagnoses surpassing 10,000. First noted in May, it is the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak, behind the 2014–2016 Guinea-Liberia-Sierra Leone crisis (about 11,000 deaths among 28,600 infections). Weeks show a stable 400–500 new infections, a plateau not yet indicating a decline. Only about a quarter of new cases arise from people identified through contact tracing, implying most new patients were infected by individuals not yet traced. Transmission occurs via contact with infected body fluids (blood, saliva, sweat). No vaccine is available for this Ebola variant yet, though researchers hope one will be available next year. Infections have been detected in Congo, as well as Kenya and Uganda, and Nigeria. Control is hampered by weak health systems, distrust of aid workers, and regional conflicts.

article.articleHeadline: Ministry: All Ebola contacts set to leave quarantine by November 11
article.articleSummary: Kenya will be declared Ebola free after 42 consecutive days without a new case once the last confirmed patient tests negative twice (tests taken at least 48 hours apart) and is discharged. To date, nine confirmed Ebola cases and two deaths have been recorded; seven patients remain in designated facilities, and all contacts are to complete surveillance by November 11. The outbreak began with a single imported case on October 6, a traveler from the Democratic Republic of Congo via Uganda who tested positive for Bundibugyo virus; the last confirmed case in the Kenyan cluster was on October 20. Ninety-eight contacts are under monitoring and will be released in four groups beginning November 3; the first 20 were released after 21 days without symptoms. The countdown starts after the final discharge. WHO notes heightened surveillance at entry points and health facilities, with no evidence of wider transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Rio de Janeiro registra alta expressiva nos casos de mpox em dois meses
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rio de Janeiro records a sharp rise in mpox cases in two months.
article.articleSummary: Rio de Janeiro city (capital of Rio de Janeiro state) reports dozens of mpox cases over a two-month period, signaling active transmission and surpassing numbers seen in the prior interval. The outbreak indicates substantial circulation of mpox virus in the capital, with ongoing surveillance required. Transmission is mainly via direct contact with skin lesions, bodily fluids, and respiratory secretions, with intimate contact and prolonged exposure as key routes. Common clinical signs include fever, generalized body aches, malaise, and lymphadenopathy, followed by skin lesions that evolve through multiple stages until healing. Public health guidance prioritizes vaccination before exposure for high-risk groups, including laboratory professionals handling the virus, and individuals with documented close contact to suspected or confirmed cases within defined time windows to reduce symptom development and spread.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreaks in several African countries, with over 10,000 confirmed cases and a case fatality rate of 50%.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreaks have spread across central Africa, with more than 10,000 confirmed cases and a case fatality rate around 50%. The epicenter is Ituri Province in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo near the border and forests, echoing the 2018 outbreak. The Bundibugyo virus drives this wave; there are no vaccines or antivirals specifically for Bundibugyo, unlike the Zaire strain targeted by Ervebo. DR Congo has launched a vaccine trial (coded ‘Hope’) to adapt existing Zaire vaccines for Bundibugyo, but broad deployment is months away. Imported cases appear in Uganda, Kenya (9 cases), and Nigeria (1 case). Sequencing indicates a common central-DRC strain. Local mortality remains high (roughly 25–50%), while evacuated patients in Europe may have a 10–20% CFR due to advanced care. WHO has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern amid rapid spread and surveillance challenges in conflict zones and high cross-border movement.

article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) driven by a rare Bundibugyo strain has killed more than 5,000 people. Since May, the DRC has reported over 10,000 infections, with eight of 26 provinces affected and many deaths occurring outside treatment centers. article.articleHeadline: A New Report From The Independent Panel - Hiding In Plain Sight: Mpox And The Cost Of Neglecting Known Threats
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) has surged from a largely zoonotic disease of West and Central Africa to outbreaks in 82 countries with over 14,000 cases in 2026; 145 countries have reported mpox in the last four years. Madagascar reports the largest outbreak with more than 3,400 cases and 22 deaths as of mid-August. The disease now counts humans as a reservoir and has shown sustained human-to-human transmission across regions, with 3,800 EU/EEA cases and notable local spread, with painful lesions lasting weeks. In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, prior to 2022 only about one-third of suspected cases could be confirmed due to limited testing, despite around 2,000 suspected annually; vaccines and diagnostics existed but were not deployed where needed, and a global mpox vaccine stockpile was announced in August 2026. The report warns neglect and delayed tools—rapid tests, affordable vaccines—fuel repeat emergencies and urges sustained community-centered investments; lessons mirror COVID-19.

triage.headline_ja: 独立パネルによる新報告書 - 見過ごされてきた脅威：Mpoxと既知のリスクを軽視した代償
triage.triage_reason: Mpoxが82カ国・145カ国へ拡大し持続的なヒト-ヒト感染がみられる中、DRCを含む複数国での公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが報告されており、IHR基準を2つ以上満たすためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: 本記事は独立パネルによる政策提言レポートであり、新規発生報告ではなく既存のMpox流行への批評・総括。マダガスカル・アンゴラは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCは記事中で具体的な検査体制の課題等が言及されているため含めた。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus TBC Anak di Jogja Naik, Gowongan Perkuat Edukasi Keluarga
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Childhood Tuberculosis Cases in Jogja on the Rise, Gowongan Strengthens Family Education
article.articleSummary: Childhood TB prevention gains prominence in Gowongan, Yogyakarta City, Indonesia, as part of stunting reduction efforts. Gowongan Village government hosts CETING NGEBUL (Cegah Stunting Ngagem Dhahar Kembul) on 27 Oct 2026, focusing on recognizing TB in children, transmission prevention, and the importance of timely examinations and treatment, per Dr. Feli of Yayasan Uloro Jogja. The initiative highlights TB as a continuing public health issue: SITB 2022 reports 194.6 TB cases per 100,000 residents in Jogja City from 805 new cases; TB in children rose from 133 cases in 2021 to 398 in 2022. National incidence is 354 per 100,000, with Indonesia second globally to India. Elimination target is 2030. Collaboration involves Gowongan’s government, TP PKK, Tim Pendampingan Keluarga, and Tim Pelaksana Keluarga Siaga TB, strengthening family roles in TB prevention and stunting control.

triage.headline_ja: ジョグジャカルタの小児結核症例が増加、ゴウォンガンが家族教育を強化
triage.triage_reason: 既知の流行病である結核の地域啓発活動に関する記事であり、新規の異常事態や国際的拡大のリスクは認められない。
triage.notes: インドに関する言及は結核罹患率の国際比較（インドネシアが世界第2位）であり、イベント発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: ÉPIDÉMIE D'EBOLA - Les passagers en provenance du Kenya mis en quarantaine
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak - Passengers from Kenya quarantined.
article.articleSummary: Madagascar imposes a 21-day quarantine on passengers arriving from Kenya, now designated a 'special measures' country alongside the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Nigeria, per the Ministry of Public Health. The rule, under interministerial note 569 to strengthen border health measures to curb Ebola introduction, takes effect Monday. Kenya has Ebola cases, with five to six direct flights weekly connecting to Madagascar; a preparation window ends Sunday since travelers already en route cannot modify trips. Quarantined individuals will be housed in government-designated hotels, with all lodging and meals at their expense. Authorities previously feared capacity to host 500–600 arrivals from Kenya or transit through Madagascar. Travelers are urged to limit movements to avoid quarantine and prevent infection or importation. To date, Madagascar has reported no Ebola cases; two suspected cases were negative. All travelers from affected countries remain under surveillance; any fever triggers investigation.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行 - ケニアからの渡航者を検疫
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱のアウトブレイクに関連し、複数国（DRC、ケニア、ナイジェリア）が特別措置対象とされ、マダガスカルが国境検疫を導入するなど国際的な公衆衛生対応が取られているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はマダガスカルによる検疫措置が主題だが、エボラ発生国としてケニア、DRC、ナイジェリアが『特別措置国』に指定されている。対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ。ケニア・ナイジェリア・マダガスカルは対象国リスト外のため除外。DRCでの具体的な発生状況の詳細は記事内に記載がなく、特別措置国指定からの推定である点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in DR Congo passes 5,000
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has killed more than 5,000 and infected over 10,000 since its May declaration, with latest figures announced Oct 30, 2026. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved treatments or vaccines. Delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have allowed spread to eight of the DRC's 26 provinces, with cross-border cases in Nigeria and in Kenya and Uganda. This is the second-largest outbreak on record, behind 2014–2016’s epidemic of about 28,600 infections and 11,000 deaths in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone. Travel restrictions have increased: Saudi Arabia suspended travel to and entry from Kenya, barred entry for Kenyans who recently stayed in affected countries within 21 days, and paused visas. Saudi had previously suspended travel to DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan in June.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ大規模流行（死者5,000人超、感染10,000人超）が複数国への越境拡大と渡航制限を引き起こしており、IHR基準の複数項目に該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC国内での流行を主題としており、ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダへの越境例やサウジアラビアの渡航制限は言及されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれない（ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・サウジアラビアは対象国外）。治療薬・ワクチン未承認のBundibugyo株による深刻な流行で、2014-2016年の西アフリカ流行に次ぐ規模。

article.articleHeadline: Wabah Ebola di Republik Demokratik Kongo tewaskan ribuan orang
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo killed thousands of people.
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 28, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths (case fatality rate 48.6%), spanning 67 health zones in eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces. North Kivu Province, especially the Beni Health Zone, has 2,391 cases and 1,341 deaths (overall figures), with Beni recording 661 cases and 443 deaths (CFR 67%). The outbreak, declared on May 15 and caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, is the largest Ebola outbreak on record in the region and the second-largest globally. Frontline health workers face grave risk: Dr. Marie-France Shogogo died in Beni, and three doctors died within 72 hours at a Beni Ebola treatment center. Treatment facilities operate at 86.3% capacity, and only 82.2% of identified contacts are monitored (vs. 95% target). Africa CDC urged stronger protection for frontline responders.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、数千人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.6%、1万人超の感染者・5千人近い死者という大規模アウトブレイクであり、過去最大規模かつ医療従事者の死亡や対応能力の逼迫が確認されているためIHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: Africa CDCが最前線の対応者への保護強化を要請しており、国際支援の必要性が示唆されている。接触者追跡が目標95%に対し82.2%にとどまるなど、感染拡大リスクが継続している。

article.articleHeadline: CDC Cà Mau: Hai người tử vong do viêm não mô cầu đều chưa rõ nguồn lây
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ca Mau CDC: Two people died from meningococcal meningitis, both with unknown sources of infection.
article.articleSummary: Ca Mau Province's CDC reports two deaths from meningococcal meningitis in Song Doc commune, with unknown infection sources and no epidemiologic link between cases. Case 1: N.D.M., a 33-year-old woman from ấp Rạch Dinh, hospitalized Oct 27 at Trần Văn Thời General Hospital and later transferred to Ca Mau General, presenting fever and widespread rash. She had about 50 close contacts; 7 at home, and around six days before onset attended a funeral with ~10 close contacts. Case 2: D.K.N., a 46-year-old woman from ấp Tân Hòa, hospitalized Oct 22 and died Oct 23 at 19:10; she had 37 close contacts, including 2 cohabitants, a person who drove her to hospital, 10 at a shared meal, 6 around the time of death, and 3 who handled the body. No source or transmission link established. Authorities are tracing contacts; training with Pasteur Institute (HCMC) and Tropical Diseases Hospital (HCMC) aims to improve recognition, screening, and treatment. Public urged to seek care for fever or rash; note carriers may be 10–25% without symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: カマウ省CDC：髄膜炎菌性髄膜炎で2人死亡、いずれも感染源不明
triage.triage_reason: 髄膜炎菌性髄膜炎による死亡例が2件発生し、感染源・疫学的関連が不明であることからIHR基準（深刻性・異常性）を2つ満たすためフルリスク評価が妥当。
triage.notes: 2症例間の疫学的関連は未確認。接触者追跡とパスツール研究所・熱帯病病院との連携による対応が進行中。無症状キャリアが10〜25%存在するとの指摘あり、地域内での拡大リスクに注意が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 高中肺結核篩檢爆「78人共用針頭」傳已有愛滋、梅毒確診　家長氣炸衝校園討監視器
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: High School Tuberculosis Screening Reveals "78 People Shared Needles"; Reports of HIV and Syphilis Diagnoses; Parents Furious, Rush to Campus to Demand Surveillance Cameras.
article.articleSummary: Tuberculosis (TB) screening at Kangping County High School in Shenyang, Liaoning Province, China triggered controversy after parents alleged 78 students (grades 10–11) shared a single needle during tuberculin skin testing, violating the one-person-one-needle standard. Online rumors linked this to HIV and syphilis infections; authorities clarified the claim as untrue and confirmed a procedural lapse. Initial tests on the 78 students reportedly showed no abnormalities, and the government has opened investigations into the medical staff’s qualifications, potential outsourcing of screening, and school supervision. The school will conduct follow-up blood tests for HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B and C. Officials stressed that there are no confirmed infections to date, but acknowledged window periods necessitating 3–6 months of ongoing monitoring. Final accountability will be determined per investigation results and legal process.

triage.headline_ja: 高校の結核検診で「78人が注射針を共用」判明、HIVや梅毒感染の噂拡散　保護者が激怒し監視カメラ設置を要求
triage.triage_reason: 注射針共用による感染症（HIV・梅毒等）のリスクが懸念されているが、現時点で感染確認はなく、当局は3〜6か月の経過観察を行う方針であるため、続報を注視する段階。
triage.notes: 現時点で感染確認なし。医療過誤（注射針の使い回し）による血液媒介感染症（HIV、梅毒、B型・C型肝炎）の潜在的リスクに関する事案であり、当局は3〜6か月のウィンドウピリオドを考慮した追跡検査を実施予定。続報次第でリスク評価を再検討。

article.articleHeadline: Ilocos Norte logs 65 new dengue cases
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever outbreak in Ilocos Norte, Philippines: 65 new dengue cases recorded in morbidity week 42 (Oct 11–17), bringing January–October 2026 total to 2,777 cases and 4 deaths, per PESU data through Oct 29. Data cover weeks 1–42. Laoag City registered 17 new cases in week 42, highest in the province, with year-to-date total 400 dengue cases. Health authorities urge sustained prevention measures to curb transmission, including eliminating stagnant water, maintaining clean surroundings, and precautions against mosquito bites. The update highlights ongoing dengue activity in Ilocos Norte and emphasizes continued vector-control efforts to prevent further increases in 2026.

triage.headline_ja: イロコス・ノルテ州でデング熱新規症例65件を記録
triage.triage_reason: 地域的なデング熱の季節的流行であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、継続的な感染拡大が見られるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: フィリピン・イロコス・ノルテ州における地方自治体レベルのデング熱定期報告。年間累計2,777例、死亡4例で、地域保健当局による通常の媒介対策の呼びかけが中心。

article.articleHeadline: Bác sĩ cảnh báo nhiều người cao tuổi mắc cúm A nguy kịch vì nguyên nhân ít ngờ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Doctors warn that many elderly people infected with influenza A are in critical condition due to an unexpected cause.
article.articleSummary: Influenza A hospitalizations rise among the elderly in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. From Sep–Oct 2026, 49 influenza A inpatients were treated at Thong Nhat Hospital, with 16 still hospitalized as of Oct 30, including 4 on oxygen. Three cases illustrate severity: a 73-year-old N.V.Q. from Tan Binh Ward admitted Oct 29 with fever, cough, and dyspnea; oxygen saturation fell and pneumonia was seen on imaging; treated with oxygen, antibiotics, and antivirals. A 71-year-old V.Q.H. from Binh Truong Ward was admitted on day 4 with fever, productive cough, sore throat, myalgia; lung base injury; on IV antibiotics for 7 days. An 82-year-old B.N.V. from Tan Phu Ward developed pneumonia and respiratory failure with multiple comorbidities (carotid stenosis, CKD stage 3, hypertension, thrombocytosis, dyslipidemia, GERD, GI bleeding); he requires oxygen and close monitoring. All three were unvaccinated. Elderly face higher risk due to immune senescence and comorbidities; cardiovascular events risk 6–10× in the first week. Do not self-medicate with antibiotics; antivirals for those ≥65 with comorbidities; vaccination, light activity, proper nutrition, masking, and hand hygiene advised.

triage.headline_ja: 医師が警告:季節性インフルエンザA型により重症化する高齢者が多数、意外な原因で
triage.triage_reason: ホーチミン市で季節性インフルエンザA型による高齢者の重症化・入院例が報告されているが、通常の季節性インフルエンザの枠内であり、異常な病原性変異や国際的拡大の兆候は確認されていない。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザAによる高齢者の重症化事例の報告。未接種者が多く、基礎疾患を持つ高齢者のリスクが強調されているが、新型株や異常な感染拡大を示す情報はない。続報で感染者数の推移や地域拡大の有無を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola Death Toll Tops 5,000 as Cases Pass 10,000 | EconoTimes
article.articleSummary: DR Congo’s Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has infected more than 10,000 people and caused over 5,000 deaths across eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces since the May declaration. The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment. WHO notes vaccination of participants in Bunia as part of the DRC‑led Tumaini trial testing vaccine candidates against this strain. Al Jazeera cites delays in case detection, conflict and strained health services as drivers of faster spread. Cases have been reported in Kenya and Uganda, with Nigeria the fourth African country to report a case. Saudi Arabia suspended travel to Kenya, barred entry for travelers who stayed in Kenya or another affected country within 21 days, and paused visas for Kenya arrivals. As of Oct 19, the National Institute of Public Health counted 9,637 confirmed cases and 4,646 deaths; the outbreak is the deadliest Ebola epidemic in the DRC and the second largest on record.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴのエボラ死者数が5,000人を突破、感染者数は10,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 死者5,000人超・感染者10,000人超の大規模流行で、複数国（ケニア、ウガンダ、ナイジェリア）への国際的拡大とサウジアラビアによる渡航制限が既に発生しており、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ケニア、ウガンダ、ナイジェリア、サウジアラビアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCがコンゴ民主共和国として事象の主要発生地。承認済みワクチン・治療法がないBundibugyo株によるDRC史上最大規模のエボラ流行で、既に複数国への越境拡大と渡航制限が発生している重大事案。

article.articleHeadline: أكثر من 5 آلاف حالة وفاة جراء تفشي فيروس إيبولا بالكونجو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 deaths from the Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 31, 2026, more than 5,000 people have died from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 10,060 cases since the virus was first detected in May 2026. The current wave is the deadliest in the country’s history, with transmission across eight of 26 provinces and many deaths occurring outside treatment centers. Cases have also been reported in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda. The World Health Organization warned that containing an outbreak spanning East, West, and Central Africa will be highly complex. Additionally, major airlines urged the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to revisit the rule requiring travelers to certify they were not in the DRC in the 21 days before arrival.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラウイルス流行による死者5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ流行が複数国（DRC、ケニア、ナイジェリア、ウガンダ）に拡大し、渡航制限措置の見直しが議論されるなど、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大・渡航制限）に該当するため。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダでの症例報告があるが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。米国やアンゴラ、モザンビークは発生地域リストに含まれるが記事主題ではないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: TPHCM hơn 1.600 ổ dịch tay chân miệng, 5 trường hợp tử vong
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ho Chi Minh City reports more than 1,600 hand, foot and mouth disease outbreaks, with 5 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City (TPHCM) reports continuing dengue and hand, foot and mouth disease outbreaks. By week 43 of 2026, dengue has exceeded 42,500 cases with 11 deaths, while hand, foot and mouth disease tallies exceed 44,000 cases with 5 deaths and more than 1,600 outbreaks. The EV71 strain is circulating, raising concern about potential severe complications, particularly among preschool children. On October 31, 2026, a campaign launch was held in Dĩ An Ward to mobilize multi-sector action against dengue and hand, foot and mouth. Health officials call for aggressive vector control—elimination of standing water, larval breeding sites, and environmental sanitation—and for rigorous hand hygiene, disinfection of toys and surfaces, and protection in schools and family settings. They urge community participation, early case detection, and rapid local response rather than reactive measures.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市で手足口病の集団発生が1,600件以上、死亡5例
triage.triage_reason: ホーチミン市で手足口病・デング熱が大規模に流行し死亡例も出ているが、国際的拡大や渡航制限の兆候はなく、既存の公衆衛生対応の範囲内と見られるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: デング熱と手足口病(EV71含む)の同時流行で症例数・死亡者数が多く、地元当局が多部門対応を開始している。季節性流行の範囲内か、拡大傾向かは続報で確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: الكونجو الديمقراطية.. أكثر من 5 آلاف حالة وفاة جراء تفشي فيروس إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo: more than 5,000 deaths due to Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths with 10,060 cases since first detected in May. The spread covers eight of the country’s 26 provinces, and many deaths occur outside treatment centers. Cross-border cases have been reported in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda. The World Health Organization warns that containing this outbreak will be a complex task as it extends across East, West, and Central Africa. Separately, major U.S. and international airlines are urging the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to revisit rules requiring travelers to the United States to attest they have not visited the DRC within 21 days before arrival.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：エボラ出血熱の流行により死者5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が大規模流行し死者5,000人超、複数国への越境拡大と渡航制限議論が発生しており、IHR基準の複数に該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへの越境症例が報告されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。米国の渡航制限議論も対象国外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: TP.HCM ghi nhận hơn 42.500 ca sốt xuất huyết, 11 người tử vong
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ho Chi Minh City records more than 42,500 dengue fever cases, 11 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City reports more than 42,500 dengue cases and 11 deaths, alongside over 44,000 hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) cases with 5 deaths this season. In week 43 of 2026, dengue cases topped 42,500 with about 1,800 suspected cases last week—up ~10% from the monthly average—while HFMD outbreaks exceed 1,600, largely in schools, with EV71 circulating and capable of severe disease. A city-wide campaign launched Oct 31, 2026 in Dĩ An ward, led by Deputy Director Huỳnh Minh Chín, directs ward-level action to intensify environmental cleanups, eliminate larval habitats, and avoid indiscriminate spraying. The Ho Chi Minh City CDC (HCDC) will coordinate messaging and surveillance; health stations must monitor 100% of dengue risk points in Oct–Nov 2026; schools must monitor pupils, sanitize surfaces, and complete checks of at least 50% of preschools in Oct–Nov, aiming to finish all by year-end. Community teams will reinforce education and household-level interventions.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市でデング熱患者が42,500人を超え、11人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: デング熱とHFMD(EV71)の両方で死亡例を伴う大規模な流行が継続しており、市当局が大規模な対策キャンペーンを展開するなど行政の関心が高いため、フルリスク評価への移行が妥当。
triage.notes: デング熱とHFMD(EV71)の季節的流行が例年を上回る規模で発生し、死亡例も報告されているが、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは記載なし。市当局（HCDC）主導で大規模対応が進行中であり、今後の推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Saudi Arabia Halts Visas for Kenyan Travelers Amid Ebola Outbreak
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak in Kenya with nine confirmed cases and two deaths, linked to a single cluster that began when a Kenyan man returning from the Democratic Republic of Congo on Oct 3 died two days later. Eight additional infections identified among the index patient’s contacts, including relatives and healthcare workers; a third confirmed case died on Oct 23. WHO reports 20 contacts completed the 21-day quarantine and cleared; 98 remain under observation. Saudi Arabia suspends travel for its citizens to Kenya and halts visa issuances for arrivals from Kenya, forbidding entry for anyone who has been in Kenya in the prior 21 days, including via third country. Measures are part of a broader Saudi response to the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola affecting several African nations; earlier bans included DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan.

triage.headline_ja: サウジアラビア、エボラ出血熱流行を受けケニア人渡航者へのビザ発給を停止
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、ブンディブギョ株エボラの複数国にまたがる感染拡大と渡航制限措置が確認されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 主要な発生地はケニアだが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。記事は、サウジアラビアがブンディブギョ株エボラの流行国としてDRC・ウガンダ・南スーダンへの渡航制限を既に実施していると明記しており、DRCは対象国リストに含まれるため記載。ケニアの指標症例はDRCからの帰国者であり、DRCでの感染拡大が背景にあると推察される。

article.articleHeadline: Mù Cang Chải chủ động kiểm soát bệnh dại
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mù Cang Chải takes proactive measures to control rabies.
article.articleSummary: Rabies control in Mù Cang Chải commune (14 hamlets) reports no new human cases or deaths since 2022; the last fatal case occurred in 2021 (Mồ Dề hamlet, Mùa A Vùa). Ongoing risk comes from stray dogs/cats and unregulated movement. The commune issued directives for 2026 and 2026–2030, implementing a six-pronged plan: strengthen state management; tightly control dog/cat populations and vaccinate; actively detect and intervene in suspected cases; expand communication; protect humans by advising wound care and timely vaccination; ensure resources, inspection and supervision. Vaccination of companion animals reached 85% in Mồ Dề; vaccination teams visit households. About 250 people were encouraged to vaccinate, including 31 from poor households receiving free vaccination. Future efforts include a full pet census and annual vaccination to maintain no rabies deaths.

triage.headline_ja: ムーカンチャイ、狂犬病対策を積極的に実施
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病の予防的取り組みに関するルーチン報告であり、新規症例や死亡者も報告されていないため、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 2022年以降新規症例・死亡者なし。地方自治体の予防的対策（ワクチン接種、動物管理）に関する報告記事であり、危機的状況を示す内容ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Death Toll in DR Congo Surpasses 5,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000, with more than 10,000 infections across eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces as of 2026-10-30. The outbreak is the deadliest on record for the country, exceeded only by the 2014-2016 epidemic across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone. The ongoing outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no approved treatments or vaccines. Delayed detection, ongoing conflict, and strained health services have impeded containment. The virus has spread beyond the DRC to Nigeria—the fourth African country to report a case—along with Kenya and Uganda, extending exposure into West and East Africa. Authorities continue to monitor spread and assess the impact of travel restrictions and cross-border control measures as the outbreak evolves since it was declared in May.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超え、ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダへ国際的拡大が確認されており、IHR基準の複数(深刻性・異常性・国際拡大)に該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでの大規模アウトブレイクを主題としている。ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダへの拡大が言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。ワクチン・治療薬が未承認のBundibugyo株であり、紛争による対応困難も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Sốt xuất huyết, tay chân miệng chưa có thuốc đặc trị: Người dân cần làm gì?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever and hand-foot-mouth disease have no specific treatment: What should people do?
article.articleSummary: As of October 31, 2026, Ho Chi Minh City health authorities launched a dengue fever and hand-foot-mouth disease prevention campaign in Dĩ An Ward, Bình Dương Province, Vietnam. In the first ten months of 2026, the city reported over 42,500 dengue cases with 11 deaths and more than 44,000 hand-foot-mouth disease cases with 5 deaths, while more than 1,600 outbreaks were detected; combined totals exceed 86,500 cases and 16 deaths. Both diseases have no specific treatments, making prevention critical. Authorities urge ongoing household and community actions: eliminate mosquito breeding sites, remove standing water, and for hand-foot-mouth disease, promote handwashing with soap, sanitize toys, disinfect schools, and monitor children’s health. The campaign included field surveys in Di An, with 28 neighborhoods mobilized, five mobile loudspeakers, and checks at a local kindergarten (Thong Nhat) for hygiene and infection control.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱と手足口病に特効薬なし：住民は何をすべきか？
triage.triage_reason: ホーチミン市でデング熱・手足口病の症例数（計86,500件超）と死亡者（16名）が多く、重症度・流行継続性の観点でWPRO基準に複数該当し、当局による予防キャンペーンも実施されているため、フルリスク評価での確認が望ましい。ただし季節性の風土病的流行であり国際的な異常事態ではない点に留意。
triage.notes: デング熱・手足口病はいずれも例年ベトナム南部で季節性に流行する疾患であり、本記事は地方自治体による定例的な予防啓発キャンペーンを報じるもの。国際的な拡大や渡航制限のリスクは記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: 刚果（金）伊波拉疫情 已致逾5000人死亡
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed more than 5,000 people.
article.articleSummary: As of 30 October 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports more than 5,000 deaths and over 10,000 infections in the current Ebola outbreak, the deadliest on record. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain has no approved treatments or vaccines. Since the outbreak began in May, transmission has accelerated due to delayed detection, regional conflict, and an overwhelmed health system; eight of the country’s 26 provinces have been affected, with many fatalities occurring outside treatment centers. The case load and fatalities continue to rise, underscoring ongoing containment challenges. Spillover and imported cases have been reported in neighboring countries, including Kenya, Uganda, and Nigeria, underscoring cross-border risks and the need for intensified regional public health measures.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、死者5000人超に
triage.triage_reason: 死者5000人超・感染1万人超の史上最悪規模のエボラ流行で、ワクチン・治療薬が存在せず、周辺国への越境感染も報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する重大シグナルである。
triage.notes: 記事はDRC国内の流行が主題。ケニア、ウガンダ、ナイジェリアへの波及が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Эксперт Шахмарданов рассказал о частоте проявления симптомов лихорадки Зика
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Expert Shakhmardanov spoke about the frequency of Zika fever symptoms.
article.articleSummary: Zika fever in Russia remains largely asymptomatic; only about 20% of infected individuals develop clinical symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, conjunctivitis) 3–14 days after exposure, lasting 2–7 days. In adults with normal immunity, illness is typically mild with very rare deaths. The primary public health concern is risk of microcephaly in newborns or Guillain-Barré syndrome, even from otherwise mild infections. There is no specific antiviral treatment; care is symptomatic—rest, fluids, antipyretics, and analgesics. The acute phase usually ends within about one week for uncomplicated cases; most patients do not require hospitalization or special monitoring. As of 31 October 2026, a single imported case was identified in Moscow in a woman who had returned from Bali, reported by Rospotrebnadzor.

triage.headline_ja: 専門家シャフマルダノフ氏、ジカ熱の症状発現頻度について語る
triage.triage_reason: ロシアでバリ帰国者の輸入症例1件が報告されたのみで、専門家による一般的な症状解説記事であり、公衆衛生上の新たな脅威や異常性は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事はジカ熱の症状頻度に関する専門家の一般的解説が主題。唯一の具体的症例はバリ(インドネシア)から帰国したモスクワの女性の輸入例であり、ロシア自体は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。インドネシアは感染推定地として言及されているため含めた。

article.articleHeadline: Ho Chi Minh City records 42,500 dengue cases and 11 deaths in 2026
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, Ho Chi Minh City has recorded more than 42,500 dengue cases and 11 deaths in 2026. From Oct 19-25, 1,785 dengue cases were recorded, 9.7% above the four-week average, signaling continued transmission during the rainy season. Authorities warn that rainy-season breeding could drive further infections. A citywide intensive prevention campaign for dengue and hand, foot and mouth disease was launched on 31 October by the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Health and the People’s Committee of Di An ward. The plan directs health stations to inspect identified dengue risk sites in October–November, with fogging used only when indicated and not as a replacement for larval elimination. Residents should spend 10-15 minutes weekly cleaning, cover water containers, and remove stagnant water. Seek medical care for fever and warning signs of severe dengue; sustain prevention beyond the campaign. Hanoi reports new dengue clusters amid rainy season.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市で2026年に デング熱症例42,500件、死亡11人を記録
triage.triage_reason: ホーチミン市で季節性デング熱の症例・死亡者数が多いが、例年の雨季パターンに沿った拡大であり国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは見られないため、経過観察とする。
triage.notes: Bluedotが付与した疾患名に『Foot And Mouth Disease（口蹄疫）』が含まれるが、記事本文では『hand, foot and mouth disease（手足口病）』の予防キャンペーンに言及しており、動物由来の口蹄疫とは異なる誤タグの可能性が高い。デング熱は雨季に伴う季節性流行であり、ハノイでも新たなクラスターが報告されているが、国際的な拡大や渡航制限の兆候はない。

article.articleHeadline: Ca tay chân miệng tăng, TP HCM báo động nguy cơ dịch lan trong trường học
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cases of hand-foot-mouth disease are increasing; Ho Chi Minh City warns of the risk of outbreaks spreading in schools.
article.articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City reports 44,000 hand-foot-mouth disease (HFMD) cases this year, up >65% vs. the same period last year, with EV71 circulating and risk of school- and preschool-linked spread. Five HFMD deaths and over 1,600 outbreaks have occurred since January. EV71 can cause severe neurological, cardiac, and respiratory complications, especially in children. HFMD shows two seasonal peaks, March–May and September–November, the latter aligning with school return and higher contact. Authorities urge parents to seek care for fever, mouth ulcers, or vesicles on hands/feet, and for signs such as drowsiness, vomiting, ataxia, or abnormal breathing. To curb transmission in schools, health authorities require daily health monitoring, early outbreak detection, and thorough cleaning of classrooms, play areas, furniture, and toys; caregivers should wash hands and keep sick children at home. Dengue fever, with >42,500 cases and 11 deaths, is rising during the rainy season; vector control, environmental sanitation, and following professional guidance for insecticide use are urged.

triage.headline_ja: 手足口病の症例が増加、ホーチミン市が学校内での流行拡大リスクを警告
triage.triage_reason: ホーチミン市で手足口病（EV71）の症例が前年比65%以上増加し死者も発生、デング熱も同時に流行しており公衆衛生上の懸念が高い。学校を通じた感染拡大リスクがあり、WPRO基準複数該当・社会的関心も高いためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: EV71による手足口病とデング熱が同時流行しており、学校・保育施設を通じた感染拡大が懸念される。季節性の流行だが前年比大幅増加かつ死亡例あり、注意深い追跡が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Idées | Ebola galopante
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ideas | Rampant Ebola
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak now exceeds 10,000 cases: 10,224 infections, 4,964 deaths, 2,733 recoveries as of Oct 27, 2026, across 66 health zones in 8 provinces. This is the 17th outbreak in the DRC and the third involving Bundibugyo virus (no licensed vaccine or specific treatment). WHO cites challenges: dignified funerals are hard to ensure and infection control in non-Ebola facilities stands at 47.8%, with 60% of deaths occurring in communities. More than 400 health workers infected, over 50 dead; insecurity and governance gaps hinder response, including salary arrears. Community mistrust remains a major hurdle; a village-centered approach is urged. In Kenya, nine cases (eight secondary; two deaths) stem from a single imported case from DRC via Uganda (Oct 3–5), with all symptoms developing in quarantine. Tumaini vaccine trial begins in Bunia (Oct 23): first injection, testing Ervebo for cross-protection and additional vaccines; 16,000 frontline workers protected to some degree; trials for treatments and post-exposure prophylaxis ongoing.

triage.headline_ja: 意見 | 急拡大するエボラ出血熱
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行が1万人超の症例・死亡者を出し、ケニアへの国際的な伝播も確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大なシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: ケニア・ウガンダへの越境伝播が報告されているが、両国は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。治療薬・ワクチンの臨床試験（Tumaini試験）も進行中で、国際的な注目度・支援ニーズが高い。

article.articleHeadline: خبرگزاری آریا - بیش از 5000 کشته در شیوع ابولا در جمهوری دموکراتیک کنگو؛ گسترش ویروس به هشت استان
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Aria News Agency - More than 5,000 killed in the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo; the virus has spread to eight provinces.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) caused by the Bundibugyo strain has surpassed 5,000 deaths and 10,000 reported infections since the outbreak began in May. There is no approved treatment or vaccine for the current strain. The epidemic has spread across eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces, with many fatalities occurring outside formal treatment centers, highlighting access and security challenges. This year’s outbreak is the second-largest globally, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that infected about 28,600 and killed over 11,000 in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Nigeria reported its first Ebola case last week, signaling spread to West Africa; Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases in East Africa. Data cited are government-disclosed figures as of October 2026.

triage.headline_ja: アリア通信 - コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行で5000人以上死亡、ウイルスは8州に拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行が5000人以上の死者、1万人以上の感染者に達し8州に拡大、さらにナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダへの国際的拡大が報告されており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性、異常性、国際的拡大）に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア、ケニア、ウガンダへの拡大が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。承認された治療法・ワクチンがない点、治療施設外での死亡が多い点はアクセス・治安上の課題を示唆し、管理可能性に懸念あり。

article.articleHeadline: "多毒株"活跃，今年流感季提前！防护要趁早
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Multiple strains are circulating; this year's flu season is starting earlier. Take precautions early.
article.articleSummary: China CDC Weekly flu surveillance shows the autumn–winter influenza season has begun, with multiple strains circulating. Influenza A dominates: H3N2 ~70% of positives, H1N1 ~30%. The season features co-circulation of several strains and an earlier onset. Distinguishing influenza from the common cold: influenza has rapid onset with high fever, malaise, and severe systemic symptoms; cold onset is gradual with nasal symptoms and milder illness; influenza is more likely to cause complications and a 7–10 day illness. High-risk groups include children, those 65 and older, pregnant women, chronic disease patients, and the immunocompromised; pneumonia, encephalitis in children, myocarditis in young adults, and reduced appetite/withdrawn behavior in the elderly are warning signs. Prior flu infection offers weak cross-protection; A–then–B sequences can occur. Vaccination window is Nov–Mar; best timing Sept–Oct. 2026–2027 vaccines updated to include trivalent split, trivalent subunit, and trivalent live attenuated vaccines. LAIV is for 3–17 years and not advised for elderly or immunocompromised.

triage.headline_ja: “多毒株”が活発化、今年のインフルエンザシーズンは早め到来！早めの予防対策を
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザの通常の流行情報であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められず、通常の公衆衛生啓発記事と判断される。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザ（A型H3N2優位、H1N1混在）の例年通りの流行開始に関する一般向け予防啓発記事。異常な重症化や新規株出現の報告はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Anjing Positif Rabies Serang 2 Warga di Jembrana dalam Sehari, Satu Korban Digigit di Wajah
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rabid dog attacks two residents in Jembrana in one day, one victim bitten on the face.
article.articleSummary: A stray dog in Banjar Sumbersari, Melaya, Jembrana, Bali, was later confirmed rabies-positive after attacking two residents on 24 October 2026. Ni Ketut Sutari was bitten on the leg in the morning and given Rabies Vaccine (VAR); Ni Putu Sekarini was bitten on the face in the afternoon and treated with Rabies Serum (SAR) due to high-risk exposure. Laboratory tests at Balai Besar Veteriner Denpasar confirmed the dog’s rabies status, per local official I Gusti Ngurah Putu Sugiarta of the Jembrana Livestock and Animal Health Office. In response, authorities conducted emergency rabies vaccination in Banjar Sumbersari, vaccinating 21 animals (20 dogs, 1 cat) two days after the incident to curb spread. This incident and follow-up vaccination were reported via Tribun Bali and cited by the local health department.

triage.headline_ja: 狂犬病陽性の犬、ジェンブラナで1日に住民2人を襲撃、1人は顔を噛まれる
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病に感染した犬による散発的な咬傷事例で、適切な曝露後治療と緊急ワクチン接種が実施されており、インドネシア・バリ島では既知の風土病的状況のため、国際的な公衆衛生上の懸念には該当しない。
triage.notes: 狂犬病はバリ島において既に風土病化しており、本件は局地的な咬傷事例と迅速な対応（ワクチン接種・血清投与・動物の緊急ワクチン接種）が報告されている。新規性や異常性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Death Toll in DR Congo Passes 5,000 as Cases 10,000
article.articleSummary: By Oct 30, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed more than 5,000 and infected over 10,000 since it was declared in May, making it the deadliest outbreak in the country and the second-largest on record globally after 2014–2016 West Africa. It is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. Delayed detection, ongoing conflict, and a strained health system have allowed spread across eight of 26 provinces, with many deaths outside treatment centres. Nigeria has reported an Ebola case, while Kenya and Uganda have linked cases. Saudi Arabia suspended travel to and from Kenya, reflecting regional concerns. Security attacks hinder response, including the killing of a nurse and injury to another health worker in eastern Congo; the WHO condemned the incidents. The current epidemic exceeds the 2018–2020 DRC outbreak in scale.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ死者数が5,000人を突破、感染者は1万人に
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおける大規模エボラ流行（死者5000人超、感染1万人超）で複数国への拡大、渡航制限、治療薬・ワクチン未承認など、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大事案。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア、ケニア、ウガンダへの波及やサウジアラビアの渡航停止措置が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれない（ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダ・サウジアラビアは対象国外）か、主発生国でないため除外。主たる発生国はDRCのみ対象国リストに該当。

article.articleHeadline: Små barn drabbas hårdast av ebola i Kongo-Kinshasa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Young children are hardest hit by Ebola in Kongo-Kinshasa.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, hits children hardest. In North Kivu, one of four infected is a child. At an Ebola treatment center in Butembo, 24 of 30 admitted children died from June to September this year. Doctors Without Borders warns that children require stronger protection and inclusion in research on the virus, and there is no approved vaccine or treatment for the new virus. Small children have underdeveloped immune systems and are prone to rapid dehydration from Ebola-related diarrhea, making severe symptoms harder to reverse. At the transfer center in Butembo, suspected cases are separated from their families; many are too young to understand. The response uses plexiglass-sided rooms, a 'low-risk' area, and dedicated caregivers in full PPE. MSF helps clinics with infection-control measures; why children are disproportionately affected remains unclear. A recovered boy’s hug to his parents offered a hopeful moment.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国（旧ザイール）でエボラ出血熱、幼い子どもが最も深刻な被害を受けている
triage.triage_reason: 北キブ州で進行中のエボラ流行があり、子どもの致死率が極めて高く（治療センターで30人中24人が死亡）、承認されたワクチン・治療法がない「新しいウイルス」との記述から異常性も高い。国際支援団体（国境なき医師団）が関与しており、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は『新しいウイルス』で承認ワクチン・治療法がないと述べており、通常のザイールエボラウイルス（Erveboワクチンあり）とは異なる種である可能性が示唆される。続報でウイルス種と国際的拡大リスクの確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو.. وفيات إيبولا تتجاوز 5000 حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: Ebola deaths exceed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: As of October 31, 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo has recorded more than 5,000 Ebola deaths in the current outbreak, with over 10,000 people infected since it was declared in May 2026. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. Delayed detection, conflict, and weak health systems have accelerated spread, with many fatalities occurring outside treatment centers. The virus has spread across eight of the country’s 26 provinces. This year’s outbreak is the second-largest globally, behind the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak that infected over 28,600 and killed more than 11,000 in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Nigeria reported an Ebola infection last week, indicating West Africa expansion; Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases in East Africa.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：エボラ死者数5000人超
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ大規模流行（死者5000人超、感染1万人超）で、ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる致死的かつ国際拡大（ナイジェリア、ケニア、ウガンダへの波及）が報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではナイジェリア、ケニア、ウガンダへの感染拡大も言及されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。主要な発生地はDRCである。

article.articleHeadline: TPHCM tăng cường phát hiện sớm ca sốt xuất huyết, tay chân miệng chuyển nặng
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ho Chi Minh City strengthens early detection of dengue fever cases; hand, foot, and mouth disease becomes severe.
article.articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City launches a high-priority campaign to strengthen early detection of dengue fever and to curb severe hand, foot, and mouth disease through the end of 2026. For dengue, authorities require 100% surveillance of risk points across districts in October–November 2026, prioritizing areas with cases or outbreaks and re-auditing facilities not meeting standards. For hand, foot, and mouth disease, 100% of kindergartens and childcare centers with cases or outbreaks must be inspected and monitored; other facilities should reach at least 50% coverage in October–November, aiming for 100% by year-end. Health facilities must promptly identify signs of deterioration for timely consultations and transfers, and strengthen communication and weekly reporting of results.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市、デング熱の早期発見および手足口病の重症化防止を強化
triage.triage_reason: デング熱・手足口病は季節性の既知疾患で、当局が通常の監視・対策を強化する行政的な取り組みの報告であり、異常な拡大や重症化急増を示す具体的データはないが、継続的なモニタリングが必要。
triage.notes: 記事は行政の予防的対策キャンペーンの発表であり、具体的な症例数・死亡者数・異常な増加傾向のデータは記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Can International Travel Increase Your Risk of Tuberculosis?
article.articleSummary: Open Forum Infectious Diseases study (2010–2022) at a California federally qualified health centre serving a predominantly Asian American population found documented international travel associated with higher odds of TB test conversion. Among 5,668 patients with no prior TB history, at least one prior negative test, tested annually or every two years, those with documented international travel had 1.95 times the odds of converting from a negative to a positive TB test (95% CI 1.07–3.57) versus non-travelers. Most trips were to East and Southeast Asia, with >90% of recorded destinations in countries with medium or high TB prevalence. Two individuals were diagnosed with active TB after test conversion. The study cautions that travel is not proven causal and findings may not generalize beyond this single California centre. Routine TB testing for all travelers is not recommended; travel history should inform risk assessment and follow-up to distinguish latent infection from active disease.

article.articleHeadline: 三亚工地涉"登革热"风险工人被安置居民区引担忧，官方：已转移_腾讯新闻
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Sanya construction site workers at risk of dengue fever relocated to a residential area, sparking concerns; officials say they have been moved.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever risk prompted the relocation of uninfected construction workers from nearby sites to a residential area in Sanya, Hainan, amid a dengue outbreak that affected a nearby project. As of Oct 31, 2026, workers at the Sanya Hengda Meili Zhaizuan complex in Jiyang District Chun Guang Community were housed in four buildings for health monitoring, not for isolating confirmed patients; all have since been moved out. Prior to relocation, workers underwent blood sampling to rule out infection; current results were negative, and ongoing surveillance and sampling are planned. Local authorities performed disinfection and mosquito control, and residents reported a lack of advance notice. Dengue fever and chikungunya fever are vector-borne by Aedes mosquitoes; dengue presents with sudden fever, headache, retro-orbital pain, and my/soft tissue pain, while chikungunya involves fever, joint pain, and rash. No confirmed cases among workers; monitoring continues.

article.articleHeadline: Число жертв Эболы в ДР Конго превысило 5 тыс.
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola death toll in DR Congo has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has 5,026 laboratory-confirmed deaths among 10,351 cases, with a case-fatality rate of 48.6%. The outbreak began May 15 in DR Congo and neighboring Uganda and is the continent's second-deadliest Ebola event. In DR Congo, cases have been reported across eight provinces. Uganda declared its outbreak over in July, with the WHO confirming the end in August. In October, new infections were detected in Kenya and Nigeria. The data highlight the sustained threat of Ebola in central and eastern Africa and the need for ongoing surveillance and cross-border coordination to contain spread. As of 31 October 2026, it remains the continent's second-deadliest Ebola outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Schon mehr als 5.000 Ebola-Tote im Kongo | Foto: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP/dpa
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Already more than 5,000 Ebola deaths in the Congo | Photo: Sebastien Kitsa Musayi/AP/dpa.
article.articleSummary: DRCongo reports more than 5,000 Ebola deaths and 10,351 cases since mid-May, with 1,101 currently in treatment or isolation and 2,788 recovered; true totals may be higher due to undetected spread since February before the May outbreak announcement on May 15. The surge is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with ongoing international spillovers: Kenya cases tied to a Kenyan who stayed in Congo; Nigeria reporting its first Ebola case on Oct 20 linked to a Swiss diplomat's wife after Uganda travel; a European case in France (doctor) from a mission in eastern Congo in June, who recovered. No vaccine or specific therapy exists yet for Bundibugyo; transmission is via contact with body fluids causing fever, diarrhea, and bleeding. Since July, trials of two antiviral therapies and vaccine candidates have been underway; Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus vaccine) has been studied but is approved only for Zaire ebolavirus."

article.articleHeadline: 秋冬流感流行季已開啟，多毒株共同活躍！現在打流感疫苗晚不晚？
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The fall–winter flu season has begun, with multiple strains circulating simultaneously. Is it too late to get the flu vaccine now?
article.articleSummary: China reports rising flu activity. For the week ending Oct 25, southern China remains high and northern areas rise; 145 influenza-like outbreak events were reported, up from 28 last week, signaling the season has begun. Dominant strain is A/H3N2 (~67% of A samples), with A/H1N1 increasing to 32.8%; B/Victoria circulating. Multi-strain circulation and an earlier peak coincide with colder weather and indoor crowding, raising transmission in schools and offices. Flu complications include pneumonia; in children under 2, encephalitis (including necrotizing encephalitis); myocarditis and myositis; risk of liver and kidney injury. High-risk groups: children, adults ≥65, pregnant women, chronic disease, immunocompromised. Vaccination best in Sep–Oct, but still beneficial later; protection takes 2–4 weeks. Available vaccines: trivalent split and trivalent subunit for ≥6 months; trivalent live-attenuated for 3–17 years. Oseltamivir post-exposure prophylaxis for high-risk; 1 pill daily for 7 days; if symptoms develop, treat (2x daily for 5 days).

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Outbreak Kills More Than 5,000 In DR Congo
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 5,000 people and infected over 10,000 since it was declared in May, the government reported on 2026-10-31. It is the deadliest Ebola epidemic on record, with eight of DR Congo's 26 provinces affected and many fatalities outside treatment centres. Authorities have yet to find a way to bring the outbreak under control. The geographic spread has expanded to West Africa, as Nigeria reported an Ebola case last week—the fourth African country affected—while East African nations Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases. In response to cross-border transmission and travel considerations, major airlines have urged the US CDC to reconsider a rule requiring all US-bound travellers to attest they have not visited the Democratic Republic of Congo in the prior 21 days.

article.articleHeadline: Ебола в Конго: над 5000 потвърдени смъртни случая
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo: over 5,000 confirmed deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (Bundibugyo ebolavirus) has reached 10,351 confirmed cases and 5,026 deaths (case fatality rate 48.6%). The outbreak spans 67 of 178 health zones across eight provinces; Ituri remains the epicenter with 71% of cases, and North Kivu accounts for 58.4% of new cases in the last 24 hours. As of October 29, 77 new cases were identified in North Kivu, Ituri, Ot-Uele, and Chopo, with 34 deaths (20 in the community, 14 in treatment centers). 22 patients have recovered after two negative tests. The outbreak was declared May 15, 2026 and is the second largest in history; WHO has deemed it a PHEIC. Transmission in the community remains a concern, complicating contact tracing, as many deaths occur outside facilities. Authorities are expanding surveillance, lab testing, isolation, and contact tracing; counts remain dynamic.

article.articleSummary: As of 31 Oct 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reports that Ebola deaths have surpassed 5,000 in the current outbreak. Health authorities also report new and ongoing cases in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda, indicating cross-border transmission. Ebola virus disease is a life-threatening illness spread by direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of infected people, causing high fever, diarrhea and bleeding. The outbreak is particularly difficult to contain because there is no specific vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola. Laboratory confirmation remains essential for case management, surveillance, and outbreak control. The report also notes imported cases in other countries, underscoring the need for regional cooperation and strict infection prevention to prevent further exportation.

article.articleHeadline: TP Hồ Chí Minh mở chiến dịch cao điểm phòng, chống bệnh sốt xuất huyết và tay chân miệng
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ho Chi Minh City launches an intensive campaign to prevent and control dengue fever and hand, foot, and mouth disease.
article.articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City launches an intensive campaign on dengue fever and hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) on Oct 31, 2026, to curb rising cases during the rainy season and year-end. By Oct 30, 2026, the city recorded over 42,500 dengue cases with 11 deaths and more than 44,000 HFMD cases with 5 deaths, alongside about 1,600+ HFMD outbreak clusters. The EV71 dengue/HFMD strain circulation raises concerns for severe complications, especially in preschools. Campaign priorities include proactive vector control, environmental sanitation, enhanced surveillance and rapid outbreak investigation, and avoiding indiscriminate chemical spraying. In schools and child-care facilities, daily health monitoring, early HFMD detection, classroom/toy sanitization, and strong health-education collaboration among Health, Education, and parents are emphasized. Post-launch, Dĩ An ward reported high dengue activity with a death and conducted risk-point surveys with corrective actions; authorities will extend campaigns citywide. Lam Dong Province reports 87 severe dengue cases (1 death) and ~3,560 HFMD cases (2 deaths).

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市、デング熱・手足口病の集中的な予防対策キャンペーンを開始
triage.triage_reason: デング熱・手足口病ともに症例数・死亡者数が多く、EV71株流行による重症化懸念があり、市・省当局が集中対策キャンペーンを開始するなど行政の関心が高いためフルリスク評価に進むべきと判断。
triage.notes: デング熱・手足口病はベトナムにおける雨季の季節性流行であるが、2026年は症例数・死亡者数が多く(デング熱42,500例・11死亡、手足口病44,000例・5死亡、ラムドン省でも死亡例あり)、EV71株循環による重症化リスクが指摘されている。市・省当局が集中対策を講じている点から社会的関心・行政対応は高いと判断した。国際的拡大や渡航制限の兆候は現時点でなし。

article.articleHeadline: Mittlerweile mehr als 5000 Ebola-Tote im Kongo

Experts warn that actual numbers are likely higher than reported. The article provides no details on symptoms, transmission, or laboratory confirmation beyond the totals. The figures reflect confirmed infections and deaths and highlight a persistent, severe public health crisis in the DRC as of 2026-10-31.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola si v Kongu vyžiadala viac ako 5000 životov. Vírus sa ďalej šíri
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has claimed more than 5,000 lives in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The virus continues to spread.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has claimed over 5,000 lives and infected more than 10,000 people since mid-May. As of Oct 30, 2026, eight of the DRC's 26 provinces are affected, with many patients dying outside health facilities. The surge is driven by the rare Bundibugyo Ebola virus, for which there is no approved treatment or vaccine. Delayed detection, ongoing armed conflict, and an overburdened health system hinder containment. This is the second-largest Ebola outbreak by case count globally this year, surpassed only by West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone), which infected over 28,600 and killed more than 11,000. Cases have been reported beyond DRC: Nigeria became the continent’s fourth country to record an Ebola case last week, with confirmations in Kenya and Uganda.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Deaths in the Congo Have Already Exceeded 5,000
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by Bundibugyo virus, has surpassed 5,000 deaths (5,026) and 10,351 infections, with 1,101 in treatment or isolation and 2,788 recovered. Health authorities say the toll may be higher, with transmission believed to have run undetected since February before the May 15 outbreak announcement. The Bundibugyo strain presents fever with diarrhea and bleeding and spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids. No vaccine or targeted treatment exists for Bundibugyo, complicating containment; early stages can resemble malaria, delaying isolation. Trials for antivirals and several vaccines are underway since July, including testing Ervebo against Bundibugyo; Ervebo is approved only for Ebola virus disease caused by the Zaire strain. Imported/exported cases include Kenya (case traced to a Kenyan man who died), Nigeria (first case on Oct 20), a Swiss diplomat’s wife after Uganda travel, and a June case in France.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-Zahlen steigen weiterhin drastisch: Tausende Tote und mehr als 10.000 bestätigte Fälle
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola numbers continue to rise sharply: thousands of deaths and more than 10,000 confirmed cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to rise, with more than 10,000 confirmed infections and about 4,928 deaths (2,708 recovered) as of October 26, across eight provinces, notably Ituri with over 7,200 cases and North Kivu with more than 2,300, spanning 66 health zones. Transmission remains intense, worsened by a high number of deaths occurring outside medical facilities. The Bundibugyo virus drives this outbreak; symptoms include fever, weakness, gastrointestinal distress, and bleeding in severe cases. No vaccine is specifically approved for Bundibugyo; Ervebo is approved for Zaire ebolavirus, but its efficacy against Bundibugyo is unproven. A Phase 2/3 trial began October 23 in Bunia (Ituri), testing several vaccines including Ervebo. Animal data suggest possible protection, but human evidence is lacking. Exported/imported cases include Uganda, France, Kenya (9 infections, 2 deaths), and Nigeria (imported case on October 20; 54 contacts monitored). EU/EEA risk remains very low for the general population.

article.articleHeadline: Rio de Janeiro registra 74 casos de Mpox em dois meses - Sim Notícias
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rio de Janeiro records 74 Mpox cases in two months - Sim Notícias.
article.articleSummary: Rio de Janeiro reports 74 mpox cases in two months (September–October 2026), seven times higher than the same period in 2025, with 45 confirmed in September and 29 in October. Mpox is caused by an Orthopoxvirus and transmits mainly through direct contact with skin lesions, body fluids, and respiratory secretions during close, prolonged contact; sexual contact can also facilitate spread. Symptoms include fever, malaise, body aches, lymphadenopathy, and skin lesions evolving to crusts. Nationwide, mpox cases reach 13 states per the Ministério da Saúde. Early diagnosis enables isolation and reduces transmission. Vaccination prioritizes pre-exposure for higher-risk groups: cisgender men, travestis, and transgender women aged 18+ living with HIV; laboratory workers aged 18–49 handling the virus. Post-exposure vaccination should occur within 4 days of contact, or up to 14 days if asymptomatic. Source: CNN Brasil (Fernanda Palhares).

triage.headline_ja: リオデジャネイロ、2か月間でMpox症例74件を記録 - Sim Notícias

article.articleHeadline: Saudi Arabia bans travel, visas for Kenya over Ebola fears
article.articleSummary: Kenya reports nine Bundibugyo Ebola virus infections and two deaths, in a single outbreak cluster traced to a Kenyan man who travelled from the DRC through Uganda to Nairobi. Eight other cases include four family members and four healthcare workers; 135 contacts traced, with the first 20 completing 21-day monitoring and cleared on October 26; 98 remain to be released in phases from November 3 after assessments. Among seven hospitalized patients, two in isolation tested negative initially and await repeat testing after 72 hours; five remain stable, with no evidence of community transmission. Saudi Arabia bans travel to Kenya, halts visas for travellers from Kenya, and imposes 21-day entry bans for those who have stayed in Kenya or other Ebola-affected countries; similar restrictions have targeted DRC, Uganda and South Sudan. Weqaya says the kingdom’s health status is stable and monitoring. Published Oct 31, 2026.

Delayed detection, ongoing conflict, and overwhelmed health services have accelerated transmission, affecting eight of the country’s 26 provinces, with many fatalities occurring outside treatment centers. article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : deux jeunes médecins emportés en moins de 48 heures
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: Two Young Doctors Carried Away in Less Than 48 Hours.
article.articleSummary: Two Congolese doctors died within 48 hours from Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo: Dr. Safari Samuel died October 29, 2026 in Lwemba, Ituri, likely contracted at his health facility; Dr. Marie-France Shogogo died October 28, 2026 at the Ebola Treatment Center in Beni, North Kivu. Samuel, who graduated two years ago and previously studied in Goma, left 15 others ill awaiting care at his hospital. Shogogo, a three-year graduate from the University of Goma, died at the Beni ETC. Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya mourned the losses and urged stronger protection for frontline health workers amid a response still hampered by equipment gaps. The outbreak has caused about 5,000 deaths and over 10,000 cases to date. The World Food Programme mobilized $214 million over six months for vital food aid, logistics, telecommunications support, UN humanitarian air service operations, and continued Ebola treatment center construction; recalling the August 10, 2026 death of Dr. Charles Mbusa Munyumu in Katwa.

article.articleHeadline: Еболата во Конго уби повеќе од 5.000 луѓе

article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) caused by the Bundibugyo strain has killed more than 5,000 people, according to government data. article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in DR Congo exceeds 5,000 -- Health Ministry
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have surpassed 5,000, with 10,351 confirmed cases and 5,026 deaths (case fatality rate 48.6%), according to the Ministry of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare. The outbreak began May 15 in the DRC and in Uganda; Uganda’s outbreak was declared over July 28, with the WHO confirming this on August 25. In Kenya, the first Ebola case was confirmed on October 6, involving a Kenyan national who had previously lived in the DRC; the patient arrived in Nairobi via Uganda on October 3 and died October 5, with eight cases detected in Kenya as of October 19. The Kenyan case was imported from the DRC via Uganda, illustrating cross-border transmission within an ongoing outbreak centered in the DRC.

article.articleHeadline: Cách vệ sinh răng miệng và chăm sóc da cho trẻ mắc tay chân miệng tại nhà
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How to maintain oral hygiene and skin care for children with hand, foot and mouth disease at home.
article.articleSummary: Hand, Foot, and Mouth Disease (HFMD) in Vietnam spreads mainly via fecal–oral contact, saliva, blisters, and stool from infected children, with year‑round circulation and higher cases in the southern provinces; peaks occur March–May and September–December. It primarily affects children under 5, especially under 3, and outbreaks are common in daycare and school settings. At home, isolate the child for 10–14 days and notify schools or local health authorities to disinfect surfaces and monitor contacts. Ensure a well‑ventilated, sunlit environment. Manage fever with paracetamol (10–15 mg/kg per dose, up to 4 times daily) and, if fever persists, ibuprofen as advised; provide oral rehydration solution as needed. For care, use saline or saltwater mouth rinses, gentle cleaning, daily bathing with antiseptic soap, and trim nails to prevent scratching. Feed with soft foods; continue breastfeeding if applicable. Monitor for warning signs and seek prompt medical care if symptoms worsen.

article.articleHeadline: Epidemie außer Kontrolle: Mehr als 5000 Ebola-Tote im Kongo - und kein Ende in Sicht
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Epidemic Out of Control: More Than 5,000 Ebola Deaths in the Congo — and No End in Sight.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo reports 5,026 Ebola deaths and 10,351 cases from a Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak; 1,101 patients remain in treatment or isolation, with 2,788 recovered. Official outbreak notification occurred on May 15, with experts warning totals may be higher due to undetected transmission since February. The Bundibugyo strain is advancing swiftly; cases have appeared in Kenya linked to a deceased Kenyan in Congo. Nigeria reports its first Ebola case (October 20); a Swiss diplomat’s wife fell ill after a trip to Uganda; a June case in France involved a doctor deployed to eastern Congo. There is no vaccine or targeted therapy for Bundibugyo; antiviral and vaccine trials have been ongoing since July, including assessment of cross-protection by Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus vaccine). Separately, a US Science Advances study shows skin as a potential transmission route, with Ebola infecting dermal macrophages, endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and keratinocytes, reaching the epidermis within three days.

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola death toll surpasses 5,000 as outbreak spreads
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus has killed more than 5,000 people and infected over 10,000. It has spread to eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces, making it the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country and the second-largest globally after 2014–2016 West Africa. Response is hampered by insecurity, delayed detection, and overstretched health services, with many deaths occurring in communities rather than treatment centers, underscoring gaps in early case finding and timely care. A September Africa CDC review reported some progress, including declines in Ituri, but warned transmission is not consistently under control, with rising cases in parts of North Kivu and ongoing gaps in contact tracing. There are no approved vaccines or specific treatments for Bundibugyo virus; research continues. The outbreak has reached Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria, and WHO notes a case in France, indicating international transmission risk.
