article.articleHeadline: Ebola has topped 10,000 cases. Africa's top health official says the world should pay attention
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-31, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (Bundibugyo strain) has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases and 5,000 deaths. Declared mid-May, it is the largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in DRC and second only to West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic. Ongoing conflict, public distrust, and the lack of an approved treatment or vaccine for Bundibugyo hinder containment, with scientists noting months of undetected spread in remote areas. The outbreak has extended to neighboring countries, including Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria; Nigeria reported its first infection in a decade, and a Nigerian-born Swiss diplomat’s wife was evacuated to Switzerland for treatment. Canada has committed about $8 million to the response, including $2 million to Africa CDC, and authorized Moderna’s Bundibugyo-targeted vaccine trial in July, alongside October outbreak alerts for Kenya and Nigeria. Genomic sequencing by Canadian–Congolese teams exceeds 1,000 genomes to aid surveillance and assess potential cross-protection.

article.articleHeadline: Làm báo trong đỉnh dịch COVID-19
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Covering the COVID-19 outbreak at its peak.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 emerged in late 2019 and became a global pandemic by March 2020. In Vietnam, the first SARS-CoV-2 infection was recorded in Ho Chi Minh City in late January 2020, with waves prompting strict social distancing, centralized quarantine, and lockdowns across many provinces; Hanoi and other cities also reported deaths. Amid this, the Cand newspaper persisted in information, outreach, and production, with editors, reporters, and drivers required to undergo two weeks of centralized quarantine as F1/F2. Health reporter Tran Hang tracked frontline hotspots, operating mainly from National Institute of Tropical Diseases, Bach Mai Hospital, and Hanoi Obstetrics Hospital. Bach Mai’s first confirmed case was a nurse from the Tropical Diseases Center; she tested negative twice, while authorities mandated health declarations for anyone who visited Bach Mai from 12 March 2020. Editorial teams maintained shifted work, and strict 5K measures to prevent publication disruption.

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as worry of continent-wide spread mounts

The ongoing outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus and was declared in mid-May in Bunia, eastern Congo; authorities have since struggled to contain it, with cases recorded in other African countries. The surge marks Congo's outbreak as the second-deadliest Ebola event in history, exceeded only by the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that killed about 11,000 across multiple countries. The rising toll has sparked mounting concerns about continent-wide spread and authorities’ containment capabilities. The article does not specify laboratory confirmation or infection sources.

article.articleHeadline: Por el rebrote de ébola en África, Estados Unidos impuso un nuevo requisito obligatorio para poder ingresar por vía aérea
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Due to the Ebola resurgence in Africa, the United States imposed a new mandatory requirement for entry by air.
article.articleSummary: Due to a resurgence of Ebola in Central Africa, the United States imposes a new mandatory air-entry rule issued by the CDC. Beginning November 3 at 23:59, all international flights to North America must present a signed declaration certifying that the traveler was not in the Democratic Republic of the Congo during the previous 21 days. Anyone physically present in the DRC, including layovers without deplaning, must wait 21 days outside DRC before boarding a U.S.-bound flight. The measure applies to US citizens, permanent residents, foreigners, and flight crews on direct or connecting itineraries. Exemptions include overflights, aircraft transporting patients with government authorization, and humanitarian or emergency medical evacuations. Additional conditions apply for those who stayed in Uganda or South Sudan in the prior 21 days. Airlines must collect and retain declarations for at least 42 days. The order runs through December 18, unless modified.

article.articleHeadline: Surto de ébola na RDCongo já provocou mais de 5.000 mortos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has already killed more than 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has caused more than 5,000 deaths, with 10,351 confirmed infections and 5,026 fatalities (case fatality 48.6%) as of Oct 29, per the National Institute of Public Health. Recovered: 2,788; hospitalized or in isolation: 1,101. Ituri province (epicenter) accounts for 36.4% of new cases, North Kivu 58.4%; the epidemic spans 67 health zones in eight of the 26 provinces, including Ituri, North Kivu, Tshopo, Bas-Uele, Haut-Uele, South Kivu, Ubangi-Sud, and Ubangi-Nord. The Bundibugyo strain has no specific treatment; WHO is coordinating vaccine development. Since late August, Congo started large-scale vaccination with Ervebo. The outbreak has reached Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths; end Aug), Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths), and Nigeria (1 case); France reported an associated case, with evacuees to the Netherlands and Germany. Urgent coordinated action is urged; transmission via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and bleeding.

article.articleHeadline: Saudi Announces Kenya Travel And Entry Restrictions Over Ebola Concerns
article.articleSummary: On 30 October 2026, Saudi Arabia announced travel and entry restrictions to mitigate Ebola concerns related to Kenya. Saudi citizens' travel to Kenya is suspended, and Saudi Arabia has suspended issuing all visa types for travelers from Kenya and barred their entry. The measures apply to arrivals from Kenya and to travelers who recently stayed in Kenya or other Ebola-affected countries within the past 21 days, even if transiting other nations; the 21-day rule focuses on recent stay, not duration of restrictions. Weqaya, Saudi Arabia's Public Health Authority, says the internal situation remains reassuring and ongoing monitoring is maintained. The actions build on June measures restricting Saudi citizens' travel to, and arrivals from, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda and South Sudan. No end date is provided for the new Kenya restrictions.

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola Death Toll Tops 5,000 as Fears of Africa-Wide Spread Grow
article.articleSummary: Ebola in Congo has killed 5,026 of 10,351 reported infections, according to Congo's Ministry of Health, giving a case-fatality rate of nearly 50%. As of 2026-10-31, government data released on Saturday show a sharp rise in fatalities, fueling concern among health experts about whether authorities can contain the highly lethal virus. The data reflect a rapid rise in deaths, underscoring the heavy toll on families and stretched health systems as transmission remains persistent with an expanding geographic footprint and heightened risk to neighboring nations as cross-border cases are monitored.

article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused more than 5,000 deaths among 10,351 confirmed infections as of Oct 29, with a 48.6% case fatality rate. article.articleHeadline: El ébola causa ya 5.000 muertos y 10.000 casos mientras el mundo mira para otro lado
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has already caused 5,000 deaths and 10,000 cases as the world looks the other way.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases and 5,000 deaths across the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria (Nigeria declared Ebola-free after evacuating the sole patient to Switzerland) as of 2026-10-31. The Kenyan index case traveled over 2,000 kilometers from Buta, DRC, through RDC territories to Uganda and ultimately Nairobi, where he died on Oct 5; initial misdiagnosis as Rift Valley fever delayed recognition. The WHO reconstructs a cross-border route: Buta, Aketi, Likati, Bondo, Kisangani, Beni, Kasindi, Kampala, Entebbe, then Nairobi. In Kenya, 9 cases and 2 deaths by late October, all linked to the index patient via a 135-person contact list quarantined and monitored. The outbreak—driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, the second-worst and fastest-growing—exposed diagnostic gaps for non-Zaire filoviruses and was amplified by mistrust, armed conflict, and weak health systems; Uganda’s response is highlighted as a success example.

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 5 000
article.articleSummary: Death toll from the Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has risen above 5,000, making it the DRC's deadliest Ebola epidemic on record. article.articleHeadline: Point Santé : Ebola gagne l'Afrique de l'Ouest, la riposte sanitaire s'organise sur le continent
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health Update: Ebola Gains Ground in West Africa, the Health Response Is Being Organized Across the Continent.
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak surges past 10,000 laboratory-confirmed cases with about 5,000 deaths, making the Bundibugyo strain the deadliest yet in the country since declaring the outbreak on May 15, 2026. There is no vaccine or approved treatment; containment hinges on early detection, isolation, and rigorous contact tracing. Nigeria reports its first Ebola case in over a decade in a woman who had stayed in Uganda; as of Oct 29, 62 contacts are under surveillance and the patient was evacuated to Switzerland on Oct 26. Uganda has deployed 34 field staff across 31 high‑risk districts, focusing on border areas like Ntoroko to strengthen detection and response while inquiries trace the patient’s transit. Africa CDC provides about $1.5 million to Kenya to bolster surveillance, case management, and emergency operations; 20 contacts of the initial imported case completed a 21‑day quarantine by Oct 26. Togo has enhanced entry-point surveillance; polio campaigns unfold in Malawi and South Sudan, with prevention activities in Ethiopia and Burkina Faso. Africa CDC notes a $4.3 billion annual funding gap for community health workers.

triage.headline_ja: 健康速報：エボラが西アフリカへ拡大、アフリカ大陸全体で保健対応が組織化
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）流行が10,000例・死者約5,000人に達し同国史上最悪となっており、ナイジェリアへの輸入例やスイスへの患者搬送など国際的拡大が確認されているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域に多数の国が含まれるが、対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ。ナイジェリア、ウガンダ、ケニア、スイス、トーゴ、エチオピア、ブルキナファソ、マラウイは対象国リスト外のためverified_locationsから除外。ワクチン・承認治療法が存在しない点は流行しやすさ・管理可能性の観点で重要な懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola Deaths Top 5,000 as Worry of Continent-Wide Spread Mounts
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo has killed 5,026 people and infected 10,351, as of Oct 31, 2026, according to the Congolese Ministry of Health. The fatalities, concentrated in Bunia and surrounding areas, reflect a nearly 50% lethality rate. The outbreak continues to spread, with cases recorded in other African countries, raising concerns about continent-wide transmission. The latest government data published on Oct 31, 2026 underscore the challenge of containment amid sustained transmission. Experts warn about authorities’ capacity to contain the deadly virus as the epidemic extends beyond regional borders. The report signals an ongoing crisis in Congo with potential spillover, emphasizing the need for heightened surveillance and public health responses to curb further fatalities.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超え、大陸規模の拡大への懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%の大規模エボラ流行がコンゴで継続し、他のアフリカ諸国への感染拡大が報告されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する深刻な公衆衛生事例である。
triage.notes: 記事では他のアフリカ諸国への感染拡大が言及されているが、具体的な対象国リスト内の国名は明記されていないため、DRCのみをverified_locationsに計上した。

article.articleHeadline: Plus de 5.000 décès liés à Ebola recensés en République démocratique du Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 Ebola-related deaths recorded in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused 5,026 deaths and 10,351 infections since May. Currently, 1,101 people are under treatment or in quarantine, and 2,788 have recovered. Experts warn the toll could be higher, estimating Ebola may have circulated undetected since February, months before the outbreak was officially declared on 15 May. The update underscores a heavy mortality burden and a period of undetected transmission prior to the declaration, with transmission continuing within the DRC and the need for sustained surveillance and response to curb spread.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ関連死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 大規模なエボラアウトブレイク（死者5,026人、感染者10,351人）が継続中であり、深刻な公衆衛生影響と国際的拡大リスクを有するため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 2月から5月の公式宣言まで未検出の伝播があった可能性が指摘されており、サーベイランス体制の不備が示唆される。継続的な監視と対応強化が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 七歲女童感染甲型流感現危殆｜METROHK.com.hk
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Seven-year-old girl infected with Influenza A is currently in critical condition | METROHK.com.hk
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-31, Hong Kong reports a severe Influenza A (H1) infection in a seven-year-old girl with underlying illness, currently in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit at Tuen Mun Hospital. She developed runny nose, diarrhea and abdominal pain on Oct 29, then fever and seizures; respiratory testing confirmed Influenza A (H1) with septic shock. She had no recent travel and was unvaccinated for the 2026/27 season. Household contacts were asymptomatic; three classmates had mild flu symptoms. The Centre for Health Protection urges vaccination and school infection-control measures as investigations continue. Since the season began in late June, overall influenza activity remains above baseline, with 28 severe pediatric cases this season: 20 discharged, 2 stable, 4 critical, 2 deaths. Vaccination is recommended for everyone aged six months and older; the 2026/27 vaccine program started Sept 17, with school outreach in about 1,600 schools and completion expected by mid-December.

triage.headline_ja: 7歳の女児が甲型インフルエンザに感染し重篤な状態|METROHK.com.hk
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザA(H1)による小児重症例の個別報告であり、香港衛生署も通常の季節性活動の範囲内として対応している。渡航歴なし、濃厚接触者も軽症または無症状であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 本季は28件の小児重症インフルエンザ症例（退院20、安定2、重篤4、死亡2）が報告されているが、季節性インフルエンザの既知のパターン内であり、CHPはワクチン接種と学校での感染対策強化を呼びかける通常の公衆衛生対応を行っている。

article.articleHeadline: وفيات إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية تتجاوز 5 آلاف حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,000 deaths and more than 10,000 infections, according to health ministry data released on 2026-10-31. The current wave is driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which no licensed vaccine or targeted therapy exists. The case fatality rate is about 50%. Authorities cite challenges including late detection, armed conflict, and overburdened health services. The outbreak has spilled across borders, with confirmed infections in Kenya and Nigeria, raising concern about regional spread in Africa. This outbreak ranks as the second-largest Ebola surge on record, behind West Africa (2014–2016) when over 11,000 deaths occurred. The report underscores ongoing transmission and the need for vigilance, cross-border surveillance, and public health response despite limited medical countermeasures for this strain.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱による死者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 死者5000人超・感染1万人超の大規模アウトブレイクで国境を越えケニア・ナイジェリアへの感染拡大が確認されており、IHR基準の複数該当とWHO通知相当の深刻な公衆衛生事象である。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリアへの感染拡大が報告されているが、両国は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ワクチン・治療法未確立のBundibugyo株によるもので、致死率約50%、史上2番目の規模のアウトブレイクとされる。

article.articleHeadline: Број жртава епидемије еболе у ДР Конгу премашио 5.000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus has killed more than 5,000 people and infected over 10,000 since the outbreak was declared in May, as of Oct 31, 2026. Eight of 26 provinces are affected, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centers due to late case detection, armed conflict, and an overwhelmed health system. There is currently no approved treatment or vaccine for Bundibugyo ebolavirus. Nigeria reported a case last week, signaling spread to West Africa, while cases have also been detected in Kenya and Uganda. The 2026 outbreak is the second-largest globally, following the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that hit Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone with about 28,600 cases and over 11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴのエボラ流行による死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 死者5,000人超・感染者10,000人超の大規模流行で、ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダへの国際的拡大も確認されており、IHR基準の複数該当とWPRO基準も複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダへの拡大も記載されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ギニア・リベリア・シエラレオネは2014-2016年流行への言及で、今回の2026年流行とは別事象のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: 7歲長期病患女童染甲流併發敗血性休克 情況危殆 - 香港商報
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 7-year-old chronically ill girl with influenza A (H1N1) infection complicated by septic shock; condition critical.
article.articleSummary: In Hong Kong, the Centre for Health Protection reported a severe pediatric influenza case on 31 October 2026: a 7-year-old girl with chronic illness infected with influenza A(H1N1) and septic shock, currently in critical condition. She developed symptoms on 29 October (runny nose, diarrhea, abdominal pain) and, on 30 October, fever and seizures, prompting admission to Tuen Mun Hospital and transfer to the pediatric ICU. Lab tests confirmed influenza A(H1N1). Investigations show no travel and she had not received the 2026/27 seasonal flu vaccine. Household contacts were asymptomatic; three classmates had mild flu symptoms but did not require hospitalization. The Center urged schools to implement infection control. Hong Kong's flu season began in June and remains above baseline activity. This season has 28 pediatric severe influenza cases: 20 recovered, 2 stable, 4 critical, 2 deaths; vaccination urged, especially for high-risk groups.

triage.headline_ja: 7歳の基礎疾患のある女児がインフルエンザA（H1N1）に感染し敗血性ショックを併発、容体危篤 - 香港商報
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザによる重症小児例だが、既知の季節性流行パターン内の事象であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限の懸念は低い。小児重症・死亡例が継続している点は注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Saiba como acontece a transmissão e as melhores formas de se prevenir da Mpox
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Learn how Mpox is transmitted and the best ways to protect yourself from Mpox.
article.articleSummary: Mpox infection in Rio de Janeiro state has reached 211 confirmed cases, surpassing 119 reported in 2025, with 117 cases under investigation. A new mpox subtype is reportedly circulating in Rio. Transmission occurs via direct contact with skin lesions, bodily fluids (including saliva and genital secretions), contaminated objects, and prolonged close respiratory exposure; infectiousness begins 1–4 days before lesions and continues until all lesions heal and a new skin forms. Prevention emphasizes avoiding contact with lesions or mucous membranes of suspected/confirmed cases, avoiding intimate contact during symptoms, not sharing personal items, and isolating until complete healing. Hygiene measures include frequent handwashing, environmental cleaning with bleach, keeping wounds covered, and using a separate bathroom when possible for 21 days or until scabs fall. Vaccination with MVA-BN is available but doses are in shortage; SUS serves specific groups, requiring two subcutaneous doses 28 days apart. Not yet classified as outbreak or epidemic; heightened vigilance for people living with HIV.

triage.headline_ja: Mpoxの感染経路と予防法について知る
triage.triage_reason: リオデジャネイロ州でMpox症例が前年を上回る211例に増加し新亜種の流通が報告されており、ワクチン不足やHIV感染者への警戒も示されているためフルリスク評価が妥当。
triage.notes: 新亜種の詳細（クレードI/IIの別等）や重症度・死亡例の有無は記事内で言及されておらず不明。公式にはまだアウトブレイクや流行とは分類されていない点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: [Video] TP Hồ Chí Minh ghi nhận hơn 42.500 ca sốt xuất huyết, 11 người tử vong
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: [Video] Ho Chi Minh City records more than 42,500 dengue fever cases, 11 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam: as of week 43 (late October 2026), the city has recorded over 42,500 dengue cases and 11 deaths. In the past week there were nearly 1,800 suspected cases, up about 10% from the prior month's average. In response to the ongoing rainy-season dengue dynamics, on October 31 the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Health launched a high-intensity citywide anti-dengue campaign. The agency requires local authorities to initiate large-scale environmental sanitation, eliminate mosquito breeding sites, and strictly sanction violations of dengue prevention regulations. Health stations across the system must monitor and address 100% of dengue risk points in October and November 2026 to curb transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 【動画】ホーチミン市、デング熱患者4万2500人超、死者11人を記録
triage.triage_reason: ホーチミン市で季節性のデング熱が大規模に流行し、死者も発生しており、当局が全市的な緊急対策を実施していることから社会的・行政的関心が高く、スクリーニング基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: デング熱はベトナムで季節性に流行する風土病であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、症例数・死者数の規模と当局の緊急対応から国内公衆衛生上の重要イベントとして注視すべき。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : États-Unis exigent une déclaration sanitaire obligatoire pour les voyageurs aériens
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: The United States requires a mandatory health declaration for air travelers.
article.articleSummary: United States imposes a declaration for travelers destined to the United States to curb Ebola. Beginning 3 November 2026 at 23:59 EST (4 November 5:59 Paris time) through 18 December 2026 at 23:59 EST, this measure is subject to extension. The CDC requires each traveler to attest they have not been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) in the previous 21 days—the Ebola incubation period. It is a travel declaration, not a medical certificate. Presence in the DRC includes layovers and transfers in Congolese airports. A form is required for each traveler; minors must be signed by a parent/guardian, and signers may assist disabled travelers. The form, available in English (airlines may provide translations), applies to all passengers to the U.S., including transit. Without signed attestation, boarding is denied; carriers must keep copies for 42 days and provide on request. Exemptions possible for certain medical or humanitarian cases.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：米国、航空旅客に健康申告書の提出を義務化
triage.triage_reason: 米国がコンゴ民主共和国からの渡航者に対し健康申告を義務化する渡航制限措置を導入しており、IHR基準（渡航制限・国際拡大リスク）に複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCにおけるエボラ流行を受けた米国の渡航制限措置についてであり、実際の発生国はDRC。パリ・米国・フランスは政策実施の文脈で言及されているのみで発生地ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Бројот на смртни случаи од ебола во Конго надминува 5.000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of Ebola deaths in Congo exceeds 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Since mid-May in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ebola deaths exceed 5,000, with 5,026 confirmed fatalities among 10,351 cases. Currently, 1,101 people are being treated or in quarantine, and 2,788 previously infected have recovered. Experts warn the true toll may be higher, as transmission could have begun undetected from February, months before the outbreak was officially declared on May 15. The epidemic, caused by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus, is spreading rapidly within Congo; cases have appeared in Kenya, linked to a Kenyan national who contracted the virus in Congo and later died. On October 20, Nigeria reported its first case: a Swiss citizen who fell ill after a several-week trip to Uganda. One European case has been documented: a doctor in France after a humanitarian mission to eastern Congo, who recovered. Transmission is via direct contact with infected individuals or their bodily fluids; symptoms include high fever, diarrhea, and bleeding.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国での大規模エボラ流行（死者5,000人超）に加え、ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランスへの国際的な感染拡大が確認されており、IHR基準の複数該当とWPRO基準の該当が認められる。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランスでの症例は輸入例であり、発生国は主にコンゴ民主共和国。これら3国は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola devastuje Kongo. Počet zemřelých překročil další vysokou hranici
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola devastates the Congo. The death toll has crossed another high threshold.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-31, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed more than 5,000 people and infected over 10,000 since mid-May. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo strain (Orthoebolavirus zairense), with no approved drugs or vaccines. The virus has spread to eight of 26 provinces, and many deaths occur outside health facilities. Contributing factors include late detection, ongoing armed conflict, and an overburdened health system, accelerating transmission. This year’s epidemic is the second-largest in history, surpassed only by the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, which infected over 28,600 and caused more than 11,000 deaths (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone). Nigeria reported a case last week, signaling spread to West Africa, with additional cases in Kenya and Uganda. Ebola symptoms include fever, body pains, vomiting, and diarrhea; untreated case fatality can reach up to 90%. The virus was first identified in 1976 in Congo.

triage.headline_ja: エボラがコンゴを襲う。死者数がさらに高い閾値を超えた
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行が5000人超の死者・10000人超の感染者を出し、ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダへの拡大も報告されており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性、異常性、国際拡大）に該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでの大規模エボラ流行を主題としている。ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダへの拡大が言及されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。シエラレオネ・リベリアは過去の2014-2016流行の比較対象であり、現在の発生地域ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent-wide spread mounts
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed 5,026 people and infected 10,351, with 2,788 recoveries, a near 50% case‑fatality rate. The eastern provinces of Ituri and North Kivu are the epicenters, reporting 9,782 confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths. Since mid‑May, the outbreak has spread to 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, with 50 zones currently reporting active cases. The Bundibugyo virus has no vaccine or approved treatment; care is supportive. About 80% of new cases arise from outside monitored contact chains, and roughly one‑third of deaths occur outside treatment centers before testing. Kenya has eight cases and two deaths; Nigeria has one exported case evacuated to Switzerland, signaling continent‑wide spread after earlier Ugandan cases. Insecurity and health‑worker strikes in Ituri and North Kivu hinder tracing, testing, and response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超え、大陸全体への拡大懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）流行が5,000人超の死者・1万人超の感染者を出し、ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへの越境拡大も確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当しフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイス・ウガンダへの越境症例が報告されているが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。治安悪化や医療従事者のストライキが対応を阻害している点も注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Zbog salmonele povučeno pileće meso iz Brazila sa tržišta na Kosovu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chicken meat from Brazil recalled from the market in Kosovo due to salmonella.
article.articleSummary: On 31 October 2026, Kosovo's Food and Veterinary Agency ordered a temporary ban on sale and recall of two brands of frozen chicken meat imported from Brazil after laboratory tests found Salmonella Minnesota (Salmonella enterica serotype Minnesota). The products, distributed by Apetit DOO, should not be consumed and must be returned to retailers. The action follows extraordinary import controls ordered by Kosovo's Minister of Agriculture Armenda Muje. All affected lots are under official supervision; consumers should verify packaging and avoid those serials. Salmonella Minnesota can cause gastrointestinal infections via contaminated food and cross-contamination during handling. Authorities are auditing the entire imported quantity—tracking from entry to shops, reviewing labeling, production/expiry dates, veterinary certificates, and storage conditions, with additional analyses. The importer bears responsibility for safety and recall; AUV will supervise and determine further measures, including destruction if needed, and will inform the public of results.

triage.headline_ja: サルモネラ菌混入によりブラジル産鶏肉がコソボの市場から回収
triage.triage_reason: 対象国（ブラジル）で疾病が発生しているのではなく、コソボにおける輸入食品の予防的リコール事案であり、対象国リストにも該当しないため見送り。

article.articleSummary: A 7-year-old girl in Hong Kong with chronic illness contracted Influenza A(H1) and developed septic shock, now in critical condition. She began with runny nose, diarrhea, and abdominal pain; fever and seizures led to emergency care at Tuen Mun Hospital, followed by admission to the pediatric intensive care unit. Respiratory testing confirmed Influenza A(H1). She had no recent travel and was not vaccinated for this season. Household contacts are asymptomatic; in her class, three other students recently showed mild flu symptoms but none required hospitalization. The Centre for Health Protection advised the school on infection-control measures and continues investigation. Since the influenza season began in late June, Hong Kong’s activity remains above baseline but appears to be easing. This season records 28 severe pediatric influenza cases (20 recovered/discharged, 2 stable, 4 critical, 2 deaths). CHP urges vaccination for high-risk groups to prevent severe outcomes.

triage.headline_ja: 慢性疾患を持つ7歳女児がA型インフルエンザに感染、敗血性ショックを併発し危篤状態
triage.triage_reason: 個別の重症小児例であり季節性インフルエンザの範囲内と考えられるが、重症化・死亡例が複数出ている点から経過観察が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Zu schnell und zu tödlich: Über 5000 Seuchen-Tote im Kongo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Too Fast and Too Deadly: Over 5,000 Outbreak Deaths in the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus Ebola outbreak in the Congo (DRC) has 10,351 infections and 5,026 deaths as of October 2026, the second deadliest Ebola outbreak. Declared mid-May; weekly 400–500 new cases; no plateau in sight. Only about 25% of new infections come from known contact chains; three-quarters occur via undetected transmission. Mistrust and reduced aid hinder response. No approved vaccine for Bundibugyo ebolavirus; Ervebo targets Zaire ebolavirus with uncertain cross-protection. About 30 confirmed cases have been exported to Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda; risk to other fragile regions like South Sudan. Early symptoms: fever, headache, sore throat, weakness; later vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, rash; severe disease includes kidney/liver failure, bleeding, shock, multiorgan failure. Transmission via body fluids; Europe can isolate and trace contacts, but Congo struggles.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：速すぎて致死率も高い：コンゴで5,000人超が死亡

triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）が主たる発生地。スーダン・ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリアは対象国リスト外のため除外（ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリアへの感染例輸出は言及されているが対象国リストに含まれず）。ワクチン未承認で未検出感染経路が75%を占めるなど、極めて深刻な状況。

article.articleHeadline: دولية وعالمية - أكثر من 5000 حالة وفاة جراء تفشي فيروس إيبولا بالكونجو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: International and Global - More than 5,000 deaths due to Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, health authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo report that the Ebola outbreak first detected in mid-May has resulted in 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed cases. Currently, 1,101 people remain in treatment or in isolation, while 2,788 have recovered. The data illustrate the scale and persistence of Ebola transmission within the country since the mid-May onset, with a sizable number of active cases alongside a substantial recovery total. This update provides the latest official counts shaping the ongoing public health understanding of the outbreak in the DRC. The figures confirm the continued impact of Ebola in the region.

triage.headline_ja: 国際・世界 - コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱流行により5000人以上が死亡

article.articleHeadline: Број жртава епидемије еболе у ДР Конгу премашио 5.000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The death toll from the Ebola epidemic in the DRC has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Death toll from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000 with over 10,000 infections since May. The epidemic is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there are no approved treatments or vaccines. Late case detection, ongoing armed conflict, and an overburdened health system have accelerated spread, with eight of 26 provinces affected and many deaths outside treatment centers. This year’s outbreak ranks as the second-largest globally, after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that sickened more than 28,600 and killed over 11,000 in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Nigeria recently became the fourth African country to report an Ebola case, signaling spillover to West Africa, with additional cases reported in East Africa (Kenya and Uganda).

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴのエボラ流行による死者数が5,000人を超えた
triage.triage_reason: DRコンゴでエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ型）による死者が5,000人、感染者が10,000人を超え、ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダへの越境拡大も報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はDRコンゴでの流行を主題としており、ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダ・シエラレオネ・アンゴラ・モザンビーク・リベリア・ギニアは文脈上言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRコンゴの武力紛争と医療体制の疲弊が流行拡大の要因として指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Έμπολα στο Κονγκό: 5.026 νεκροί και ανησυχία για την εξάπλωση
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Congo: 5,026 dead and concern about the spread.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed cases, yielding a case fatality rate of about 50%. The outbreak is ongoing and driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, which emerged in mid-May and has since spread to other African countries, sparking concern about wider regional transmission. As reported by the Democratic Republic of the Congo Ministry of Health on Saturday, 31 October 2026, the deadly virus continues to spread rapidly, challenging authorities to curb transmission. This outbreak ranks as the second-deadliest Ebola epidemic in history, surpassed only by the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, which killed about 11,000 people across multiple countries. Health officials continue response efforts to contain the spread and protect populations across the region.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱：死者5,026人、拡大への懸念
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ大規模流行（死者5,026人、致死率約50%）で、他のアフリカ諸国への拡大懸念もあり、IHR基準の深刻性・異常性・国際拡大リスクに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。

article.articleHeadline: Uzmanladan "benzeri görülmedi" uyarısı: Salgın Avrupa'ya dayandı
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Experts warn of an "unprecedented" outbreak: The epidemic has reached Europe.
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 31, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ituri region faces an unprecedented Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus. Total cases reach 10,091, with 4,887 deaths in the DRC; Uganda and Kenya report two deaths each. This is the first time three African regions are affected simultaneously, and officials warn the outbreak could reach Europe, including the United Kingdom. Africa CDC Director Dr. Jean Kaseya urged immediate preparedness and release of pledged funds. The outbreak was officially declared May 15 in Ituri, though genomic data indicate transmission began in February. Bundibugyo virus spreads via direct contact with bodily fluids and during funeral rites; no approved treatment exists, though vaccine trials are underway with results expected in 3–6 months. An imported case was identified in France in June in a doctor returning from DRC, and Nigeria confirmed a case in Abuja from a Ugandan traveler.

triage.headline_ja: 専門家が「前例のない」警告：流行がヨーロッパに到達

article.articleHeadline: 伊波拉疫情肆虐民主剛果 死亡人數突破5000人
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak ravages the Democratic Republic of the Congo; death toll surpasses 5,000.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-31, the Democratic Republic of the Congo is hit by a severe Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus. The DRC Ministry of Health reports 10,351 infections and 5,026 deaths, a case fatality rate near 50%. The outbreak began in mid-May and has intensified, with spread reported to other African countries. It is described as the second-worst Ebola epidemic on record, surpassed only by the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak that killed about 11,000 people. The situation remains unstable as authorities struggle to contain transmission across affected areas. Ongoing transmission underscores sustained regional public health challenges and the need for continued control measures.

article.articleHeadline: Chủ động phòng bệnh não mô cầu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Proactive prevention of meningococcal disease
article.articleSummary: Meningococcal disease is rising in Vietnam among children and adults, with rapid, potentially fatal progression without timely treatment. In the past month cases have been reported in Ho Chi Minh City and Ca Mau; by mid-October the southern region logged 42 infections and 7 deaths. Early signs resemble flu—fever, headache, fatigue, and nausea—before rapid deterioration with cold extremities, skin mottling, weak pulse, and severe leg pain, risking shock, coma, and multi-organ failure. Neisseria meningitidis can colonize healthy throats and spread via respiratory droplets, even from asymptomatic carriers. Vaccination is emphasized by WHO. Vietnam offers vaccines for serogroups A, B, C, Y and W-135; serogroup B vaccine is for infants from 2 months, conjugate vaccines for A, C, Y, W-135 from 2 or 9 months, and BC vaccine for broader use. Preventive measures include hand hygiene, masking in crowds, environmental cleanliness, and prophylaxis for close contacts.

triage.headline_ja: 髄膜炎菌感染症の予防に積極的に取り組む

article.articleHeadline: TP. Hồ Chí Minh ghi nhận hơn 42.500 ca sốt xuất huyết, 11 ca tử vong
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ho Chi Minh City records more than 42,500 dengue fever cases, 11 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever and hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) are being tracked in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam. By week 43, the city has recorded over 42,500 dengue cases with 11 deaths and more than 44,000 HFMD cases with 5 deaths. In week 43, nearly 1,800 suspected dengue cases were reported, up about 10% from the four-week average. HFMD outbreaks are rising, with EV71 circulating and posing a risk of severe complications in children. Health authorities will intensify surveillance, early detection, and outbreak containment, while strengthening treatment capacity to reduce severe cases and fatalities. Local governments are urged to mobilize for environmental cleanup, identify and eliminate hotspots, and ensure schools and childcare centers monitor health and disinfect facilities. Public guidance stresses removing standing water, larval control, handwashing, and seeking care for symptoms. Five loudspeaker vehicles were deployed along main streets in phường Dĩ An to support hotspot surveys.

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent-wide spread mounts
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo virus, has killed 5,026 of 10,351 infections (≈50% case fatality) with 2,788 recoveries. Since May, 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces have reported cases, concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu, which together account for 9,782 confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths. The outbreak is the continent's second-deadliest, behind West Africa's 2014–2016 epidemic (≈11,000 deaths). About 80% of new cases arise from outside known transmission chains, and roughly one-third of deaths occur outside treatment centers before testing. There is no vaccine or treatment; care is symptomatic. In October, Kenya (8 cases, 2 deaths) and Nigeria (1 case evacuated to Switzerland) confirmed cases, signaling continent-wide spread. Health workers have staged strikes for unpaid wages, hindering response efforts.

article.articleHeadline: Afrique: Ebola - Après la RDC, Madagascar étend les mesures de quarantaine aux voyageurs du Kenya et du Nigeria
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Africa: Ebola - After the DRC, Madagascar extends quarantine measures to travelers from Kenya and Nigeria.
article.articleSummary: Madagascar tightens Ebola surveillance and extends border controls to travelers from Kenya and Nigeria, despite no suspected or confirmed cases in the country. Following ministerial note #569, the health ministry reinforced border health measures at Ivato International Airport, including enhanced traveler identification, medical checks, and mandatory quarantine in dedicated facilities with rigorous medical follow-up. The measures previously applied to travelers from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are now extended to Kenya and Nigeria to prevent introduction of the virus. All currently quarantined individuals are monitored and healthy; no infections detected among them. Authorities remind that Ebola-like symptoms such as diarrhea, fever, or vomiting are not diagnostic, and appropriate tests confirm infection. A public hotline, 115, provides information. The DRC remains the Ebola epicenter with thousands of cases; Kenya reports imported cases and related contagions, while Nigeria has its first imported case, prompting heightened surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ：エボラ出血熱 ― DRCに続き、マダガスカルがケニア・ナイジェリアからの渡航者にも検疫措置を拡大

article.articleHeadline: 7-year-old girl in critical condition at Tuen Mun Hospital after severe influenza A infection
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, a seven-year-old girl with an underlying illness in Hong Kong is in critical condition after influenza A (H1) infection. On 29 Oct she developed runny nose, diarrhoea and abdominal pain; by 30 Oct she had fever and a convulsion and was admitted to Tuen Mun Hospital, then transferred to the paediatric intensive care unit. Laboratory tests confirmed influenza A (H1) with septic shock. She had no travel history during incubation and had not received the 2026/27 seasonal influenza vaccine; household contacts are asymptomatic, and three classmates have mild flu-like symptoms. Since the season’s start, Hong Kong has recorded 28 severe paediatric influenza cases: 20 discharged, 2 in stable condition, 4 in critical condition, and 2 fatalities. Public health officials urge vaccination for high-risk groups and emphasize hygiene. The 2026/27 programme began 17 Sept with School Outreach and a new eHealth consent system; about 1,600 schools are participating, with outreach ending mid-December.

triage.headline_ja: 屯門病院でA型インフルエンザ重症感染により7歳女児が重体

The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain is identified as the origin of this epidemic. Eight of the 26 provinces have been affected, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centers. No approved treatment or vaccine exists for Bundibugyo ebolavirus, according to Reuters. The report underscores the scale and persistence of transmission across multiple regions, highlighting ongoing public health challenges in Central Africa.

article.articleHeadline: CHP records case of severe paediatric influenza infection
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong's CHP records a severe paediatric influenza case: a seven-year-old girl with an underlying illness developed influenza A (H1) and septic shock, now in critical condition after fever and convulsions on October 30, following initial symptoms on October 29. She had no travel history and had not received the 2026/27 Seasonal Influenza Vaccine (SIV). Three classmates have mild flu-like symptoms. CHP urged vaccination for high-risk groups and advised schools to strengthen infection-control measures. Since June, Hong Kong’s influenza season has persisted for four months, with 28 severe paediatric influenza cases this season (20 recovered, 2 stable, 4 critical, 2 deaths). Vaccine protection wanes after about nine months; WHO recommends annual SIV for those six months and older. The 2026/27 SIV program began Sept 17, with e-consent via eHealth; about 1,600 schools; outreach expected to finish mid-December. Public urged to vaccinate and maintain hygiene.

triage.headline_ja: 衛生防護センター、重症小児インフルエンザ感染症例を記録
triage.triage_reason: 香港における季節性インフルエンザの重症小児例報告であり、CHPによる定期サーベイランスの一環。重症度・流行しやすさの観点は該当するが、異常性や国際的拡大の懸念は低く、ルーチン報告の域を出ない。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザ（H1型）による重症小児例で、今季28例中2例死亡。香港衛生当局（CHP）による定期的な公衆衛生報告であり、ワクチン接種呼びかけが主目的。新規病原体や異常な拡大パターンは確認されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Експерти: Морбили отново може да стане ендемична болест в САЩ, това застрашава Европа
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Experts: Measles could once again become an endemic disease in the United States, which threatens Europe.
article.articleSummary: Measles could re-enter the United States as an endemic disease amid rising cases. US totals exceed 4,500 this year, nearly double 2023–24 levels. A JAMA projection warns that without improved vaccination, US endemicity could yield up to about 851,000 cases, more than 170,000 hospitalizations, and roughly 2,550 deaths over the next 25 years. Measles is highly contagious, transmitting four days before rash; 15 minutes of face-to-face contact can suffice. Global outbreaks are led by Bangladesh, Indonesia, and Guatemala. Europe’s vaccination coverage remains below the 95% elimination target, with about 92% first dose and 88% second dose; pockets of under-vaccination can spark clusters in otherwise protected populations. The Urkult festival in Sweden caused cases but no sustained transmission, reflecting herd immunity. In the WHO European region, 12 states are endemic and Romania had the most cases in 2024; six countries show re-established endemic transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 専門家:麻疹が再びアメリカで地方病化する可能性があり、それが欧州を脅かす
triage.triage_reason: 米国での麻疹再地方病化の可能性と、インドネシアを含む世界的な流行拡大が指摘されており、IHR基準が複数該当するためフルリスク評価に進むべきと判断した。
triage.notes: 記事は主に米国・欧州の麻疹動向に関する分析記事であり、インドネシアは世界的流行をリードする国の一つとして言及されているのみで、具体的な現地発生詳細は記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا" يحصد أرواح أكثر من 5000 شخص في الكونغو الديمقراطية منذ منتصف مايو الماضي
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola has claimed more than 5,000 lives in the Democratic Republic of the Congo since mid-May last year.
article.articleSummary: Ebola has claimed 5,026 lives and infected 10,351 people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo since mid-May 2025, health authorities say. Of the total cases, 1,101 individuals remain under treatment or in isolation, while 2,788 have recovered. The outbreak remains ongoing as of 2026-10-31, indicating sustained transmission within the DRC over more than a year. The report highlights a heavy disease burden with a high fatality count relative to cases and continued active cases.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、コンゴ民主共和国で昨年5月中旬以降5000人以上の死者を出す
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで1年以上にわたり継続し、致死率が高く症例数も多いため、IHR基準・WPRO基準の双方で複数該当しフルRRAが必要と判断される。
triage.notes: 致死率は約48.6%と非常に高く、長期間（1年以上）にわたる持続的な感染拡大が確認されている。国際的な支援の必要性が高いと推測される。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola suma más de cinco mil muertos en Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak has killed more than five thousand people in the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (declared May 15) has reached 10,351 confirmed infections and 5,026 deaths, with 2,788 recoveries and 1,101 hospitalized or in isolation as of Oct 29, per the National Institute of Public Health. Lethality is 48.6%, and contact tracing coverage is 84.5%. The epidemic, the second deadliest and most contagious in history, has spread to additional provinces; about 80% of new cases arise outside known contact chains, complicating control efforts. The AU and WHO have urged coordinated action, warning the outbreak remains uncontained. The Bundibugyo strain has no specific treatment; two vaccines are in early human trials. Congo began Ervebo vaccination in late August, with preliminary positive signals against Bundibugyo in animals. Cases linked to the outbreak have appeared in Uganda (20 cases, 15 imported, 2 deaths), Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths), Nigeria (1), and France; three evacuees reached the Netherlands (1) and Germany (2).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、死者5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で史上2番目に致死的なエボラ流行が進行中で、致死率48.6%、複数国への越境拡大も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリア、フランス、オランダ、ドイツへの波及症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。主発生地はDRC東部。

article.articleHeadline: السعودية تُعلّق السفر إلى كينيا بسبب الإيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Saudi Arabia suspends travel to Kenya due to Ebola
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, Saudi Arabia suspended travel to Kenya and halted issuing visas to travelers from Kenya, and barred entry of those arriving from Kenya or other Ebola-affected countries, including travelers arriving via third countries who had stayed in the affected areas within 21 days before arrival. The measures, adopted following risk assessments by the Saudi health authorities, build on July 2019 precautionary protocols and were enhanced in May 2026 for travellers from risk countries. In June 2026, Riyadh also suspended travel to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan and prohibited entries from those countries due to Ebola concerns. Additional safeguards apply to travelers from neighboring outbreak regions, including health screening at entry points, epidemiological investigations, and rapid-response procedures. The Saudi Public Health Authority (Weqaya) says the domestic health situation remains stable and is under continuous, vigilant surveillance, with ongoing regional and international coordination.

triage.headline_ja: サウジアラビア、エボラ出血熱を理由にケニアへの渡航を停止
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の流行を受け、サウジアラビアがケニア・DRC・ウガンダ・南スーダンへの渡航停止措置を実施しており、IHR基準（国際拡大リスク・渡航制限）に明確に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はサウジアラビアの渡航制限措置が主題だが、感染拡大国としてケニア・DRC・ウガンダ・南スーダンが言及されている。対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。ケニア・ウガンダ・南スーダン・サウジアラビアは対象国リスト外のためverified_locationsから除外。エボラ発生の一次情報源（WHO等）での確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Natal sem Peru? Entenda se doença aviária afetará ceia de final de ano
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Christmas Without Turkey? Find Out If Avian Disease Will Affect the Year-End Feast.
article.articleSummary: Newcastle disease (DNC) was detected at a turkey farm in Nova Itaberaba, Santa Catarina, Brazil, prompting immediate control measures by the Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária (MAPA). The site was blocked by the Official Veterinary Service, with bird movements suspended and the birds kept on site while the investigation continues; 6,000 birds were culled to eradicate the focus. DNC is a highly contagious viral disease affecting more than 200 bird species. In poultry, symptoms include sneezing, labored breathing, dropped wings, twisted neck, loss of appetite, and greenish diarrhea. Human infection is rare and usually mild, with conjunctivitis among the most common symptoms; exposure occurs via direct contact with infected birds or contaminated materials. Consumption of properly cooked poultry remains safe. Despite the outbreak, Brazil’s Christmas turkey supply is not expected to be affected; ABPA says holiday stocks are secured. Temporary export restrictions to Mexico, China (Santa Catarina), and Chile were announced, with no quantified economic impact yet.

triage.headline_ja: 七面鳥のないクリスマスに？ 鳥インフルエンザが年末の祝宴に影響するか解説
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルの七面鳥農場でニューカッスル病が検出されたが、ヒトへの感染は稀で軽症、家きん業者による迅速な封じ込め（殺処分・移動制限）が実施されており、国際的な公衆衛生リスクは低いと判断される。
triage.notes: 中国・メキシコ・チリへの輸出制限が発表されているが、発生地はブラジルのサンタカタリーナ州のみであり、他国は輸出先としての対象に過ぎないため verified_locations には含めない。ヒト感染は稀で軽症（結膜炎が主）であり、公衆衛生上の深刻な懸念は低い。

article.articleHeadline: حصيلة وفيات فيروس /إيبولا/ في الكونغو الديمقراطية تتجاوز 5000 حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola virus death toll in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa, 31 October 2026 — The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused 5,026 deaths and 10,351 infections since the latest flare was detected in mid‑May 2026. Health authorities report 1,101 people currently receiving treatment or in quarantine, with 2,788 recovered. The figures reflect cumulative totals for the ongoing outbreak as of 31 October, indicating sustained transmission in affected regions within the DRC. The report emphasizes the severity of the situation and the continued public health response by national authorities, underscoring the persistent risk of Ebola in the country and the need for ongoing surveillance, containment measures, and clinical management to curb further spread.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラウイルス死者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱がDRCで大規模な流行を継続しており(死者5,026人、感染者10,351人)、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 累計死者数が5,000人を超える大規模流行であり、2026年5月中旬から継続中。国際的な支援と監視体制の強化が必要とされる状況。

article.articleHeadline: Accusé de répandre le virus Ebola, un infirmier a été lynché à mort par la foule en République démocratique du Congo : "La santé n'est pas une cible", dénonce l'OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Accused of spreading the Ebola virus, a male nurse was beaten to death by a mob in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: "Health is not a target," says the WHO.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to fuel violence against health workers. On October 24, 2026, in Bafwasende, Tshopo Province, a nurse died and another was seriously injured after a mob accused responders of deliberately spreading the virus; Bafwasende has about 15,000 residents. Since the outbreak began in May 2026, attacks on clinicians and humanitarian staff, arson at health tents, and threats have hampered the response, amid rumors that responders disseminate the disease or possess vaccines they refuse to share. NPR highlights tensions around funeral protocols that keep families away from the deceased, increasing contamination risk with certain rites. UN Ebola coordinator Julien Harneis condemned the attack and called for a thorough investigation; WHO Africa regional director Dr. Mohamed Yakub Janabi stressed that health is not a target and urged action against misinformation. This incident illustrates the peril frontline workers face and ongoing transmission risk.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスを拡散させたと非難された看護師が、コンゴ民主共和国で群衆によってリンチされ死亡：「医療は標的ではない」とWHOが非難
triage.triage_reason: 2026年5月以降継続中のDRCエボラ流行において、医療従事者への暴力が頻発し対応が阻害されている。IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し、国際機関（WHO・UN）の関与や社会的関心も高いためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 記事は2026年5月に始まったDRCエボラ流行における医療従事者への暴力事件を報じている。流行は継続中であり、対応妨害による感染拡大リスクが懸念される。地域情報のBafwasende・Tshopoは国レベルの対象リストに含まれないため、DRCのみをverified_locationsとした。

article.articleHeadline: 7歲女童感染甲流危殆　同班3名同學現輕微流感病徵 (17:39) - 20261031
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 7-year-old girl infected with influenza A in critical condition; three classmates in the same class now showing mild flu symptoms (17:39) - 20261031
article.articleSummary: 7-year-old girl in Hong Kong is critically ill with Influenza A(H1) presenting septic shock. Respiratory samples tested positive for influenza A(H1) at Tuen Mun Hospital after onset of runny nose, diarrhea and abdominal pain on Oct 29, followed by fever and convulsions on Oct 30, leading to admission to the pediatric intensive care unit. She had no travel during the incubation period and was unvaccinated against seasonal influenza. Household contacts are asymptomatic. In the same class, three classmates have recently developed mild flu-like symptoms and did not require hospitalization. No deaths reported. This case triggers local surveillance for possible spread within the class; no information on imported or exported cases.

triage.headline_ja: 7歳女児が甲型インフルエンザに感染し重篤、同じクラスの3人の同級生に軽い流感症状
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザA(H1)による重症例が1例報告されたが、季節性流行株であり異常性は低い。同級生3名に軽症の感染が見られるため、クラス内拡大の可能性を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザA(H1N1)による香港での小規模クラスター。重症例は1例のみで、他は軽症。地域の学校内サーベイランスが開始されたが、国際的な拡大リスクは低いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Number of Ebola deaths passes 5,000 amid fears over containment efforts
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 31, 2026, DR Congo's Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus has 5,026 deaths from 10,351 infections, with 2,788 recoveries (nearly 50% case-fatality). Declared mid-May, the outbreak has spread to 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, with 50 zones currently active. Ituri and North Kivu remain epicenters, reporting 9,782 total confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths. The Bundibugyo virus has no vaccine or specific treatment; patient care is supportive. Containment is hampered by ongoing eastern Congo conflict, including M23 activity and Islamist insurgencies near Uganda, with attacks on health workers. triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の死者数が5,000人を超える、封じ込め対策への懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で発生したエボラ（ブンディブギョウイルス）が死者5,000人超・致死率約50%に達し、ケニア・ナイジェリアへの拡大、スイスへの患者搬送も確認されるなど国際的拡大リスクが極めて高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへの感染/搬送事例があるが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。DRCが発生の主体かつ対象国に該当するため記載。ワクチン・特異的治療法がないブンディブギョウイルス株であり、紛争地域での対応困難も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as worry of continent-wide spread mounts
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo, caused by Bundibugyo virus, has reached 5,026 deaths from 10,351 infections, according to the Congolese Ministry of Health. Centered in Bunia, the mid-May outbreak has persisted, with the latest data reported on Saturday. The case-fatality rate stands at about 49–50%. Cases are recorded in other African countries, indicating continued spread beyond the initial epicenter. Authorities describe the surge as a challenge to containment efforts and raise fears of continent-wide spread. This outbreak is the second-deadliest Ebola episode on record, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak that killed about 11,000 people across multiple countries. The figures underscore the ongoing severity and the urgent need for intensified public health response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超え、大陸規模の拡大懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: 死者5,000人超・致死率約50%という深刻な公衆衛生インパクトがあり、他のアフリカ諸国への拡大も報告されているためIHR基準で複数該当し、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 記事ではアンゴラ等他国への拡大が示唆されているが、対象国リストにDRC以外の該当国（アンゴラ）は含まれないため記載せず。2014-2016年の西アフリカ流行に次ぐ規模とされ、歴史的にも重大な流行。

article.articleHeadline: Viện Pasteur TPHCM hỗ trợ Cà Mau ứng phó bệnh não mô cầu
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ho Chi Minh City Pasteur Institute assists Ca Mau in responding to meningococcal disease.
article.articleSummary: Ca Mau Province, Vietnam reports 8 meningococcal disease cases in 2026 through Oct 30, with 3 deaths. In October, 3 cases occurred; two deaths in Song Doc commune were five days apart and linked to Neisseria meningitidis group B. The Ca Mau Center for Disease Control is investigating infection sources and epidemiological links, and has identified 87 close contacts for prophylaxis and health monitoring. Ho Chi Minh City Pasteur Institute, led by PGS.TS Nguyen Vu Thuong, is assisting Ca Mau with field supervision, prevention measures, and capacity building, stressing early detection, rapid reporting, effective treatment, infection control in communities and schools, and coordinated response plans. The local health sector is urged to bolster diagnostic capacity, stock medications and equipment, and train staff to recognize meningococcal signs. Separately, Ho Chi Minh City reports five student meningococcal cases in Oct 14–20, with one death, underscoring school-based surveillance needs. Neisseria meningitidis can cause meningitis or septicemia and spreads via respiratory secretions.

triage.headline_ja: ホーチミン市パスツール研究所、カマウ省の髄膜炎菌感染症対応を支援
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・カマウ省で髄膜炎菌感染症のクラスター発生（8例中3例死亡、短期間に複数死亡）に加え、ホーチミン市でも学校関連の集団発生（1例死亡）が報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへの移行が妥当。
triage.notes: カマウ省とホーチミン市の2クラスターが報告されており、学校関連感染拡大のリスクと濃厚接触者87名の管理状況など続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Bhagalpur News: बांका: खुरपका बीमारी से पशुपालकों में मायूसी, विभाग बेखबर
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bhagalpur News: Banka: Foot-and-mouth disease leaves livestock owners disappointed, department unaware.
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease is spreading rapidly among livestock in Banka block, Bhagalpur district, Bihar, with Dhkana and Bandri villages among the hardest hit and dozens of villages affected. Farmers report animals displaying signs of the disease, but there has been no concrete action from the Department of Animal Husbandry. They fear a swift spread could cause substantial economic losses if not controlled. Residents have urged authorities to deploy veterinary teams, provide treatment, medicines, and vaccination, and launch a targeted campaign to stop transmission. The article does not provide case counts, laboratory confirmation, or infection sources, only growing concern and calls for intervention as of 31 October 2026.

triage.headline_ja: バガルプールニュース：バンカ：口蹄疫の流行で畜産農家が落胆、当局は無反応
triage.triage_reason: 動物の口蹄疫発生であり人への直接影響は確認されていないが、獣医当局の対応不足により拡大が懸念されるため継続観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 本事例は動物（家畜）の口蹄疫であり、人獣共通感染症としてのヒトへの感染リスクは記事内で言及されていない。経済的損失への懸念と当局の対応不足が住民の関心を集めているが、人の公衆衛生への直接的影響は不明。

article.articleHeadline: Cambian los requisitos para ingresar a Estados Unidos por un brote de ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Entry requirements for entering the United States change due to an Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: CDC issues a health-entry rule for U.S.-bound travel due to an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Effective 23:59 on November 3, 2026, all international flights to the United States require a signed declaration stating the traveler has not been in the DRC during the prior 21 days. The measure applies to U.S. citizens, permanent residents, foreign nationals, and flight crews on destination or transit itineraries through U.S. airports. Exemptions cover overflights that do not land, aircraft carrying patients with government authorization, and emergency medical evacuations. Anyone with physical presence in the DRC in the last 21 days must wait 21 days outside that country before boarding to the U.S. Special provisions for those who recently stayed in Uganda or South Sudan: U.S. citizens may enter via designated airports for health checks; foreign nationals and permanent residents cannot enter until 21 days since leaving those countries. Airlines must collect and retain declarations for at least 42 days and verify them prior to boarding. The order remains in effect through December 18, 2026, unless updated.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行により、米国への入国要件が変更
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱流行を受け、米国が渡航制限（入国要件変更）を既に発動しており、IHR基準の国際的拡大リスク・渡航貿易制限に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はCDCによる米国の入国規制に関する内容で、発生源はDRCのエボラ流行。ウガンダ・南スーダンも言及されるが対象国リストに含まれず除外。米国も対象国リスト外。

article.articleHeadline: Korban Jiwa Wabah Ebola di RD Kongo Tembus 5.000 Orang : Okezone News
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak death toll in DR Congo reaches 5,000
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa authorities say Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have surpassed 5,000, marking the deadliest Ebola outbreak on record in the country. The outbreak, declared in May 2026, has infected over 10,000 people. It is driven by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no approved treatment or vaccine. Delays in detection, ongoing conflict, and overwhelmed health systems have allowed the virus to spread, now reaching eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces. The latest death toll was announced on Friday, 30 October 2026. The outbreak remains ongoing with no containment. The report provides no details on infection sources or cross-border export cases.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、死者数が5,000人を突破
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最悪規模のエボラ流行が進行中であり、死者数・感染者数が甚大かつ8州に拡大、治療・ワクチンもなく国際的拡大リスクが高いため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ワクチン・治療薬が未承認のBundibugyo株による史上最悪規模のエボラ流行。紛争により医療システムが圧迫され、封じ込めに至っていない。国境を越えた輸出例の有無は記事内で言及なし。

article.articleHeadline: 민주콩고 에볼라 사망자 5천명 넘어...아프리카 전역 확산 우려
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 5,000, raising concerns about spread across Africa.
article.articleSummary: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have surpassed 5,000, with 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed cases as of Oct 30 local time, per AP citing the DRC health ministry; about 2,788 people have recovered. WHO notes roughly one-third of deaths occurred without care before testing. This outbreak ranks as the second-largest Ebola spread on record, after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (28,616 cases, 11,310 deaths), but is spreading more rapidly. The virus involved is Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare form for which no approved vaccines or therapeutics exist. Much of the outbreak area lies in rebel-held territory, hindering response, with public distrust and unpaid salaries complicating control efforts. Last week Nigeria reported Ebola infections, signaling spread to West Africa, and cases have also emerged in East Africa’s Kenya and Uganda.

article.articleHeadline: UGM Kaji Teknologi Wolbachia untuk Menekan Penularan DBD, Seberapa Efektif?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gadjah Mada University Studies Wolbachia Technology to Curb Dengue Transmission, How Effective Is It?
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever remains a major public health issue in Indonesia. Gadjah Mada University (UGM) and partners are evaluating Wolbachia-based dengue control through the SHIELD project in five Indonesian cities, including Yogyakarta and Semarang, to assess effectiveness, sustainability, costs, and integration with other interventions such as vaccination. Wolbachia is a naturally occurring bacterium that, when present in Aedes aegypti, inhibits dengue virus replication and transmission. It is released into the environment to increase the proportion of Wolbachia-infected mosquitos. In Yogyakarta, the intervention reduced dengue incidence by 77% and dengue-related hospitalizations by 86%. Monitoring in 2023–2024 showed Wolbachia in 89% of local Aedes aegypti. Over five years after full deployment in Yogyakarta, dengue cases were 76% lower than in comparable Java cities without Wolbachia. Semarang shows positive trends with Wolbachia above 60%. Wolbachia complements, rather than replaces, existing dengue control efforts (3M Plus).

triage.triage_reason: 本記事はデング熱対策技術（ウォルバキア）の研究・効果評価に関する報道であり、新規の異常発生や公衆衛生危機を示すものではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: デング熱は地域の既知の風土病であり、本記事はその対策技術（ウォルバキア法）の有効性研究に関するもので、アウトブレイクや異常事態の報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola deaths exceed 5,000 as fears grow over spread across Africa
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-31, the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Bundibugyo virus Ebola outbreak has killed 5,026 people among 10,351 recorded infections, with a case fatality rate near 49%. Declared in mid-May, the outbreak is the second-deadliest Ebola episode on record after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. Government data indicate the virus has spread beyond Congo to four other countries, fueling fears of wider cross-border transmission. The Bundibugyo strain, first identified in Uganda in 2007 and previously infecting the DRC in 2012, features symptoms such as fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, sore throat, and can progress to vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and kidney/liver impairment; bleeding may occur in late stages. There is no approved vaccine or specific antiviral for Bundibugyo; management relies on early diagnosis, isolation, and supportive care. Ebola spreads via contact with blood, secretions, and bodies of the deceased, and through contaminated surfaces.

Africa CDC offered condolences and urged greater protection for health workers. The outbreak, declared May 15, 2026, is caused by the Bundibugyo Ebola virus, a rare strain with no approved targeted therapy or vaccine. As of October 28, 2026, the official tally lists 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths (case fatality rate 48.6%), with spread to 67 health zones across eight of 26 provinces. In Beni, 661 cases and 443 deaths (CFR 67%); in North Kivu province overall, 2,391 cases and 1,341 deaths. Some government figures cited by Al Jazeera exceed 5,000 deaths. Challenges hindering response include delayed detection, ongoing conflict, and overwhelmed health services.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Two deaths from meningococcal meningitis in Ca Mau: Source of infection not yet known—what recommendations has the Pasteur Institute in Ho Chi Minh City issued?
article.articleSummary: Ca Mau Province, Vietnam, reports two meningococcal meningitis deaths in Song Doc commune, bringing the province’s total to three deaths as of Oct 31, 2026. The first case is a 46-year-old woman from Tan Hoa hamlet who onset Oct 20 with fever and chills, then cough and rash; she was hospitalized Oct 22–23 and died. The second case is a 33-year-old woman from Rach Dinh hamlet who developed sore throat, fever, and rash on Oct 27; she was admitted the same day, transferred to Ca Mau Provincial Hospital at about 19:35, and died despite treatment. The infection source remains unidentified; health authorities are tracing close contacts and surveilling the surrounding area. Carriage of Neisseria meningitidis may be 10–25% in the community, so contacts should receive prophylactic antibiotics and be isolated for 10 days or longer. Authorities will partner with Pasteur Institute Ho Chi Minh City and Ho Chi Minh City Tropical Disease Hospital to strengthen detection, screening, and treatment.

MSF teams are continuing to operate across six of the eight affected provinces to contain transmission and save lives.

article.articleHeadline: Experten gehen von Dunkelziffer bei Ebola-Toten aus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Experts estimate an undercount of Ebola deaths.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reports 5,026 Ebola deaths, with infections rising across eight provinces, making it Africa’s fastest-growing outbreak. Experts warn official counts underestimate the true impact, with infections potentially two to three times higher due to surveillance gaps and underreporting. More than half of deaths occur outside treatment centers amid security constraints and limited aid access, while contact tracing remains weak and cases often die at home or in non-Ebola facilities where they go unrecognized. Bundibugyo symptoms can resemble malaria. There is no Bundibugyo-specific licensed vaccine; Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus) may offer partial protection, supported by lab data showing T-cell responses against Bundibugyo and Sudan viruses. Bundibugyo vaccines are in early trials since July, with broad deployment unlikely before mid-2027. MSF warns production bottlenecks could limit vaccine access; conflict zones in the North-East complicate response.
