article.articleHeadline: Saudi Arabia bans entry of travellers from Kenya over Ebola concerns
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak prompts Saudi Arabia to ban entry from Kenya and suspend Kenyan visas, restricting direct arrivals and travellers transiting through other countries who have stayed in Kenya or any outbreak country within the previous 21 days. Saudi also bans travel by its citizens to Kenya and halts issuance of all Kenyan visas, while maintaining restrictions on travellers from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. Across Africa, the multi-country Ebola outbreak exceeds 10,000 confirmed cases and 5,030 deaths as of 31 Oct 2026. The DRC reports 10,351 cases and 5,026 deaths; Uganda 20 cases, 2 deaths; Kenya 9 cases, 2 deaths; Nigeria monitoring one imported case, with no deaths. In Kenya, the situation is stable with no new infections in more than 10 days; nine cases linked to a single DRC-related cluster, no community transmission. First 20 contacts completed 21-day quarantine; remaining 98 to be released in phases from next week.

triage.headline_ja: サウジアラビア、エボラ懸念でケニアからの渡航者の入国を禁止
triage.triage_reason: 複数国にまたがるエボラ流行で1万例超・5千人超の死亡が報告されており、国際的な渡航制限措置（サウジアラビアによる入国禁止）も実際に発生しているためIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCを起点とする多国間エボラ流行とサウジアラビアによる渡航制限措置について報じている。対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみで、ケニア・ウガンダ・南スーダン・ナイジェリア・サウジアラビアは対象国リスト外のためverified_locationsから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Surto de ébola na RDCongo já provocou mais de 5 mil mortos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has already claimed more than 5,000 lives.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has claimed 5,026 lives from 10,351 confirmed infections as of Oct 29, 2026. Case fatality is 48.6%; 2,788 have recovered and 1,101 are hospitalized or in isolation. The outbreak began May 15 in eastern DRC and has spread to eight provinces, with Ituri (36.4%) and North Kivu (58.4%) accounting for the majority of new cases; 67 health zones across eight of 26 provinces are affected. Bundibugyo strain; no specific treatment, though Ervebo vaccination campaign started in late August. Uganda reported 20 cases (including 15 imported from DRC) and ended its outbreak on Aug 26. Other linked cases appeared in Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths), Nigeria (1 case), and an associated case in France; evacuated infections in the Netherlands (1) and Germany (2). Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and hemorrhagic manifestations. WHO and the African Union urge urgent coordinated action.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク、死者5000人超に
triage.triage_reason: 大規模なエボラアウトブレイクが複数国に拡大し死亡率48.6%と非常に高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため即時フルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリア、フランス、オランダ、ドイツでも関連症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないか、DRCからの輸入例であるため、主発生地であるDRCのみをverified_locationsに記載。WHOおよびアフリカ連合が緊急対応を要請している点から、既にWHO通知相当の深刻な国際的イベントと判断。

article.articleHeadline: コンゴのエボラ熱死者5000人超える　承認済みワクチンなく流行収束めど立たず
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 5,000; with no approved vaccine, no end in sight to the outbreak.
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 30, 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 10,351 cases and 5,026 deaths, driven by the eastern Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain. The outbreak spans eight provinces, and there is no approved vaccine for Bundibugyo, limiting prevention and leaving the trajectory uncertain. Beyond the DRC, Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria have reported cases, indicating cross-border spread. An AU CDC official Kasaye on Oct 29 urged a continent-wide response, emphasizing coordinated public health action. Ongoing armed conflict in eastern DRC complicates case finding and contact tracing, hampering containment efforts. The article provides no vaccine or end-date, signaling an ongoing outbreak with continued transmission and rising regional concern.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ熱死者5000人超える　承認済みワクチンなく流行収束めど立たず
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）が1万人超の症例・5000人超の死者を出し、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境拡大が報告されており、IHR基準の複数該当とWPRO基準にも該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ブンディブギョ株に承認済みワクチンがなく、東部の武力紛争により症例探知・接触者追跡が困難な状況。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola im Kongo: Experten gehen von Dunkelziffer bei Ebola-Toten aus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Congo: Experts estimate an undercount of Ebola deaths.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-31, more than half of Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo occurred outside treatment centers, increasing transmission risk to families and communities. Security challenges, displacement, and restricted aid hinder surveillance and response; contact tracing remains inadequate and many patients die at home or in ordinary hospitals not recognized as Ebola. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, whose symptoms can resemble malaria. Most cases are in the North-East and East, conflict-affected regions with many militias, further limiting care-seeking. There is no licensed Bundibugyo-specific vaccine. The Ervebo vaccine against Zaire ebolavirus may trigger T-cell responses to Bundibugyo and Sudan viruses in a German lab study, but cross-protection is unproven. MSF warns production bottlenecks could limit Ervebo access. Bundibugyo vaccines are in early trials since July; broad use is unlikely before mid-2027. No official outbreak duration estimates.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱：専門家は死者数が過少申告されていると推定
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行が拡大し、治療施設外での死亡が半数以上、紛争地域での対応困難、有効ワクチン未確立という重大かつ異常な状況であり、国際的拡大・管理困難性の観点からフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ドイツは研究機関（ワクチン交差防御研究）としての言及のみで、発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外。ブンディブギョ株のためEvebo（ザイール株用）の有効性は未証明。

article.articleHeadline: Muertes por ébola en Congo superan las 5,000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola deaths in Congo exceed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo exceed 5,000, with 5,026 fatalities among 10,351 infections, a case fatality rate around 50%. The Congolese Ministry of Health reported these figures on Saturday, October 31, 2026, describing the outbreak as the second deadliest in Ebola history as transmission remains relentless. Cases have also been reported in other African nations, signaling broader regional spread and ongoing pressure on health systems. The report notes ongoing transmission and a high toll, underscoring the ongoing challenge for health authorities.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ出血熱による死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%で死者5,000人超、感染拡大が継続し他のアフリカ諸国にも波及しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し国際的懸念が高い。
triage.notes: 記事では他のアフリカ諸国での症例報告にも言及しているが、具体的な国名（対象国リスト内）は明示されていないため、DRCのみをverified_locationsに含めた。

article.articleHeadline: У ДР Конга колькасць загінулых ад ліхаманкі Эбола перавысіла пяць тысяч чалавек
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the DR Congo, the death toll from Ebola fever has surpassed five thousand people.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo continues a major Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus. Since May 2026, 10,351 people have been infected and 5,026 have died (roughly a 49% fatality rate). There is currently no approved vaccine for this strain. The weekly incidence remains 400–500 new cases, with less than a quarter linked to known transmission chains, complicating detection and isolation. An Emory University infectious-disease expert, Bogumi Titandji, notes the virus is propagating at a very high, sustained level. Armed conflict, mistrust of health workers, and shrinking international aid hinder control efforts. Cases have been reported outside the DRC in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda; European epidemiological services assess the EU risk as very low. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids of symptomatic individuals; initial symptoms include high fever, headache, and muscle pain, followed by vomiting, diarrhea, and bleeding, with severe cases ending in multi-organ failure.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱による死者数が5000人を超えた
triage.triage_reason: DRCで大規模なエボラ流行（感染1万人超、死者5千人超、致死率約49%）が継続し、周辺国にも拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリアでの症例報告があるが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。承認ワクチンが存在しない点、武力紛争・医療従事者への不信・国際支援減少が制御を阻害している点が特に懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Mongbwalu Ebola Center Clears Confirmed Cases as DRC Reports 77 New Confirmed Cases | EconoTimes
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus disease (Ebola) in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with Mongbwalu, Ituri province, reporting a milestone as no confirmed cases remained under care at Mongbwalu after the last discharged patients. For the period ending Oct 29, INSP reported 77 new confirmed cases and 34 deaths, lifting national totals to 10,351 confirmed cases and 5,026 deaths, with 2,788 recoveries and 1,101 in isolation or treatment centers, amounting to a 48.6% case-fatality rate. MSF runs Mongbwalu with 65 beds and notes six of eight provinces are affected, with ongoing case detection elsewhere; six provinces currently active in response. WHO has described transmission as elevated through Oct 20, 201; the outbreak is characterized as moving rather than shrinking and constitutes the largest Bundibugyo outbreak in the DRC, and the second documented Bundibugyo outbreak in the country since 2012.

triage.headline_ja: モングバルのエボラセンター、確定症例をクリア、一方DRCは77件の新規確定症例を報告
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大のブンディブギョ型エボラアウトブレイクが継続中で、累計死亡5,026人・CFR48.6%と深刻かつ異常な公衆衛生事象であり、複数州に拡大しているためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: WHO・MSFが関与する進行中の大規模アウトブレイクで、6州中6州が影響を受けており、感染拡大は縮小ではなく移動していると報告されている。史上最大のブンディブギョ型エボラ流行かつ2012年以降2例目の同型流行。

article.articleHeadline: В ДР Конго число погибших от лихорадки Эбола превысило пять тысяч человек
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the number of deaths from Ebola fever has exceeded five thousand.
article.articleSummary: Since May 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused 5,026 deaths among 10,351 infections, making it the second-deadliest Ebola epidemic on record. The outbreak is driven by Bundibugyo virus, with no approved vaccine available. Weekly, 400–500 new cases are detected, and less than a quarter are linked to known transmission chains, complicating case finding and isolation. Ongoing challenges include armed conflict, distrust of health workers, and reduced international aid. Cases have been reported outside the DRC, including Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda. Transmission occurs through direct contact with bodily fluids of symptomatic patients, who become infectious after symptom onset. Symptoms commonly start with high fever and headache, then vomiting, diarrhea, bleeding, and potential multi-organ failure in severe cases. European public health authorities consider EU risk very low, citing strengthened surveillance and contact tracing.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱による死者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が大規模流行し、周辺国（ケニア、ナイジェリア、ウガンダ）にも症例が波及しており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大）に該当するため。
triage.notes: ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。記事はDRC国内の大規模流行が主題であり、他国への拡大は懸念事項として言及されている。

article.articleHeadline: 近打县蚊症飙升136.8% 雨季需清理室内外积水
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Jinda County Mosquito-Borne Disease Surges by 136.8%; Rainy Season Requires Clearing Indoor and Outdoor Standing Water
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever in Perak, Malaysia, shows a sharp rise. In the 41st epidemiological week (Oct 11–17), Jinda County recorded 71 dengue cases, pushing the weekly total to 2576 with 29 cases in a single day; two deaths occurred in Jiangsha and Muya Lin. Year-on-year incidence surged 66.9% statewide, led by near district (Kinta) with 49 cases (69.01% of Perak’s total). Other districts also reported cases, while surveillance notes 24 active outbreak zones (8 new), with 7 controlled, 2 uncontrolled, 1 hotspot, and 6 ended. By Oct 17, 1034 cases occurred in outbreak zones and 1434 in non-outbreak zones. The northeast monsoon is forecast to persist through March 2027, with heavier rainfall from Nov 2026–Jan 2027. Public health advisories urge clearing indoor and outdoor standing water and inspecting containers such as water-filter trays, dish-rack bases, storage vessels, and pet bowls to curb Aedes breeding.

triage.headline_ja: 近打県の蚊媒介感染症が136.8%急増、雨季に向け屋内外の水たまり除去が必要
triage.triage_reason: マレーシア・ペラ州（近打県）でデング熱症例が急増し死亡例も発生しているが、季節性の流行であり国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは認められず、対象国リストにも該当しないため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 本イベントはマレーシア（対象国リスト外）での季節性デング熱流行であり、発生地域リストに含まれる中国（江西省）は記事主題と無関係のため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: V Demokratični republiki Kongo zaradi ebole umrlo že več kot pet tisoč ljudi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, more than five thousand people have already died from Ebola.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ebola caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus is spreading rapidly. Since the outbreak was officially declared on May 15, authorities report 5,026 deaths and 10,351 infections, with about 1,100 people in quarantine or under treatment. The true toll may be higher, as experts say the virus may have circulated undetected since February. Bundibugyo ebolavirus is difficult to contain and currently has no approved vaccine for this strain. Since July, two antiviral treatments are in clinical trials, and vaccine candidates are under evaluation. Researchers are also testing whether Ervebo, an existing Ebola vaccine for the Zaire strain, offers protection against Bundibugyo. Ebola transmits through direct contact with infected individuals or their bodily fluids and can cause high fever, diarrhea, and bleeding.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱により既に5千人以上が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 多数の死者・感染者を伴う大規模なエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行であり、承認ワクチンがない点やヒト-ヒト感染の継続性から国際的拡大リスクが高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ株には承認ワクチンがなく、既存のザイール株用ワクチン(Ervebo)の有効性を検証中。感染拡大が2月から未検出で続いていた可能性があり、実際の規模はさらに大きい可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: Smrtonosni virus se širi z zaskrbljujočo hitrostjo, umrlo že več kot 5000 ljudi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The deadly virus is spreading at an alarming rate; more than 5,000 people have already died.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, declared May 15, 2026, with 5,026 deaths among 10,351 reported cases. About 1,100 people are currently in quarantine or receiving treatment. The true toll may be higher, as spread could have begun as early as February before the official declaration. Since July, two antiviral treatments are in clinical trials, and vaccine development is underway, including testing whether the Ervebo vaccine protects against the Bundibugyo strain. Ebola transmits via direct contact with infected individuals or their bodily fluids and can cause high fever, diarrhea, and bleeding. The report highlights ongoing transmission and active research efforts in antiviral therapies and vaccines in response to the outbreak in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: 致死性ウイルスが憂慮すべき速度で拡大、死者はすでに5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクで死者5,000人超・症例1万人超と深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、IHR基準の複数（深刻性、国際拡大リスク）に該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 致死率が高く（約49%）、2月以前から拡大していた可能性があり過小報告の懸念あり。ワクチン・治療薬の臨床試験が進行中で国際的な支援・関心が高い案件。

article.articleHeadline: Mehr als 5000 Ebola-Tote im Kongo - Experten rechnen mit hoher Dunkelziffer
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 Ebola deaths in the Congo — experts expect a high undercount.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo reports 10,351 Ebola virus disease infections and 5,026 deaths across eight provinces, marking the fastest-growing outbreak on the continent. Since the official announcement on May 15, the true burden is likely higher, with estimates suggesting infections could be two to three times the confirmed figures. Currently 1,101 people are in treatment or isolation, and 2,788 have recovered. A large share of fatalities occur at home or outside treatment centers, hindering surveillance and raising transmission risk to families. Conflict in the northeast complicates containment, with limited access for aid workers and disrupted contact tracing. Exported cases include Kenya (death linked to Congo exposure), Nigeria’s first case (October 20), and a European case linked to a doctor active in the Congo. No licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo ebolavirus; Ervebo may offer limited cross-protection via T cells, while a Bundibugyo-specific vaccine remains important.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ死者5000人超 ― 専門家は実際の数はさらに多いとみている
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱がコンゴで急拡大し、ケニア・ナイジェリア・欧州に越境拡大しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・欧州への輸出症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれない（ナイジーリアは対象国リストになし、ケニアも対象外）ため、主発生国であるDRCのみをverified_locationsに記載。紛争地域における対応の困難さと未承認ワクチンの問題が懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,000
article.articleSummary: Outbreak: Ebola in Congo caused by the Bundibugyo strain. As of 30 October 2026, Daily Monitor (Uganda) reports the Congo Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,000 people. The Bundibugyo species is described as rare, and there are no approved treatments or vaccines to combat this strain. The article provides limited detail and does not specify laboratory confirmation, transmission routes, or public health responses. The report highlights the absence of licensed medical countermeasures for Bundibugyo Ebola, underscoring the severity implied by the reported death toll. The piece does not include information on imported or exported cases or other affected locations beyond Congo.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱流行、死者5,000人以上
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行で死者5,000人超と報告されており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と承認された治療薬・ワクチンの不在という異常性から、IHR基準・WPRO基準いずれも複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事は死者数5,000人以上という重大な数値を報告しているが、検査確認、感染経路、公衆衛生対応等の詳細情報が欠如しており、続報・一次情報源での確認が必要。ウガンダは発生地域として付与されているが、記事サマリー上ではコンゴでの発生のみが主題であり、ウガンダでの発生は言及されていないため verified_locations から除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in DR Congo surpasses 5,000
article.articleSummary: Kinshasa reports that the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed more than 5,000 people and infected over 10,000 since it was declared in May. The Bundibugyo strain is responsible, with no approved treatments or vaccines. Containment has been hampered by detection delays, ongoing conflict, and weak health systems, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centers. The outbreak has spread to eight of the country’s 26 provinces, marking the largest in DR Congo’s history and the world’s second-largest Ebola epidemic after the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak, which caused more than 28,600 infections and over 11,000 deaths. On Oct 31, the National Institute of Public Health confirmed more than 10,000 confirmed Ebola cases in the country. Transmission is by direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴのエボラ死者数、5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRコンゴ史上最大規模のエボラ流行で死者5,000人超・感染者10,000人超、8州に拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 承認されたワクチン・治療薬がなく、紛争と脆弱な保健システムにより封じ込めが困難な状況。史上最大規模のDRコンゴでのエボラ流行であり、周辺国（アンゴラ等）への越境拡大リスクにも注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Meer dan 5.000 doden en 10.000 besmettingen door ebola-uitbraak in Democratische Republiek Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 deaths and 10,000 infections due to the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has caused 5,026 deaths and 10,351 infections since May, in under six months. The circulating Bundibugyo variant has no approved vaccines or treatments. The epicenter is eastern DRC, especially Ituri and North Kivu. Transmission occurs via contaminated bodily fluids—sweat, saliva, vomit, and blood. Weak health systems, aid cuts, and regional conflict hinder containment. Contact tracing is challenging; Africa CDC says about 80% of new infections occur outside monitored contact chains. Nigeria reported a case last week, following earlier cases in Kenya and Uganda; Nigeria is the fourth African country affected. In the past two months, roughly 490 weekly cases. This is the second-largest Ebola outbreak in history, after 2014–2016 West Africa (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone), which had over 28,600 cases and more than 11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行、死者5,000人超・感染者10,000人超に
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が大規模流行し複数国へ拡大、ワクチン未承認の変異株で国際的拡大リスクが高いためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア、ケニア、ウガンダへの拡大が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCが主たる発生地域であり唯一の対象国該当地域。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola death toll nears 5,000 as Africa CDC honors fallen doctor
article.articleSummary: DR Congo’s ongoing Ebola outbreak has 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths as of Oct 28, CFR 48.6%. Declared May 15 and caused by Bundibugyo virus, the outbreak affects 67 health zones across eight provinces, including Beni in North Kivu. Dr. Marie-France Shogogo died from Ebola in Beni, and Africa CDC honored her posthumously, highlighting frontline worker protections; three doctors died within 72 hours at an Ebola treatment center in Beni. North Kivu reports 2,391 confirmed cases and 1,341 deaths, with Beni’s 661 cases and 443 deaths (CFR 67.0%). Health facilities run at 86.3% capacity, while only 82.2% of identified contacts are monitored, below the 95% target, underscoring mounting strain in what is the world’s second-largest Ebola outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ死者数が5,000人に迫る中、アフリカCDCが殉職した医師を追悼
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.6%、約1万例・約5000人死亡という大規模アウトブレイクで、医療従事者の死亡や接触者追跡率が目標を下回るなど公衆衛生への深刻な影響と拡大リスクが明白であり、IHR基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 世界で2番目に大きいエボラアウトブレイクとされ、医療従事者の死亡や接触者追跡率の不足など対応能力の限界が示唆されている。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en la República Democrática del Congo ya supera los 5.000 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths, with 10,351 confirmed infections as of October 29, according to the National Institute of Public Health (INSP). Declared May 15, the outbreak is expanding to additional provinces, stressing regional health services. Deaths total 5,026, yielding a case fatality rate of 48.6%. Recoveries reach 2,788, while 1,101 patients remain hospitalized or under strict isolation. Contact tracing coverage is 84.5%, yet about 80% of new cases arise outside the traced networks, fueling community transmission. INSP calls for reinforced early detection, expanded contact tracing, and safe, dignified burials as core containment pillars, noting logistical and cultural challenges. The ongoing transmission underscores a severe public health emergency in Africa, with intensified surveillance and containment needed in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク、死者5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.6%・死者5,000人超の大規模エボラアウトブレイクで、追跡網外での市中感染が約80%に達するなど制御困難な拡大傾向があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 2026年5月15日に宣言されたアウトブレイクが複数州に拡大中で、接触者追跡網外の新規症例が約80%を占めるなど地域社会内での持続的な感染が示唆される。継続的なフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola-Virus: Mehr als 5.000 Tote in der Demokratischen Republik Kongo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola virus: More than 5,000 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues, with 5,026 deaths and 10,351 infections since May; 2,788 recoveries and over 1,000 people currently treated or under quarantine. The Bundibugyo strain is responsible; transmission occurs via body fluids, contact with contaminated objects, animal-to-human spillover, and unsafe burials. Early symptoms resemble malaria, delaying detection. Security constraints in eastern DRC from armed groups, including M23, hinder response and contribute to attacks on health workers and facilities, including a nurse killed and a politician murdered. Outside the DRC, 31 cases have been reported in Uganda, Nigeria, and Kenya, with at least four deaths; Europe records one case in France (June). In Nigeria, the wife of a Swiss diplomat tested positive, treated in Abuja, then evacuated to Switzerland. Since June, two antivirals are in trials; a local Oct 23 vaccination study in DRC tests Ervebo against Bundibugyo.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルス：コンゴ民主共和国で死者5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で5,000人以上の死者を伴う大規模エボラ流行が継続し、ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・ケニア・欧州への国際的拡大も確認されているため、IHR基準を複数満たしフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・ケニア・フランス・スイスでも症例が確認されているが、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。東部DRCでの武装勢力（M23等）による治安悪化が対応を妨げている点も重要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola deaths top 5,000 in DR Congo as WHO fears continent-wide spread of virus that kills half of infected
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo virus, has killed 5,026 people (out of 10,351 infections), a fatality rate near 50%. The mid-May outbreak has spread to 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, making it the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (about 11,000 deaths). There is no vaccine or specific treatment; care is supportive, focusing on hydration, managing shock, and treating bacterial infections. Authorities face challenges with contact tracing and testing amid local skepticism, and health workers have staged strikes over unpaid wages, including incidents at Tchomia, Ituri. A nurse and a ruling-party politician were killed in related tensions. In October, Kenya reported 8 cases and 2 deaths, and Nigeria confirmed 1 case evacuated to Switzerland, marking the outbreak as geographically widespread—the first in three African regions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱による死者数が5,000人を突破、WHOはアフリカ大陸規模での感染拡大を懸念
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%・死者5,000人超の大規模エボラ流行であり、ケニア・ナイジェリアへの国際的拡大や国外搬送例も確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し社会的関心も極めて高い。
triage.notes: 主たる発生地はコンゴ民主共和国（イツリ州含む）。ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへの拡大が報告されているが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent-wide spread mounts
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak has reached 5,026 deaths among 10,351 cases (case fatality just under 50%). The Bundibugyo strain has no vaccine or approved treatment; management centers on supportive care for dehydration, shock, and bacterial infections. Beginning mid-May, the outbreak has spread to 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, making it the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak in history. Authorities cite ongoing challenges with contact tracing and testing amid local scepticism. A nurse was killed responding to an alert, and a ruling-party politician was killed in September after advocating for health measures. Health workers have staged strikes over four months of unpaid wages, including a walkout at a treatment centre in Tchomia, Ituri, with officials noting fuel and resource shortages. In October, Kenya (8 cases, 2 deaths) and Nigeria (1 case evacuated to Switzerland) reported cases, extending the outbreak to three African regions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超え、大陸規模の感染拡大への懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: DRCでの大規模エボラ流行（死者5,000人超、致死率約50%）が複数州に拡大し、ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境伝播も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへの感染拡大が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ワクチン・承認治療法がない点、医療従事者の賃金未払いによるストライキ、住民の不信感による接触者追跡の困難など、流行制御上の深刻な課題が複数存在する。

article.articleHeadline: 今年流感季提前　多毒株活躍
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: This year's flu season starts earlier; multiple strains are active.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-31, China CDC’s latest influenza surveillance weekly report shows the autumn-winter flu season has begun with multiple strains circulating. Influenza A dominates, with A/H3N2 accounting for about 70% of positive samples and A/H1N1 about 30%. The season features co-circulation of several strains and an earlier outbreak rhythm. Cross-protection between strains is weak; after an A infection, individuals—especially children and the elderly—may still contract B. China’s high-activity period typically spans November to March, with optimal vaccination in September–October. Vaccine options include trivalent split vaccines and subunit vaccines for 6 months and older, and trivalent live attenuated vaccines for ages 3–17. Vaccines have demonstrated safety and efficacy across extensive clinical trials and post-marketing use.

triage.headline_ja: 今年の流感シーズンは早まり、複数の毒株が活発
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザの通常のサーベイランス報告であり、異常な重症度や国際的拡大リスクは示されていない。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザ（A型H3N2優勢、H1N1混在）の通常の流行開始を報告する記事で、ワクチン接種推奨情報が中心。危機性・異常性は認められない。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola suma más de cinco mil muertos en Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak has killed more than five thousand people in Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed infections, with 2,788 recoveries and 1,101 patients hospitalized or in isolation, according to INSP data through Oct 29. The outbreak, which began May 15 in the eastern DRC, has spread to additional provinces. Case fatality rate: 48.6%; contact tracing coverage: 84.5%. Importantly, about 80% of new cases come from outside the traced contact chains, signaling transmission from unknown sources and gaps in surveillance and testing. Health authorities urge intensified early detection, contact tracing, and safe, dignified burials to curb transmission. The situation remains challenging due to tracing and testing difficulties. Africa CDC notes the substantial share of cases arising outside known contact chains.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ出血熱の流行、死者5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.6%の大規模エボラ流行が複数州に拡大し、新規感染の約80%が接触者追跡網外から発生しており、国際的拡大・公衆衛生への深刻な影響が明確なためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 死者5,026人、感染者10,351人、致死率48.6%と非常に深刻。接触者追跡外からの新規感染が80%に上り、サーベイランスの隙間が示唆される。Africa CDCも懸念を表明しており、国際支援の必要性が高いと考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: Kisangani : 5 000 moustiquaires distribuées aux déplacés pour prévenir le paludisme
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kisangani: 5,000 mosquito nets distributed to the displaced to prevent malaria.
article.articleSummary: 5,000 insecticide-treated mosquito nets were distributed to displaced people in Kisangani's camps Kongakonga, Simisimi, and Lubunga on Oct 30, 2026, by Fondation La Vie en Famille in collaboration with SANRU, benefiting about 2,500 households in Kongakonga. Malaria remains a major public health issue in the Democratic Republic of Congo, especially threatening children under five, pregnant women, and those in precarious conditions. Some nets were misused for gardening or fishing, highlighting the need for proper use. Beneficiaries have lived in Kisangani since May 2023 after fleeing the Mbole-Lengola conflict and have asked to return home. Additional nets will be distributed based on need. SANRU reports alarmingly high malaria figures in Tshopo province, and the nets aim to protect communities from mosquito bites at night.

triage.headline_ja: キサンガニ:避難民にマラリア予防のための蚊帳5,000張を配布
triage.triage_reason: マラリアはDRCの既知の風土病であり、本記事は予防的な蚊帳配布という通常の公衆衛生活動を報じるもので、異常性・国際的拡大リスク・社会的関心の高まりは認められない。
triage.notes: 避難民キャンプでの風土病マラリア対策としての蚊帳配布に関する日常的な報道であり、新規の公衆衛生上の脅威を示すものではない。

article.articleHeadline: Sota ei ole Myanmarin ainoa kriisi - Tulvat, nälkä ja taudit koskettavat miljoonia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: War Is Not Myanmar's Only Crisis — Floods, Hunger and Diseases Are Affecting Millions.
article.articleSummary: Nearly four million people remain displaced within Myanmar amid the civil conflict as floods and disease surge. In Sagaing's Shwebo corridor, floods compound hunger, with over 470,000 affected by July monsoon rains per WHO. Malaria and dengue cases have risen, and cholera outbreaks have emerged across the country, including Yangon in August and in flood regions such as Rakhine’s Sittwe and the Ayeyarwady delta. The dual crises drive up food prices and transport costs as competing factions extract tolls at checkpoints from Mandalay north to Shwebo. Inflation and supply disruptions leave farming households impoverished; fertilizer prices have surged, with cascading effects on next planting season. The junta intensifies control, using checkpoints, AI-enabled surveillance, and coercive conscription—more than 100,000 people reportedly recruited, with families paying to avoid service. Yangon faces security fears amid widespread hardship.

triage.headline_ja: 戦争だけがミャンマーの危機ではない ― 洪水・飢餓・疾病が数百万人に影響
triage.triage_reason: 内戦と洪水が重なる中、コレラ・マラリア・デング熱が複数地域で拡大し、約400万人が避難民となっている人道危機であり、WHOも関与していることからWPRO基準に複数該当し社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 内戦下での洪水・飢餓・疾病の複合危機に関する記事。コレラ、マラリア、デング熱がヤンゴン、ラカイン州シットウェ、エーヤワディ・デルタなど複数地域で報告されており、WHOのデータも引用されている。疾病の重症度や死亡数などの詳細データは記事中に明示されていない。

article.articleHeadline: An Giang tăng cường phòng chống dịch tả lợn châu Phi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: An Giang strengthens prevention and control of African swine fever.
article.articleSummary: ASF outbreak in An Giang Province, Vietnam, as of 30 Oct 2026 affects 13 communes, with Giồng Riềng marking the first case on 1 Oct and Bình An reporting the latest positive on 30 Oct. Cumulative culled pigs reach 11,413, totaling 26,037 kg. Notable culls: An Bình, 14 pigs (338 kg); Bình An overall 36 pigs (1,016 kg); Ô Lâm, 56 pigs (2,641 kg) culled on 28 Oct. Thoại Sơn oversees about 955 pigs across 51 farms; on 19 Oct a farm had 35 deaths, and 28 were culled on 21 Oct; no new outbreaks there by 31 Oct. Pork markets (Mỹ Bình, Long Xuyên) continue to sell with veterinary seals, though demand is down. Province-wide pigs: 442,625 (98.4% of 2026 target), ~580 farms (188 pig farms, 180,283 pigs). Three rapid-response teams deployed; enhanced disinfection and PPE, with a 15 Oct directive to tighten controls at origin and transport hubs, supported by police and border forces, enforcing the 5 no principles.

triage.headline_ja: アンザン省がアフリカ豚熱の予防・対策を強化
triage.triage_reason: アフリカ豚熱（ASF）は豚のみに感染し人獣共通感染症ではないため、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響は認められず、国内の家畜対策レベルの事案である。
triage.notes: ASFは人への感染性がないため公衆衛生シグナルとしては見送り。畜産・貿易への経済的影響は地方当局レベルで対応中。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola outbreak deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent-wide spread mounts
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-10-31, Congo's Ebola outbreak caused 5,026 deaths among 10,351 cases, with 2,788 recoveries. Bundibugyo virus lacks a vaccine or specific therapy and cases have surged across 67 of 178 health zones in eight provinces, concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu, the epicenters reporting 9,782 confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths. The outbreak, declared mid-May, is the second deadliest in history after 2014–2016 West Africa’s 11,000 deaths. About 80% of new cases arise outside monitored contact chains; one-third of deaths occur outside treatment centers. In October, Kenya (8 cases, 2 deaths) and Nigeria (1 exported case to Switzerland) reported cases, signaling geographic spread beyond Congo. Health workers face strikes over unpaid wages and security threats, including attacks on facilities, amid conflict with armed groups (notably M23) complicating response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱、死者5,000人超え 大陸規模の拡散懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が複数国（ケニア、ナイジェリア経由スイス）に拡大しており、IHR基準の複数該当とWPRO基準の重症度・流行性・管理可能性すべてで懸念があるため。
triage.notes: ケニア、ナイジェリア、スイスでの症例も報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。主要な発生国はコンゴ民主共和国。武装勢力（M23）との紛争や医療従事者のストライキが対応を複雑化させており、ワクチンや特異的治療法が存在しないブンディブギョウイルスである点も深刻。

article.articleHeadline: تفاقم تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية: الوفيات تتجاوز 5 آلاف
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Worsening Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: deaths exceed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: DRC's Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo strain) has 10,351 confirmed cases and 5,026 deaths, as of 31 October 2026, with 1,101 active patients and 2,788 recoveries. The outbreak, officially declared 15 May after infections traced to February, may be undercounted due to undetected spread and weak health systems. It has spread across eight of 26 provinces, with many deaths outside treatment centers. This year’s surge is the second-largest globally, behind 2014–2016 West Africa. Transmission is by direct contact with infected people or fluids; symptoms include fever, diarrhea, and bleeding. No vaccine or specific treatment exists for Bundibugyo in this outbreak; two antivirals are in trials since July, and vaccines are being evaluated, including Ervebo, approved only for the Zaire strain. Imported/exported cases include Nigeria’s first case on Oct 20 (a Swiss woman who had been in Uganda), Kenya and Uganda cases, and a single European case in France (doctor).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の流行が悪化：死者5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行は死者5,000人超、感染1万人超と大規模で、ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダ・フランスへの越境拡大も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダ・フランスでの輸入症例が報告されているが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。主たる発生国はDRCのみ。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en el Congo ya es el segundo más mortífero de la historia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Congo is already the second deadliest in history.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, has reached 5,026 deaths and 10,351 cases since the outbreak was declared on May 15, with an INSP update through Oct 29 showing a 48.6% case-fatality rate. It is the second-deadliest Ebola episode on record and remains active beyond Congo’s borders, with linked cases in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria. East Congo, especially Ituri and North Kivu, bears the heaviest burden; transmission is complicated by armed conflict and limited health infrastructure. No vaccine or treatment is specifically approved for Bundibugyo; Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus vaccine) has no proven clinical efficacy against Bundibugyo, though a late-August vaccination campaign is underway. Recoveries total 2,788; 1,101 patients are hospitalized or in isolation. Approximately 80% of new infections occur outside established contact tracing, underscoring the need for rapid detection, contact tracing, isolation, and safe handling of patients and bodies.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱流行、史上2番目の致死数に
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.6%、5000人超の死者を出す大規模流行であり、国境を越えてウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの拡大、ワクチンの有効性未確認、紛争地での対応困難など、IHR基準・WPRO基準の多数に該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの関連症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。主要発生地はDRC（イトゥリ州・北キブ州）。

article.articleHeadline: Эпидемиолог назвал особенности лихорадки Зика
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: An epidemiologist described the features of Zika fever.
article.articleSummary: Zika fever is asymptomatic in about 80% of infections; approximately 20% manifest clinical features such as fever, rash, joint pain, and conjunctivitis. Onset typically occurs 3-14 days after infection and lasts about 2-7 days. In adults with normal immunity, the illness is usually mild and fatalities are rare. The major risk is for pregnant women, where infection can lead to fetal microcephaly or, less commonly, Guillain-Barré syndrome in the newborn. There is no specific antiviral treatment; management is supportive—rest, fluids, and analgesics/antipyretics—with uncomplicated cases resolving in about a week and no need for hospitalization. An imported case was reported in Moscow: a woman who had returned in September from Bali, Indonesia.

triage.headline_ja: 疫学者がジカ熱の特徴について解説
triage.triage_reason: ロシア(モスクワ)でバリ島(インドネシア)からの輸入例1件が報告された一般的な解説記事であり、新規の流行や異常事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はジカ熱の一般的な医学解説が中心で、インドネシア・バリ島はロシア人女性の渡航歴として言及されているのみであり、現地での流行発生を示す情報ではない。ロシアは対象国リストに含まれないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: 민주콩고 에볼라 사망 5천명 넘어...확진자 절반 사망
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000, with half of the confirmed cases dying.
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 31, 2026, Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths with infections over 10,000. Cumulative lab-confirmed cases are 10,351 and deaths 5,026; recoveries total 2,788. Declared May 15, the outbreak has persisted for 168 days. The causative strain is Bundibugyo ebolavirus; there is no approved vaccine or specific antiviral for this outbreak, and large portions of affected areas are under rebel control, hindering on-the-ground response. Community distrust toward healthcare workers, poor working conditions, and weak health infrastructure further hamper containment. WHO notes about one-third of deaths occurred without medical care and often before testing. The outbreak’s transmission rate in DRC is faster than past outbreaks, and globally Nigeria has reported West Africa cases while Kenya and Uganda have confirmed related infections. Authorities are strengthening early case finding, isolation, contact tracing, and cross-border surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: 民主コンゴのエボラ死者5000人超...確診者の半数が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%の大規模エボラ流行で死者5000人超、感染者1万人超。反政府勢力支配地域での対応困難、国境を越えた拡大（ナイジェリア、ケニア、ウガンダ）が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大なシグナル。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでの流行が主題であり、ナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダは関連症例の報告先として言及されているのみで、対象国リストにも含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。承認済みワクチン・抗ウイルス薬がない点、反政府勢力による支配地域でのアクセス制限、コミュニティの不信感等、対応が極めて困難な状況が強調されている。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola death toll tops 5,000 as outbreak spreads
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has killed 5,026 people and infected 10,351 (confirmed and suspected) cases, according to the Congolese Ministry of Health and AP reporting on 2026-10-31. The fatality rate is about 50%. The outbreak began in May and has spread across several provinces. Efforts to contain it are hampered by armed conflict, public distrust, shortages of resources, and disruptions to health services. The virus has also crossed borders, with cases reported in other African countries, raising concerns about further transmission. Ongoing monitoring and containment remain critical as authorities work to improve laboratory confirmation, contact tracing, and community engagement to stem transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超え、感染拡大が続く
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%、死者5,000人超、国境を越えた拡大が報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 記事は他のアフリカ諸国への越境を言及しているが、対象国リストに含まれる具体的な国名は明示されていないため、DRCのみを記載。武力紛争や医療体制の崩壊により封じ込めが困難な状況が続いている。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en la República Democrática del Congo deja más de 5.000 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has left more than 5,000 dead.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,000 deaths and more than 10,000 cases since it was declared in May. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain has no approved vaccines or treatments. The epidemic spans eight of the 26 provinces, with many deaths reported outside treatment centers. Kinshasa indicates confirmed cases exceed 10,000 as of last Tuesday. This outbreak ranks as the second-largest globally, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that produced about 28,600 cases and 11,000 deaths. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids, causing severe hemorrhagic fever symptoms. Containment faces challenges including delays in case detection, ongoing conflict, and weak health services, yet authorities continue intensified efforts to curb spread.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク、死者5,000人超に
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱（Bundibugyo株）が8州に拡大し死者5,000人超・症例1万人超と深刻化、承認済みワクチン・治療薬がなく国際的拡大・公衆衛生上の重大リスクがあるためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: Bundibugyoエボラウイルス株による大規模アウトブレイクで、史上2番目の規模とされる。紛争や医療体制の脆弱性が封じ込めを困難にしている。アンゴラは記事サマリー中で感染拡大の主題として言及されていないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Death toll from Ebola outbreak in DR Congo surpasses 5,000
article.articleSummary: Death toll surpasses 5,000 from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with cumulative cases reaching 10,351 as of the Health Ministry update on 2026-10-31. Declared in mid-May, this is the country’s largest Ebola outbreak on record and the second-largest globally after West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic. The eight affected provinces are Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Bas-Uele, Tshopo, South Ubangi, and North Ubangi. Africa CDC on 2026-10-30 urged stronger protections for frontline health workers after two young Congolese doctors died in North Kivu and Ituri. Persistent weaknesses in early detection and contact tracing remain main obstacles to stopping transmission; only about 12% of confirmed cases have been identified among previously known contacts, with many deaths occurring in communities.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクによる死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラアウトブレイクが継続しており、死者5,000人・症例1万人超、8州に拡大し封じ込めも機能不全であるためIHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: Africa CDCが医療従事者保護強化を要請、接触者追跡の捕捉率が約12%と低く、コミュニティでの死亡例が多発。国際的拡大の報告は記事内になし。

article.articleHeadline: Новый штамм коронавируса может добраться до России -- ВОЗ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A new strain of coronavirus could reach Russia — WHO.
article.articleSummary: The World Health Organization warns of rising global spread risk for the new coronavirus strain PJ.2.1. First detected in May 2026 in Ontario, Canada, PJ.2.1 has since spread to several continents, including Canada, the United States, and Europe. Health authorities say ongoing human movement increases the chance of introductions into new countries, including Russia. There are no clinical data showing a more severe illness with PJ.2.1 versus other recent SARS-CoV-2 variants; it has not been linked to higher rates of pneumonia, respiratory failure, or deaths. The main at‑risk group is people aged 60 and older. In Russia, a resident from Khabarovsk on holiday in Pattaya, Thailand, experienced a coma; preliminary diagnosis suggests infection with the new PJ.2.1 variant identified in the Kingdom of Thailand. The traveler, who went with his wife and two children, developed fever, seizures, and hallucinations days after arrival and remains comatose in a state hospital. His kidney donation to his daughter 16 years ago complicates his infection response.

triage.headline_ja: 新型コロナウイルスの新変異株がロシアに到達する可能性 — WHO
triage.triage_reason: WHOが新変異株PJ.2.1の世界的拡大リスクを警告しているが、重症化を示す臨床データはなく、タイでの重症例も腎移植による免疫抑制が交絡因子であるため、現時点では情報不足として経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 新変異株PJ.2.1は2026年5月にカナダ・オンタリオ州で初検出され、複数大陸に拡大中とされるが、重症化エビデンスは確認されていない。記事で言及される重症例（ロシア人旅行者）はタイのパタヤで発症し、過去の腎移植による免疫抑制が病状に影響している可能性がある。対象国はタイのみ該当（カナダ・米国・ロシアは対象国リスト外）。続報でのWHO評価や各国対応を注視すべき。

article.articleHeadline: उदयपुर : शोध में खुलासा : चूहों-छछूंदरों पर पल रहा जानलेवा माइट, हर बुखार डेंगू नहीं, हो सकता है स्क्रब टाइफस | Scrub Typhus Research Udaipur Chigger Mites Rodents
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Udaipur: Revelation in research: A deadly mite thriving on rats and mice; not every fever is dengue; it could be scrub typhus.
article.articleSummary: Scrub typhus, caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi, is a rising fever cause in Udaipur, Rajasthan, not just dengue or malaria. A field study by Mohanlal Sukhadia University’s Public Health Entomology Lab (June 2024–May 2026) across eight talukas—Girva, Mavli, Gogunda, Jhadol, Kherwara, Kotra, Rishabhdev, Bhinder—trapped 1,440 small mammals; 512 traps were positive. Of these, 149 hosts carried chigger mites, yielding 9,854 mites across eight genera. Leptotrombidium deliense, the principal vector, numbered 1,904 mites (19.3%). Domestic rats (Bandicota indica and Bandicota bengalensis) were major reservoirs: 137 rats examined, 58 infested; 4,565 mites on rats; average burden 78.7 mites per rat; mice none; 46% of mites were on rats. Seasonal risk rose from pre-monsoon (115 mites, 20% infected) to post-monsoon (204 mites, 34.8% infected), with all eight species active post-monsoon. Rajasthan NHM data show rising scrub typhus cases nationwide: 2,733 in 2023; 3,461 in 2024; Udaipur district counts: 2019–776; 2023–543; 2024–611; 2025–231.

triage.headline_ja: ウダイプル：研究で判明、ネズミ類に潜む危険なダニ――すべての発熱がデング熱とは限らず、スクラブチフスの可能性も
triage.triage_reason: 学術的な研究報告であり、ツツガムシ病症例数の増加傾向が示されているが、急性のアウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急対応を示す情報はないため、経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 記事はウダイプル(ラジャスタン州)における大学研究機関によるベクター・リザーバー調査の結果報告であり、季節的・経年的な症例数データも含むが、具体的な急増アウトブレイクの報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie de choléra à Mbandaka fait 14 morts et 129 cas dans deux
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The cholera epidemic in Mbandaka has caused 14 deaths and 129 cases in two.
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak continues in Mbandaka, Equateur Province, DRC, with 129 cases and 14 deaths (68 recoveries) reported in days across the Wangata and Bolenge health zones. Bolenge remains the most affected with 104 cases since the surge began; other patients are under care in Wangata. Of the 14 fatalities, most occurred in the community before admission to treatment centers. By 31 October 2026, authorities have strengthened port controls in Mbandaka and Bolenge and intensified public awareness campaigns. The outbreak is linked to recent arrivals on boats from Kinshasa, where more than 800 passengers were counted and about 100 showed symptoms compatible with cholera. Preventive measures urged include regular handwashing with soap, treating or boiling drinking water, and adherence to other health authority recommendations.

triage.headline_ja: ムバンダカのコレラ流行、2地区で129症例・14死亡
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国ムバンダカで致死率約11%のコレラ流行が継続しており、キンシャサからの船舶乗客を介した拡大リスクがあるため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: キンシャサからムバンダカへの船舶移動者（800人超、うち約100人が症状あり）が感染拡大源とされ、港湾管理強化と啓発活動が実施されている。国際的拡大や貿易制限の明確な言及はないが、国内での感染拡大リスクは高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en Ituri : 2.081 personnes vaccinées pour évaluer l'efficacité d'Ervebo - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Ituri: 2,081 people vaccinated to evaluate the efficacy of Ervebo - ACP
article.articleSummary: In Ituri, northeast Democratic Republic of the Congo, an ongoing Ervebo Ebola vaccine efficacy study against Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) vaccinated 2,081 people as of 29 October 2026, with MSF support. Cumulatively, 2,081 recipients include 865 women and 1,216 men, among whom 23 pregnant and 62 lactating women are recorded. On 29 October alone, 112 people were vaccinated (50 women, 62 men), including five lactating women; no pregnant woman was vaccinated that day. Post-vaccination adverse events following immunization (AEFI) amounted to two non-severe cases on 29 October, with no severe events reported; overall counts reach 34 non-severe and five severe AEFIs since activities began. This continued research is a key component of the Ebola response in Ituri, emphasizing prevention and protection for populations at risk.

triage.headline_ja: イツリ州でのエボラ：Erveboワクチンの有効性評価のため2,081人が接種
triage.triage_reason: DRCイツリ州でのエボラ(BDBV)ワクチン有効性研究の進捗報告であり、新規アウトブレイクの急拡大を示す情報ではないが、継続中のエボラ対応として経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はワクチン接種活動の進捗報告であり、新規感染者数や死亡者数など疾患の深刻度に関する直接的情報は含まれていない。既存のエボラ対応（MSF支援）の一環として継続監視が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يحصد أكثر من 5 آلاف وفاة في الكونغو الديمقراطية وسط اتساع رقعة التفشي
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola claims more than 5,000 lives in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as the outbreak widens.
article.articleSummary: Deaths from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000, with more than 10,000 infections since the current wave began in May, as of 31 October 2026. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain has spread to eight of the country’s 26 provinces, with deaths occurring outside facilities. Late detection, weak health systems, and community resistance are cited as key drivers amid fears of further spread. Infections have also been reported in Nigeria, Kenya, and Uganda, widening cross-border concerns. No licensed vaccine or specific treatment exists for this strain; containment relies on isolating patients, tracing contacts, and providing supportive care. Symptoms include sudden high fever, severe headache, muscle pains, fatigue, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, and possible bleeding. The strain was first identified in Uganda (2007–2008) and re-emerged in DRC in 2012. The WHO has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、コンゴ民主共和国で死者5000人超、アウトブレイクが拡大
triage.triage_reason: 死者5000人超・感染1万人超の大規模アウトブレイクで、国境を越えてナイジェリア・ケニア・ウガンダにも感染拡大、WHOがPHEIC宣言しておりIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア、ケニア、ウガンダへの感染拡大が報じられているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。WHOのPHEIC宣言済みでフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو: حصيلة وفيات فيروس إيبولا تتجاوز 5000 حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo: Ebola virus death toll surpasses 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease continues to claim lives in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with authorities reporting 5,026 deaths and 10,351 infections since the outbreak was detected in mid-May. Of the total, 1,101 people are currently under treatment or in isolation, and 2,788 have recovered. As of 2026-10-31, officials caution the true toll may be higher, as transmission has been suspected since February, months before the official outbreak announcement on May 15. Ebola spreads through direct contact with an infected person or their bodily fluids and can cause fever, diarrhea, and bleeding. The report underscores ongoing transmission and uncertainty about the outbreak’s full scope.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ：エボラ出血熱による死者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ出血熱の死者が5000人超、感染者1万人超の大規模アウトブレイクであり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクがあるためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 死者5026人、感染者10351人という大規模アウトブレイク。2月から伝播が疑われていたにも関わらず公式発表が5月15日と遅れた点、実際の被害規模が公式統計より大きい可能性が指摘されている点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية تعلن تجاوز وفيات إيبولا 5 آلاف حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo announces that Ebola deaths have surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports Ebola deaths surpassing 5,000 since the latest outbreak was detected in mid-May 2026. Authorities say 5,026 deaths have been confirmed, with 10,351 total cases reported; about 1,101 people remain in treatment or under isolation, and 2,788 have recovered. Officials warn the true toll may be higher, as the virus may not have been detected during its spread since February at least, preceding the outbreak’s official announcement on May 15. Ebola is a deadly disease transmitted via direct contact with infected patients or their body fluids, with symptoms including high fever, diarrhea, and bleeding. The update underscores ongoing transmission and potential under-detection in affected areas of the DRC, underscoring the need for continued surveillance and public health measures.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ死者数が5000人を超えたと発表
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱の大規模アウトブレイクで死者5000人超・症例1万人超、過小検出や継続的な感染拡大の懸念があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: 2月以降の未検出感染の可能性が指摘されており、実際の流行規模が公式統計を上回る恐れがある。継続的な監視体制強化が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak: Congo's Ebola death toll crosses 5,000 as outbreak spreads in other African countries
article.articleSummary: Congolese Ebola outbreak has killed 5,026 people, with 10,351 infections, a case-fatality rate near 50%, according to the Congolese Ministry of Health. The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, was declared in mid-May and has since challenged containment while spreading beyond Congo's borders to other African countries. It stands as the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak in history, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that killed about 11,000 across multiple countries. The latest government data underscore ongoing transmission and the authorities' difficulty in containing the outbreak amid regional spread. Counts come from the Congolese Ministry of Health as the latest update.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行：コンゴのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超え、他のアフリカ諸国にも拡大
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%、死者5,000人超、感染者10,351人に達し、国境を越えて他のアフリカ諸国に拡大している重大なエボラ流行であり、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 記事ではコンゴ発のアウトブレイクが『他のアフリカ諸国』に拡大したと記載されているが、具体的な対象国名（アンゴラ等）の確定は本文からは不明。アンゴラはBluedotの発生地域に含まれるが対象国リストに無いため除外。歴代2番目の規模のエボラ流行として重大性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola en el Congo: más de 5.000 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Congo: more than 5,000 dead.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to drive high mortality, with 10,351 confirmed cases and 5,026 deaths as of October 29, according to INSP. Declared May 15 in eastern DRC, the outbreak has spread to additional provinces, posing a major health-system challenge. Recoveries total 2,788; 1,101 patients remain hospitalized or in isolation. Contact tracing stands at 84.5%, but about 80% of new cases arise from people not in tracing chains, hindering early detection and enabling transmission in urban and rural communities. The INSP urges strengthened prevention and response measures, including early detection, expanded contact tracing, and dignified, safe burials to curb spread. Africa CDC and local authorities maintain ongoing monitoring to reduce new infections, highlighting enhanced surveillance and community engagement as essential to containing the epidemic.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱：死者5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ出血熱の大規模流行が継続し死者5,000人超・致死率も高く、接触追跡の捕捉率低下によるヒト-ヒト感染拡大リスクが高いためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 新規症例の約80%が接触追跡網外から発生しており、感染拡大の制御が困難な状況。Africa CDCが監視を継続中。

article.articleHeadline: Vì sao ca não mô cầu có thể xuất hiện rải rác trong cùng khu vực?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Why can meningococcal meningitis cases appear scattered within the same area?
article.articleSummary: Ca Mau Province, Vietnam, reports two meningococcal meningitis deaths in Sông Đốc commune, aged 33 and 46. In October 2026, the province recorded 8 meningococcal disease cases this year, with 3 fatalities; as of 30 October, no epidemiologic link between the two deaths has been established, and source investigations continue. Neisseria meningitidis colonizes the nasopharynx of healthy individuals and spreads via respiratory droplets up to about 2 meters and through close contact, with higher risk in households, schools, dormitories and other group settings. Invasive disease can progress within 24 hours, presenting with sudden high fever, severe headache, vomiting, neck stiffness, altered consciousness, seizures, and purpuric non-blanching rash. Early antibiotic treatment is essential; close contacts may require prophylaxis if indicated. Vaccines available in Vietnam cover serogroups A, B, C, W, X, Y; group B, BC (B and C), and quadrivalent (A, C, Y, W) formulations are advised based on age, exposure, and vaccination history.

triage.headline_ja: なぜ髄膜炎菌性髄膜炎の症例は同一地域内で散発的に発生するのか？
triage.triage_reason: ベトナム・カマウ省で髄膜炎菌感染症による死亡例（本年8例中3例死亡）が報告され、重症度が高くヒト-ヒト感染のリスクがあるため、WPRO基準の複数該当と行政・住民の関心の高まりからフルリスク評価への移行が妥当と判断。
triage.notes: 記事は啓発的内容だが、カマウ省で実際に2名の死亡例（33歳・46歳）が発生し、疫学的関連性の調査が継続中である点から、局地的クラスターとして今後の動向を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Équateur : 129 cas de choléra et 14 décès enregistrés à Mbandaka(Bilan officiel) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Équateur: 129 cholera cases and 14 deaths recorded in Mbandaka (Official tally) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak in Mbandaka, Equateur province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in Bolenge and Wangata health zones. As of Oct 31, 2026, 129 cases have been reported, with 14 deaths and 68 recoveries. Community deaths: 11; 3 deaths occurred in cholera treatment centers at Bolenge and Wangata. Bolenge remains the epicenter with 104 cases; 77 patients are under care, and 16 have been transferred to Wangata. Total recoveries in the province: 68 (47 at Bolenge CTC, 21 at Wangata). Seven new admissions were recorded in these centers. Suspicious origin linked to river vessels from Maluku and Kingabwa (Kinshasa) bound for Kisangani, Mbandaka, and Basankusu; about 100 of roughly 800 passengers developed symptoms. Response intensified: strategic meeting chaired by Mayor Yves Balo; reinforced handwashing, no handshakes, drinking-water treatment, and disinfection of motorcycle taxis; stricter port controls and isolation at key docking points such as Iyonda port and the former ONATRA site.

triage.headline_ja: 赤道州：ムバンダカで129件のコレラ症例と14人の死亡を記録(公式集計) - ACP
triage.triage_reason: DRCコンゴ赤道州ムバンダカでコレラ集団発生が拡大中（129症例・14死亡、CFR約11%）、河川船舶を介した複数都市への感染拡大リスクがあり、行政レベルの対応強化も確認されるためフルリスク評価が妥当。
triage.notes: 発生地域に『Republic of Ecuador』が含まれるが、これは誤認識（DRC国内の『Province de l'Équateur／赤道州』と地理的に混同されたもの）であり、実際の発生国はDRCのみ。コレラはDRCで風土病的だが、本件は河川船舶（マルク～キサンガニ・ムバンダカ・バサンクス間）を介した感染拡大の兆候があり注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Prefeitura de Porto Velho aprimora estratégias de identificação e tratamento da tuberculose
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Porto Velho City Hall Improves TB Identification and Treatment Strategies.
article.articleSummary: TB control training in Porto Velho, Brazil strengthens identification and treatment continuity for tuberculosis among people experiencing social vulnerability, especially those living on the streets. Led by the Municipal Health Secretariat (Semusa) and the Division of Epidemiological Surveillance (DVE) through the Municipal TB Control Program, in partnership with Associação Beradeiro, the training targets staff from the Consultório na Rua and Centro POP. It emphasizes early recognition of respiratory symptoms, active case finding, and building trust to sustain patients in care. The integrated approach with health and social services aims to bring TB services to where vulnerable individuals are, improve follow-up, and identify suspected cases. Municipal officials underscored data-driven planning (Sandra Cardoso) and addressing treatment interruption (Ivonete Ferreira) as critical to expanding TB care in Porto Velho.

triage.headline_ja: ポルト・ヴェーリョ市役所、結核の発見・治療戦略を強化
triage.triage_reason: 通常の結核対策プログラム強化に関する行政報道であり、異常な集団発生や急激な公衆衛生上の脅威を示す内容ではない。
triage.notes: 脆弱な社会層（路上生活者等）を対象とした結核対策の地域保健プログラム強化に関する通常の行政報道。

article.articleHeadline: Casos de Mpox aumentam 7 vezes no Rio em dois meses; capital está sem vacina contra a doença
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mpox cases have increased sevenfold in Rio de Janeiro in two months; the capital has no vaccine against the disease.
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) cases rise in Rio de Janeiro. In the capital over the last two months, more than 70 infections—sevenfold the prior year’s figure. September had 45 cases, the highest in three years; by October, 29 more confirmations were reported. Ten people are hospitalized at Instituto Nacional de Infectologia Evandro Chagas (Fiocruz) in Manguinhos, North Zone. Transmission is mainly via direct contact with lesions, bodily fluids, and secretions; contaminated objects can also spread the virus. Most patients have mild to moderate illness, but severe complications and death are possible. A vaccine exists, but Rio de Janeiro city currently has no doses; vaccination is prioritized for specific groups by the Health Ministry. Statewide, 211 confirmed cases in 2026, up from 119 in 2025, with 119 suspected cases under investigation. Authorities urge symptomatic individuals to seek medical evaluation.

article.articleHeadline: Actualité | L'épidémie d'Ebola a fait plus de 5 000 morts | mediacongo.net
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: News | The Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,000 people | mediacongo.net
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has killed over 5,000 people and infected about 10,000 since May, marking the largest outbreak on record in the DRC. Deaths have risen by roughly 1,000 since early October. There is no approved treatment or vaccine for the rare Bundibugyo strain driving this epidemic. Fears of regional spread persist, with Nigeria reporting a case—the fourth African country after the DRC, Kenya, and Uganda. Eight of the DRC’s 26 provinces have reported cases, and response efforts are hampered by attacks on health workers, including the killing of a nurse and injury to another health professional by armed youths. Globally, this outbreak is the second-largest ever, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that caused about 11,000 deaths and 28,000 cases in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.

article.articleHeadline: Des cliniques pour le suivi des guéris d'Ebola opérationnelles en Ituri - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Clinics for the follow-up of Ebola survivors operating in Ituri - ACP
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, specialized clinics for the follow-up of Ebola survivors operate in Bunia, the capital of Ituri Province in northeastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Dubbed 'survivors clinics,' they provide regular medical monitoring for people who recovered from Ebola, with free, appointment-based consultations and treatments to ensure tailored care, including non-Ebola sequelae. The program covers all costs, and even reimburses travel expenses for each visit to encourage consistent attendance. This initiative seeks to deliver continuous medical support, prevent health complications, and ease survivors’ reintegration into the community. Plans include rehabilitating additional health zones to expand access. Keywords: Ebola survivors, Bunia, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo, free care, follow-up, reintegration.

article.articleHeadline: HCM City steps up hand, foot and mouth disease prevention as cases exceed 44,000
article.articleSummary: Ho Chi Minh City has recorded more than 44,000 hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) cases and five deaths this year, with over 1,600 outbreaks, amid circulation of Enterovirus 71 (EV71) linked to severe complications in young children. A citywide campaign through 2026 aims to curb HFMD and dengue, coordinating actions among authorities, healthcare facilities and schools to reduce transmission and enable early detection. The HCMC Centre for Disease Control ordered kindergartens, childcare groups and paediatric vaccination facilities to disinfect at least weekly, with more frequent cleaning during outbreaks, and to monitor children's health daily and promptly report suspected cases. Parents should keep infected children at home and maintain hygiene, including handwashing and cleaning toys and surfaces. Dengue remains high with over 42,500 cases and 11 deaths; households are urged to remove stagnant water to reduce mosquito breeding.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deaths from the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000, according to data from the Ministry of Health.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused 5,026 deaths among 10,351 infections, with 2,788 recoveries. The outbreak, declared mid-May, has spread to 67 health zones across eight provinces. Kenya reports eight cases and two deaths; Nigeria has a single imported case evacuated to Switzerland; Uganda had prior cases. article.articleHeadline: 流感疫情上升，疫苗怎么打？您关心的问题一次说清
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza outbreak on the rise; how to get vaccinated? All your questions answered at once.
article.articleSummary: Week 42 surveillance shows influenza activity in Guangxi higher than same period last year, signaling outbreak risk for 2026–2027 season. Annual vaccination remains the most cost-effective protection against flu, reducing severe disease and complications. Influenza viruses evolve yearly, and protective antibodies fade after about 6–8 months, so vaccination should occur before each season. This year, rural Guangxi runs the 'one old, one young' program, offering free one-dose trivalent split-virion influenza vaccine covering influenza A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and B Victoria lineage to seniors 65+ and students; others may pay out-of-pocket, with insurance accounts usable at designated centers. Switch to trivalent vaccines aligns with WHO guidance removing Yamagata B lineage (no circulation since 2020); domestic vaccines have followed suit. Post-vaccination flu-like symptoms are usually due to other viruses, the need for ~2 weeks to develop protection, or preexisting infections. Vaccination sites include community health centers; bookings via the Guangxi CDC WeChat vaccination service.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola ultrapassa 5 mil mortes no Congo e atinge letalidade próxima de 50%
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola surpasses 5,000 deaths in the Congo and reaches a case-fatality rate near 50%.
article.articleSummary: DRC Ebola outbreak tallies: 5,026 deaths among 10,351 infections; 2,788 recoveries; case-fatality rate ~50%. Caused by Ebola Bundibugyo virus, declared mid-May, it is the second-deadliest outbreak, after the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. The outbreak spans 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, with the east-heavy Ituri and North Kivu provinces reporting 9,782 confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths. One-third of fatalities occurred without access to care; Africa CDC notes about 80% of new cases are outside monitored contact chains. Conflict, population resistance, and wage strikes hinder response; a treatment center in Tchomia (Ituri) paused operations for four months with five confirmed, ten suspected cases. Cross-border transmission includes Kenya (8 infections, 2 deaths) and Nigeria; a Nigerian patient was moved to Switzerland. Uganda had cases earlier. Bundibugyo differs from Zaire, and there is no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo; care is supportive.

article.articleHeadline: Saudi Arabia imposes Ebola-related travel bans on Kenya as countries tighten controls
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in East Africa is driving tighter border controls. Kenya has reported nine cases since an initial import about a month earlier. Saudi Arabia imposed entry restrictions on travellers from Kenya, suspended Saudi visas for Kenyans, and barred entry for those arriving via third countries who have spent time in Kenya within the past 21 days; authorities say measures aim to reduce transmission and that the public health situation is stable. The steps follow June restrictions on the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan. El Salvador likewise barred entry for travelers from Kenya and eight African countries (Angola, Burundi, Ethiopia, Central African Republic, DRC, Rwanda, Uganda), based on travel history rather than nationality. The United States raised Kenya to Level 3 travel advisory on 19 October; South Korea added Kenya to enhanced Ebola-focused quarantine from 20 October, while other countries tightened screening rather than bans.

article.articleHeadline: Saúde orienta sobre prevenção da dengue no período sazonal da doença
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health authorities advise on dengue prevention during the dengue season.
article.articleSummary: Dengue prevention is intensified in Maceió, Brazil, as October–November are strategic to curb Aedes aegypti proliferation ahead of peak transmission (January–May). The Municipal Health Secretariat of Maceió (SMS), via the Vector-borne and Venomous Animals Diseases Department (GDTVAP), conducts house visits to eliminate breeding sites, educate residents, and identify areas needing intensified control. Actions focus on reducing mosquito habitats in containers, water tanks, tires, and improperly discarded waste. Using epidemiological and entomological data, authorities define priority zones to allocate field teams and tailor interventions. Despite a reduction in cases in 2026, with 2,456 accumulated dengue cases by the 36th epidemiological week compared with 3,338 at the same point in 2025 (InfoDengue), preventive measures remain essential to sustain control. Community cooperation year-round is critical.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola fuera de control en el Congo: más de 5.000 muertos y una epidemia que ya cruzó fronteras
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Out of Control in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: More Than 5,000 Dead and an Epidemic That Has Already Crossed Borders.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared May 15, 2026, has reached 5,026 deaths and 10,351 confirmed infections as of Oct 30, 2026, with a case fatality near 49%. It is the deadliest outbreak in the DRC and the second most lethal globally, driven by the Bundibugyo Ebola variant, for which no approved vaccines or specific treatments exist. Eight of 26 provinces are affected, especially Ituri and North Kivu. Transmission occurs via direct contact with blood, secretions, and contaminated materials; many infections occur outside identified contact chains. Ongoing challenges include armed conflict in eastern DRC, attacks on health workers, and resource shortages. The outbreak has crossed borders to Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria; US and European authorities monitor potential international spread. Symptoms include fever, weakness, muscle pain, vomiting, and diarrhea; severe cases involve hemorrhage and organ failure. Early detection, isolation, and contact tracing remain essential.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola death toll in DR Congo surpasses 5,000 as outbreak spreads across eight provinces
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 5,000 people and infected 10,351 since mid-May, per the Health Ministry update on 2026-10-31. The outbreak spans eight provinces — Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Bas-Uele, Tshopo, South Ubangi and North Ubangi — and is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak on record in the DRC, and the second-largest globally after 2014–2016 West Africa. The Africa CDC urged stronger measures to protect frontline health workers after the deaths of two young Congolese doctors in North Kivu and Ituri this week. Officials cite persistent weaknesses in early detection and contact tracing, with only about 12% of confirmed cases identified among known contacts, and many infections occurring in communities, hindering containment.

The crisis is driven by the rare Bundibugyo variant (Bundibugyo ebolavirus), which initially escaped standard diagnostic tests. article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deaths from the Ebola outbreak in the DRC exceed 5,000, according to data from the Ministry of Health.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has resulted in 5,026 deaths among 10,351 infections with 2,788 recoveries, per Ministry of Health data published October 31 and cited by the Associated Press. The outbreak has spread to 67 health zones across eight provinces; Kenya reports eight cases and two deaths, while Nigeria has one confirmed case evacuated to Switzerland. Declared in mid-May, there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment; care is supportive and symptom-based. Approximately 80% of new cases originate from unmonitored contact chains, and about one-third of deaths occur before patients reach treatment centers. Conflict with armed groups (including M23) and strikes over unpaid salaries have hampered response, with treatment facilities like Tchomia in Ituri affected. Uganda has had prior cases; this outbreak is now recorded in three African regions.

triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ大規模流行が国際的に拡大（ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへの症例波及）しており、IHR基準の複数該当とWHO通知相当の重大性を有するためフルRRAに進むべき。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイス・ウガンダへの症例波及が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。DRCが主要発生国であり対象国リストに該当する。武装勢力との紛争や医療従事者ストライキが対応を妨げており、承認済みワクチン・治療法が存在しない点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: Peste 5.000 de oameni au murit de Ebola în Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 people have died of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: More than 5,000 people have died from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo as of October 31, 2026, government data show. The outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain, for which no approved treatments or vaccines exist, and eight of the country’s 26 provinces have been affected, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centers. This is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that infected about 28,600 and killed over 11,000 in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. The epidemic’s geographic reach now extends beyond DRC: Nigeria has reported a case—the fourth African country to do so—while Kenya and Uganda have confirmed cases; a Swiss citizen diagnosed in Nigeria was evacuated to Switzerland. Kenya reported a second death; lack of approved Bundibugyo-specific therapies complicates containment.

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola en el Congo supera los 5.000 muertos y ya es el segundo más letal de la historia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths and is already the second deadliest in history.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has surpassed 5,000 deaths, the second deadliest globally. As of October 29, 2026, INSP reports 10,351 confirmed infections and 5,026 deaths; 2,788 recovered; 1,101 hospitalized or in isolation. Case fatality rate 48.6%; contact tracing 84.5%. The epidemic spans eight provinces and 67 of 178 health zones. Ituri province (east, epicenter) concentrates 71.4% of confirmed cases, with 36.4% of new cases in Ituri and 58.4% in North Kivu. Bundibugyo strain lacks specific therapy; two vaccines are in Phase 1 trials, and Ervebo vaccination began in late August in DRC, designed for Zaire but showing cross-protection in animals. AU and WHO urge coordinated action; about a third of deaths occur outside treatment centers. The outbreak has spread to Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria; Uganda reported 20 infections (15 imported, 2 deaths). Border cases detected; travel bans in place. Transmission via bodily fluids; incubation 2–21 days.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola ultrapassa 5 mil mortes no Congo e atinge letalidade próxima de 50%
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola surpasses 5,000 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and reaches a case-fatality rate of around 50%.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo species) has caused 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed infections, with 2,788 recoveries and a case‑fatality rate around 50%. Declared in mid‑May, the outbreak spans 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, with the eastern provinces of Ituri and North Kivu accounting for the bulk (9,782 confirmed cases, 4,792 deaths). Cross‑border transmission has reached Kenya (8 infections, 2 deaths), Nigeria (1 confirmed case transferred to Switzerland), and Uganda. There is currently no vaccine or approved targeted therapy for Bundibugyo Ebola; care is supportive. Challenges include limited contact tracing (≈80% of new cases outside monitored chains), many deaths occurring before treatment, ongoing armed conflict, public resistance to measures, and unpaid health workers. Bundibugyo was first identified in 2007 in Uganda.
