article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Congo: dodental loopt op tot boven de 5000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: death toll rises to over 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo totals 10,351 reported cases and 5,026 deaths, with about 2,700 recoveries, per the Congolese Ministry of Health (mortality ~50%). By Oct 29, the ECDC tallied 10,274 cases and 4,992 deaths. Declared May 15, the outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, for which no approved vaccine or medicine exists. Eight of 26 provinces are affected, with the epicenter in Ituri and North Kivu, totaling 9,782 cases and 4,792 deaths. WHO recorded 50–80 new cases daily by late October; Africa CDC says roughly 80% of new cases arise outside known contact chains. Uganda reports 20 cases and 2 deaths; Kenya 9 cases and 2 deaths; Nigeria confirmed a first case on Oct 20. The US will restrict travelers who have been in Congo within the prior 21 days starting Nov 3. Ervebo vaccine trials began in Bunia on Oct 23; Oxford and Moderna candidates to be tested. The UN sought $1.1 billion; the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak killed over 11,000, making Congo’s outbreak the second-largest on record.

triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%の大規模アウトブレイクが8州に拡大し、近隣国（ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリア）への国際的拡大と米国の渡航制限措置が確認されており、IHR基準を複数満たす。

article.articleHeadline: وفيات إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية تتجاوز 5 آلاف
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed 5,026 people out of 10,351 laboratory-confirmed cases, a fatality rate of about 50%, as of 31 October 2026. The ongoing outbreak continues to challenge containment efforts. Health authorities note that about one-third of deaths occurred outside treatment centers before Ebola testing, a gap that sustains community transmission and hampers direct follow-up by health workers. The data from the Ministry of Health underscores the disease's high lethality and rapid progression, highlighting gaps in surveillance and access to care. WHO officials, including Dr. Patrick Otim, warn that the situation is a grim indicator affecting families and communities and underscores the urgent need to strengthen case finding, isolation measures, and treatment access within the country.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Half of the people who contracted Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have died, official data reveal.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues, with official government data reporting more than 10,000 infections and over 5,000 deaths. The eastern DRC remains the epicenter, where insecurity and attacks on health workers hamper response to the Bundibugyo strain, which triggered the outbreak and for which there is no approved vaccine. The ongoing transmission has raised concerns about regional spread, with the Bundibugyo strain now reported in Kenya, Uganda, and Nigeria. Authorities have implemented enhanced surveillance and protective measures to prevent cross-border spread. The high mortality rate is approximately 50%, highlighting the severity of the epidemic amid security challenges and public resistance to disease-control measures. No vaccine is approved specifically for Bundibugyo; health workers and communities face threats impacting containment efforts.

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en la República Democrática del Congo deja ya más de 5.000 personas muertas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has already claimed more than 5,000 lives.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has claimed more than 5,000 lives, with 10,351 confirmed infections and 5,026 deaths as of Oct 29. Case fatality is 48.6%; contact tracing 84.5%; 2,788 recoveries and 1,101 patients hospitalized or in isolation. Ituri (epicenter) and North Kivu are the hardest hit, accounting for 36.4% and 58.4% of new cases, respectively, with the outbreak spreading across 67 health zones in eight provinces: Ituri, North Kivu, Tshopo, Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé, South Kivu, Ubangi Sud, and Ubangi Nord. The African Union’s public health agency and WHO have urged coordinated action. The Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain has no specific treatment; two vaccines are in phase 1 trials. RDC has begun Ervebo vaccination (for Zaire lineage) with encouraging signs against Bundibugyo in animals. Imported/exported cases include Uganda (20 cases, 15 imported from DRC; 2 deaths), Kenya (9; 2 deaths), Nigeria (1); a France-linked case; evacuees to the Netherlands (1) and Germany (2). Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and hemorrhaging.

article.articleHeadline: Offiziell 5.000 Ebola-Tote: Was wir zum Ausbruch im Kongo wissen
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Officially 5,000 Ebola deaths: What we know about the outbreak in the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo faces the fastest Ebola outbreak in Africa, with 5,026 deaths confirmed and cases reported across eight provinces. The outbreak is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; more than half of fatalities have occurred outside treatment centers, heightening transmission risk for families and communities. Surveillance gaps and delays suggest true infections are higher than official tallies. In Mongbwalu, officials caution that confirmed numbers are likely a lower bound due to delayed reporting and retrospective reclassification. The northeast and east of the country are most affected, in regions long plagued by armed conflict with over 100 militias, complicating access to care and contact tracing. There is no vaccine for Bundibugyo ebolavirus; Ervebo against Zaire ebolavirus may offer partial protection. Vaccines specific to Bundibugyo are in early trials begun since July, with broad deployment unlikely before mid-2027; no official duration estimates exist.

triage.notes: Bundibugyo型エボラウイルスに対する有効なワクチンが存在せず、武装勢力による治安悪化で対応が困難。実際の感染者数は公式統計より多い可能性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: BREAKING: NCDC identifies two new suspected Ebola cases in North-East
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola cases identified by Nigeria's NCDC in the North-East have been isolated; contact tracing and laboratory investigations are ongoing, with infection status not yet confirmed as of 2026-10-31. This follows Nigeria's first Ebola case in the current outbreak, the Bundibugyo strain, confirmed around 2026-10-20 after a 42-year-old woman who travelled from Uganda via Addis Ababa to Abuja developed symptoms on Oct 7. She was diagnosed in Abuja, prompting activation of the national incident management system and expanded IPC, with 53 contacts identified (healthcare workers, domestic staff, spouse). The patient was evacuated to Switzerland on Oct 26; her husband was isolated in Zurich. By Oct 29, 62 contacts were identified. The outbreak is linked to a broader Bundibugyo outbreak declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in May 2026; Kenya has reported related infections. Public health guidance emphasizes hand hygiene and compliance with guidance.

article.articleHeadline: congo ebola outbreak: death toll passes 5,000
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed over 5,000 and sickened more than 10,000 as of 31 October 2026. The rare Bundibugyo strain drives this epidemic, for which there are neither authorized medicines nor approved inoculations. Since the outbreak was officially announced in May 2026, authorities have not yet found a means of containing it in this Central African nation. Late case identification, ongoing armed conflict, and overwhelmed medical facilities have allowed the pathogen to spread more rapidly than in previous outbreaks, marking this as the nation’s worst Ebola crisis on record. Figures released by the government indicate the toll continues to climb.

article.articleHeadline: Africa CDC Chief Jean Kaseya Appeals For Global Support To End Ebola Outbreak
article.articleSummary: On Oct 31, 2026, Africa CDC Director-General Dr Jean Kaseya urged intensified global support to end the Ebola outbreak in Africa, reporting more than 10,000 confirmed cases and 5,000 deaths. A DR Congo native living in Canada since 2013, Kaseya used a post on X to call for partners to stop Ebola at its source, noting the risk to Canada remains low. He acknowledged Canada’s contributions—early Africa CDC funding, vaccine-trial support, and scientific collaboration with Congolese researchers sequencing the virus. He cautioned against panic but urged seriousness and public engagement with response efforts. The appeal accompanies renewed efforts to strengthen surveillance, research, vaccination preparedness, and cross-border cooperation to contain Ebola and prevent further transmission.

The illness is caused by Bundibugyo virus, one of the Ebola species, declared mid-May this year. Transmission follows typical Ebola patterns: direct contact with bodily fluids, handling of the deceased, and unprotected exposure in medical settings. Cross-border concerns exist, with Kenya, Nigeria reporting related cases, and Uganda recording infections in early months. Public health authorities face containment and early-detection challenges amid high mortality and regional spread risk.

article.articleHeadline: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,000 people and infected over 10,300, across eight of 26 provinces, with Ituri in the northeast as the epicentre amid ongoing conflict. Beginning in May, the outbreak became the nation's deadliest in August and now ranks as the second-largest in DR Congo's history, with a case fatality rate of 48.6%. Kenya reports nine cases with two deaths; Nigeria confirms one woman diagnosed who was flown to Switzerland for treatment; Uganda has had no new cases since August, though travel restrictions remain. The Bundibugyo Ebola virus drives this outbreak; there is currently no treatment or vaccine for this strain. WHO Africa urges continued scale-up of control measures, greater access to affected areas, and community outreach, while testing and treatment proceed and vaccine trials are under way. Some responders have been attacked.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国で過去最悪のエボラ出血熱流行、死者5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: IHR4基準すべてに該当し、国際的拡大（ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへの波及）と高い致死率を伴う大規模アウトブレイクであり、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・スイスでの症例/渡航制限が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。主発生地はDRC（イトゥリ州中心）。紛争地域での対応困難、ワクチン・治療法未確立のBundibugyo株によるアウトブレイクである点も重大。

article.articleHeadline: Actualité | L'épidémie de choléra à Mbandaka fait 14 morts et 129 cas dans deux zones de santé en quelques jours | mediacongo.net
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: News | The cholera outbreak in Mbandaka has killed 14 people and recorded 129 cases in two health zones in just a few days | mediacongo.net
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, a cholera outbreak in Mbandaka, Equateur Province, Democratic Republic of Congo, has 129 cases across Wangata and Bolenge health zones, with 14 deaths and 68 recoveries reported in a few days. Bolenge records 104 cases, the most affected, while additional patients are treated in Wangata. Of the 14 fatalities, most occurred in the community before admission to treatment centers. Health authorities have strengthened port controls at Mbandaka and Bolenge and intensified awareness campaigns. The outbreak is linked to recent arrivals by boat from Kinshasa; over 800 passengers were aboard, about 100 with cholera-like symptoms. Preventive measures emphasize handwashing with soap, treating or boiling drinking water, and following other public health guidance.

triage.headline_ja: ムバンダカのコレラ流行、数日間で14人死亡・129人感染（2つの保健ゾーンで発生）
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約11%と高く、わずか数日で129症例・14死亡を記録しており、WPRO基準（異常性・重症度・持続曝露・流行性・管理可能性）全てに該当するためフルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 発生地域にEcuadorが含まれるが記事内容と無関係のため除外。DRCでは既に港湾管理強化や啓発活動が実施されており、キンシャサからの船舶旅客が感染源と疑われるため国内拡大リスクに注意が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 在刚果民主共和国最致命的埃博拉疫情中，超过 5000 人丧生。Australia ChinaTown News 中文华人新闻 - NEWS.CHINA.COM.AU 这里是生活在墨尔本咱自家人的地盘！把客场当主场，视异乡为故园。澳洲唐人街 - 中华澳网 China Town News澳洲唐人街;澳大利亚华人社区和主流新闻媒体
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 people have died in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: DRC's Ebola outbreak has killed over 5,000 people and infected more than 10,300 across eight provinces since May. The August peak was the deadliest, with a 48.6% case fatality rate. The epicenter remains Ituri province in the northeast, a conflict zone hindering control. Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda have confirmed cases. The UN notes this is the 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC and the second-largest. WHO Africa urges expanded control measures, better access to affected areas, and community outreach; testing and treatment continue, with vaccines in trials. The Bundibugyo strain drives the outbreak, and there is no specific treatment or vaccine yet. Transmission via contact with infected bodily fluids; vomiting, diarrhea, organ failure, and bleeding can occur. Attacks on health workers and officials impede response. Uganda reports no cases since August; Kenya has 9 cases (2 deaths); Nigeria has 1 case evacuated to Switzerland. Europe risk very low per ECDC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国で過去最悪のエボラ出血熱流行、死者5000人超

article.articleHeadline: Эбола выходит за пределы Конго: число жертв превысило 5 тысяч
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola goes beyond Congo's borders: the death toll has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed over 5,000 people with about 10,000 infections since May, marking the country’s largest outbreak and the world’s second-largest. Cases have been reported in eight of Congo’s 26 provinces and have appeared in Kenya, Uganda, and Nigeria. The outbreak is driven by the rare Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain, for which there are no approved vaccines or specific treatments. Efforts to control the epidemic are hindered by attacks on healthcare workers; last week a nurse died and another staffer was injured after an assault by youths, with authorities linking violence to misinformation about the disease. The current outbreak trails the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic (~11,000 deaths). Earlier, Congo and Uganda outbreaks prompted the Health Ministry to reach out to Kazakh citizens.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、コンゴ国境を越えて拡大：死者数は5000人を突破
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ流行が発生し、死者5000人超・感染者約1万人に達し、ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリアへの拡大も報告されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでの大規模エボラ流行を主題とし、ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリアへの拡大にも言及しているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。アンゴラも対象国リスト外のため除外。ワクチン・治療薬が未承認のBundibugyo株であること、医療従事者への暴力も流行対応を困難にしている。

article.articleHeadline: Ξεπέρασαν τους 5.000 οι νεκροί από την επιδημία Έμπολα στο Κονγκό
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The death toll from the Ebola epidemic in Congo has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 5,000 people, with 10,351 confirmed cases, as of October 31, 2026. The outbreak has spread across eight provinces: Upper Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Bas-Uele, Tshopo, South Ubangi, and North Ubangi. It is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in DR Congo’s history and the second largest globally, after the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak. Africa CDC on October 31 urged stronger protection for frontline health workers following the deaths of two young Congolese doctors earlier in the week in North Kivu and Ituri. Authorities cite persistent barriers to halting transmission, including delays in case detection and in contact tracing; only about 12% of confirmed cases have been identified among known contacts, with many deaths occurring within communities.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行による死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおける過去最大規模のエボラ流行で死者5,000人超、8州に拡大し、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクがあるためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: 史上最大規模・2番目に致死的なエボラ流行。接触者追跡の遅れ（確認症例の約12%のみ既知接触者から特定）やコミュニティ内死亡が多いなど、制御困難な状況が継続。Africa CDCが医療従事者保護の強化を要請しており、国際支援の必要性が示唆される。

article.articleHeadline: Вторая по смертоносности в истории. Вспышка неизлечимой лихорадки унесла уже более 5000 жизней в Африке
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The second deadliest in history. An outbreak of an incurable fever has already claimed more than 5,000 lives in Africa.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo reports 10,351 Ebola infections and 5,026 deaths (case fatality ~49%), with 2,788 recoveries. The outbreak is driven by Bundibugyo virus, the second deadliest in history after 2014–2016 West Africa (>11,000 deaths). The eastern provinces of Ituri and North Kivu remain the epicenter, with over 9,700 cases and nearly 4,800 deaths; the virus has spread to Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda, making it Africa’s most geographically expansive outbreak. There is no vaccine or specific therapy for Bundibugyo; patients receive supportive care. The outbreak began in mid-May and touches 67 medical zones across eight provinces. About 80% of new infections occur outside traced contacts, and about one-third of deaths occur outside medical centers without testing. Ongoing conflict in the east restricts access; healthcare workers face aggression, a nurse was killed, and Ebola treatment centers report strikes over unpaid salaries (up to four months).

triage.headline_ja: 史上2番目の致死性。アフリカで致死性の熱病の流行がすでに5000人以上の命を奪った
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で1万人超の感染・5000人超の死亡を伴うエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)の大規模流行が継続し、ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへの拡大も報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへの拡大が記載されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。紛争による医療アクセス制限、医療従事者への暴力、未払い給与によるストライキなど管理能力への懸念材料が複数存在する。

article.articleHeadline: وفيات فيروس إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية تتجاوز 5 آلاف حالة وسط مخاوف من تفشي الوباء
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola virus deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 5,000 amid fears of an outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths, with 5,026 fatalities among 10,351 laboratory-confirmed cases, yielding a case-fatality rate near 50%. The rising toll signals ongoing containment challenges and raises concerns about potential spread to neighboring African countries. The World Health Organization, on May 17, designated the outbreak in the DRC and Uganda as a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, citing high regional risk. Across Africa, Ebola has killed more than 15,000 people in five decades, and the 2018–2020 outbreak remains the deadliest on record, with about 2,300 deaths from roughly 3,500 cases.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラウイルスによる死者数が5000人を超え、流行拡大への懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: WHOがPHEIC（国際的に懸念される公衆衛生上の緊急事態）を宣言済みで、死者数5000人超・致死率約50%という深刻な公衆衛生インパクトがあり、周辺国への拡大懸念もあるためフルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事はウガンダも発生地域として言及しているが、対象国リストに含まれないため除外。PHEIC宣言日（5月17日）の年次については記事中に明記がなく不明瞭。

article.articleHeadline: Kenia defiende su gestión del ébola tras restricciones de viaje impuestas por Arabia Saudí
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya defends its handling of Ebola after travel restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia.
article.articleSummary: Kenya defended its Ebola response after Saudi Arabia restricted travel citing cases detected in Kenya. The Health Ministry said the index case was imported from the Democratic Republic of the Congo; 135 contacts were traced and 118 quarantined. Eight confirmed cases were linked to the index patient—four healthcare workers and four relatives—with no community transmission. No new cases have been reported since 19 October 2026; one death, seven remain in treatment, and five have an initial negative test after completing treatment, awaiting a second test. An additional 46 quarantined contacts are asymptomatic, joining 20 discharged. Saudi restrictions target entrants from Kenya. The index patient, Kenyan, had spent years in DRC and arrived in Nairobi 3 Oct, dying 5 Oct. The DRC outbreak reports 10,351 cases and 5,026 deaths; Uganda has 20 infections (15 imported) and two deaths; cases linked to Nigeria and France, with evacuees to the Netherlands and Germany. Bundibugyo strain; vaccines in early human trials.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、サウジアラビアによる渡航制限後、エボラ対応を擁護
triage.triage_reason: IHR2005の4基準すべてに該当する可能性が高く、DRCでの大規模エボラ流行（10,351症例・5,026死亡）を背景に国際的な渡航制限措置（サウジアラビア）が発生しているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はケニアでの輸入症例とサウジアラビアの渡航制限だが、ケニアは対象国リスト外のため除外。一方、アウトブレイクの根源かつ大規模な流行（10,351症例・5,026死亡）であるDRCは記事内で実質的な主題として扱われているため含めた。ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・フランス・オランダ・ドイツは対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Beni : dix-huit écoles touchées par Ebola dotées de dispositifs de lavage des mains - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Beni: eighteen Ebola-affected schools equipped with handwashing facilities - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease continues to affect Beni in North Kivu, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 18 schools now equipped to curb transmission. On 31 October 2026, handwashing facilities and potable-water storage tanks were provided to these Ebola-affected institutions through the PPSSP, supported by a humanitarian partner. An initial survey indicated more than ten affected schools, expanding to approximately eighteen, with ongoing plans to extend interventions. In addition to wash stations and water storage, liquid soap and alcohol-based gels were supplied to administrative offices and classrooms. Targeting prioritized schools with notified or identified cases, and nearby facilities were included. The program stresses hygiene as a critical outbreak measure and calls for intensified awareness among students, teachers, and staff to wash hands at classroom entry and exit to break the transmission chain.

triage.headline_ja: ベニ：エボラの影響を受けた18校に手洗い設備を設置 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国北キブ州ベニで継続中のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクに関する報道であり、重篤な公衆衛生イベントであるため。
triage.notes: 記事は既知のエボラアウトブレイクに対する学校での衛生対策（手洗い設備設置）の進捗報告であり、新規発生の報告ではないが、継続中の深刻な公衆衛生事案としてフルRRA対象とすべき。

article.articleHeadline: Haut-Uélé : une mission de sécurisation et sensibilisation de la population face à Ebola - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Upper Uele: a mission to secure and raise awareness among the population about Ebola - ACP
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, in Bolebole, Haut-Uélé, Democratic Republic of the Congo, a mission led by the vice-governor, Christophe Dara Matata, was mounted to restore state authority amid threats to Ebola response teams and the Ebola treatment centre in the Bolebole trade hub. Acting on a mandate from the provincial security commission on behalf of Governor Jean Bakomito, the mission aims to secure the area and raise community awareness to defeat Ebola, after insurgent movements targeted response teams along PK51 on RN25 (Nia-Nia–Wamba) corridor. Some Ebola patients are reportedly hiding at home for fear of reprisals, underscoring the need to protect responders per President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo, who chairs the national Ebola task-force. The delegation included governors' staff and the expanded provincial security committee; Bolebole currently records the highest number of confirmed Ebola cases in the province.

triage.headline_ja: オート・ウエレ州：エボラ対策チーム保護と住民啓発のための治安確保ミッション - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国オート・ウエレ州ボレボレで、反政府勢力による対応チームへの攻撃や患者の隠匿が報告され、州内で最多の確定症例を抱える治療センターの機能に支障が生じているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: BluedotのインドネシアおよびProvinsi Sulawesi Selatanのタグ付けは地理コーディングの誤りと判断。記事の主題はコンゴ民主共和国オート・ウエレ州ボレボレでのエボラ対応に関する治安問題。治療センターへの攻撃や患者の隠匿は感染拡大リスクを高める重大な要因。

article.articleHeadline: Avianca realiza estas recomendaciones a pasajeros sobre nueva declaración obligatoria en viaje a EEUU por el ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Avianca issues these recommendations to passengers about the new mandatory declaration for travel to the United States due to Ebola.
article.articleSummary: From November 3, 2026, travelers to the United States must declare they have not been in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (including in transit) during the 21 days prior to boarding. The measure, mandated by CDC guidelines, is part of U.S. Ebola public health safeguards. The Democratic Republic of the Congo reports about 9,500 Ebola cases and 4,600 deaths. Avianca advised completing the declaration in advance to avoid delays; forms can be filled online (one per passenger) or downloaded, printed, and filled physically. The requirement applies to passengers traveling to the United States or with connections to the United States whose flight departs after 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on November 3, 2026. At boarding, travelers must present the digital proof of completion or the completed and signed declaration; failure to present prevents boarding.

triage.headline_ja: アビアンカ航空、エボラ出血熱に伴う米国渡航時の新たな申告義務について乗客に案内
triage.triage_reason: DRCで約9,500症例・4,600人死亡という大規模なエボラ流行が継続しており、米国がCDC主導で渡航者への申告義務を課すなど国際的な渡航制限措置が実施されているため、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 記事は米国の渡航規制措置を主題とするが、根本的な感染症イベントはDRCでのエボラ流行。米国は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。症例数・死亡数が非常に大きく、通常のエボラ流行規模を大きく超える点で異常性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola en el Congo: la carrera contra una cadena de contagios invisible
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Congo: the race against an invisible chain of transmissions
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 31, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak has reached 10,351 infections and 5,026 deaths, making it the second deadliest Ebola event. Major transmission clusters are in Ituri and North Kivu in the east, where conflict, insecurity, and weak health infrastructure hinder access and sustained surveillance. About 80% of new cases are detected outside established contact-tracing chains, and nearly one-third of decedents did not receive care, underscoring the need for early detection and timely treatment. International spread includes Kenya (8 infections, 2 deaths), Nigeria (one case), and earlier Uganda infections, highlighting cross-border surveillance needs. WHO notes no approved vaccine or specific treatment; care is predominantly supportive. Containment demands rapid case finding, comprehensive contact tracing, safe patient care, health worker protection, community engagement, and regional coordination to sever transmission chains.

triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）大規模アウトブレイクが1万人超の感染・5千人超の死亡に達し、ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへの越境伝播も確認されており、IHR基準の複数に該当する深刻な公衆衛生上の脅威である。

article.articleHeadline: أكثر من 5 آلاف حالة وفاة بإيبولا في الكونجو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 Ebola-related deaths in Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo has logged more than 5,000 Ebola-related deaths and over 10,000 cases in the current Bundibugyo strain outbreak. There are no approved vaccines or therapies for Bundibugyo. The outbreak has spread to eight of 26 provinces, with many deaths occurring outside treatment centers. Delayed detection, ongoing conflict, and weak health services have accelerated transmission, making this the second-largest Ebola outbreak globally this year, behind the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic that infected over 28,600 and killed more than 11,000 in Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. The geographic reach has extended to West Africa, with Nigeria reporting infection last week, and Kenya and Uganda reporting cases in East Africa, underscoring cross-regional spread.

article.articleHeadline: Kongo DR Ebolas upuru skaits pārsniedz 5000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola death toll in DR Congo exceeds 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed cases, with 1,101 currently in treatment or quarantine and 2,788 recovered. Since mid-May, when the latest outbreak was detected, more than 5,000 deaths have been reported, and the true toll could be higher as experts believe the virus may have circulated unnoticed since February, months before the outbreak was officially declared on May 15. The current outbreak is driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain and was initially not detected by conventional tests. Infections began in Ituri province in northeastern DR Congo, then spread to remote northern and eastern regions affected by conflict. Data are from national health authorities as of October 31, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱による死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 死者5,000人超・確定症例10,351人という大規模なエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクであり、稀な株による検知遅延や紛争地域への拡大もあることからIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: イトゥリ州（Ituri）はDRC国内の州単位情報であり、対象国リストにはDRC（203312）として統合して記載。稀なBundibugyo株による流行で、2月から未検知の可能性があり、紛争地域での対応の困難さも指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Nigeria identifica dos casos sospechosos de ébola en el noreste del país
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nigeria identifies two suspected cases of Ebola in northeastern Nigeria.
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola virus disease cases were identified in northeastern Nigeria, with both individuals isolated and contact tracing and laboratory testing underway, after an imported case was confirmed on October 20 in a Swiss citizen of Ugandan origin who had returned from Uganda. Nigeria’s NCDC did not specify the state. Genomic analyses indicate the Nigerian case is genetically related to a virus seen in Kenya, though this does not confirm direct transmission; authorities noted a possible cross-border link at Entebbe airport on October 3. Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo involves eight provinces with 10,351 confirmed cases and 5,026 deaths. Uganda declared the outbreak over on August 26 after 20 infections, including 15 imported. Kenya reported nine linked cases and two deaths; France recorded a linked case; three people were evacuated to the Netherlands and Germany. No specific treatments exist; vaccines are in human trials.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリア北東部でエボラ出血熱の疑い症例2例を確認
triage.triage_reason: ウガンダ由来の輸入エボラ症例を起点に、ナイジェリア・ケニア・フランス・スイス・オランダ・ドイツへの国際的な拡大が既に確認されており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大）に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリアの疑い症例だが、ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・ケニアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。背景として言及されるDRCのブンディブジョ・エボラウイルス流行（8州、確認症例10,351例、死亡5,026例）は対象国に該当し、実質的な発生国として記載があるためverified_locationsに含めた。数値の規模が通常のエボラ流行と比べ非常に大きく、情報の正確性については続報での確認が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola deaths top 5,000, cases recorded elsewhere in Africa
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo virus, has killed 5,026 of 10,351 infections with 2,788 recoveries. Declared in mid-May, it is the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak after West Africa's 2014–2016 epidemic (about 11,000 deaths). The eastern provinces of Ituri and North Kivu are epicenters, with 9,782 confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths; fifty of the affected 67 health zones have active cases across eight provinces. About 80% of new infections come from outside the monitored contact chain. One-third of deaths occurred without care, and another third occurred before testing. The Bundibugyo virus has no vaccine or specific treatment; care is supportive. Security challenges — armed conflict, attacks on health workers, and unpaid-wage strikes — hamper response. Kenya (8 cases, 2 deaths), Nigeria (1 case evacuated to Switzerland), and Uganda reported cases in 2026.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱による死者数が5,000人を超え、アフリカの他地域でも症例が確認される
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブジョウイルス）流行が死者5,000人超・感染者1万人超に達し、ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへの国際的拡大も確認されており、IHR基準に複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべき。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア（スイスへ退避）・ウガンダでも症例が報告されているが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ワクチン・特異的治療法がないブンディブジョウイルスによる流行であり、医療従事者への攻撃や武力紛争が対応を阻害している点も重大なリスク要因。

article.articleHeadline: ΛΔ Κονγκό: Περισσότεροι από 5.000 νεκροί από το φονικότερο ξέσπασμα Έμπολα
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: More than 5,000 dead from the deadliest Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 5,000 people and recorded over 10,300 confirmed cases across eight of the country’s 26 provinces. The outbreak began in May and peaked in August, making it the deadliest in DRC history and the 17th outbreak there; the current case-fatality rate is 48.6%. The epicenter remains Ituri Province in the northeast, a conflict zone that hampers containment. Cases have also been confirmed in Kenya (nine cases, two deaths), Nigeria (one confirmed case evacuated to Switzerland), and Uganda (no new cases since August; travel restrictions persist). The Bundibugyo strain drives this outbreak; there is no approved therapy or vaccine for this strain, though diagnostics, treatment, and vaccine trials are ongoing. WHO Africa calls for intensified control, greater access to affected areas, and community engagement, amid attacks on health workers and responders.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴ：史上最悪のエボラ出血熱流行で死者5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: DRコンゴ史上最悪規模のエボラ流行（死者5,000人超、致死率48.6%）であり、ケニア・ナイジェリア（スイスへ搬送）等への国際的拡大、ウガンダでの渡航制限継続など、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・スイスへの症例波及が報告されているが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。Bundibugyo株には承認済み治療薬・ワクチンがなく、紛争地帯（イツリ州）での封じ込め困難が懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: L'Ebola in Congo supera i 5.000 morti e metà delle vittime non ha mai visto un ospedale
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Congo surpasses 5,000 deaths, and half of the victims have never seen a hospital.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has topped 5,000 deaths and 10,000+ cases since the May declaration, driven by the Bundibugyo strain for which there are no vaccines or approved treatments. About 66 health zones across 8 of 26 provinces have reported cases; nearly half of those infected have died, and at least half of the deaths occurred without hospitalization. Roughly 80% of new cases come from people outside monitored contact chains; Africa CDC notes control only when that share falls to 5%. The outbreak began May 15 in Bunia, Ituri, with suspected circulation in Mongbwalu since February. Cross-border spread includes Nigeria (one case) and Kenya (nine cases, two deaths). A Bunia-based TUMAINI vaccine trial began Oct 23, testing candidates including Ervebo for potential protection against Bundibugyo. Uganda imposes a 21-day quarantine for travelers from Congo. This is Congo’s 17th Ebola outbreak; the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic (Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone) was larger (28,600 cases, >11,000 deaths).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱、死者5,000人を超える。犠牲者の半数は病院を一度も受診していない
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行が5,000人超の死者・10,000人超の症例に達し、ワクチン・治療薬がないBundibugyo株による越境拡大（ナイジェリア、ケニア）も発生しており、IHR基準の複数（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大、渡航制限）に該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラ流行（第17次）を主題としており、ナイジェリア・ケニア・シエラレオネ・リベリア・ギニア・ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。致死率約50%、ワクチン・承認治療薬がないBundibugyo株、接触者追跡外からの新規感染が80%に達するなど制御困難な状況が示されている。

article.articleHeadline: Kenya seeks review of Saudi travel restrictions over Ebola
article.articleSummary: Kenya urged Saudi Arabia to reverse its suspension of travel and visa issuance for Kenyans amid an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Kenyan authorities say nine confirmed Ebola cases are traced to a single cluster linked to an imported case reported on October 6, 2026, with the outbreak contained and WHO guidance against travel and trade restrictions. Kenya warns that Saudi travel measures—visa bans and prohibitions on travelers who visited Kenya in the prior 21 days—could disrupt pilgrimages, employment, education, and trade. The government has requested WHO justification for the measures under International Health Regulations (2005) Regulation 43 within 48 hours and plans to raise the issue with Africa CDC in collaboration with affected African states. Kenya remains open to providing a detailed technical briefing to Saudi Public Health Authority on the Ebola situation.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、エボラ出血熱を理由としたサウジアラビアの渡航制限の見直しを要求
triage.triage_reason: DRCで発生したエボラ出血熱がケニアにも拡大し、サウジアラビアによる渡航制限措置が発動されるなど、国際的拡大と渡航制限の両方のIHR基準に該当するため。
triage.notes: 記事の主眼はDRCで発生したエボラ出血熱の輸入例に由来するケニアでの二次感染と、それに対するサウジアラビアの渡航制限措置に関する外交的対応。ケニアおよびサウジアラビアは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: وفيات إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية تتجاوز 5 آلاف حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpass 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 5,026 deaths, from 10,351 confirmed infections, according to the Ministry of Health on 31 October 2026. The case-fatality rate is about 50%. A World Health Organization official noted that roughly one-third of fatalities occurred outside treatment centers and before patients were tested, complicating containment of the outbreak. The data come from today’s ministry release and indicate the outbreak remains deadly and ongoing in the country, with transmission continuing alongside gaps in access to diagnostic confirmation. These figures underscore the ongoing Ebola epidemic in the DRC and the persistent challenge of diagnosing and treating cases promptly.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ死者数、5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%、死者5,000人超・感染者1万人超という深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、地域外発生例や診断前死亡など感染拡大・管理困難性が顕著なため、IHR基準複数該当でフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: WHO関係者が死亡例の約3分の1が治療施設外・検査前に発生していると指摘しており、診断・隔離体制の不備が感染拡大リスクを高めている。継続的な経過観察とフルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: República Democrática del Congo: brote de ébola ya mató a 5.000 personas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Ebola outbreak has already killed 5,000 people.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains one of the decade’s most severe public health emergencies in Africa. An INSP epidemiological report, using data through October 29, shows 10,351 laboratory-confirmed infections and 5,026 deaths, a case-fatality rate of 48.6%. Recoveries total 2,788, while 1,101 patients are currently hospitalized or under strict isolation across affected provinces. Healthcare systems face sustained strain as containment priorities focus on early detection, contact tracing, and safe, dignified burials. The contact-follow-up rate stands at 84.5%, but the remaining gap risks further spread in urban and rural settings. Notably, about 80% of new cases originate outside the existing chains of contacts under monitoring, underscoring substantial surveillance and logistics challenges.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国:エボラ出血熱の流行で既に5,000人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.6%、死者5,026人に達する大規模なエボラ出血熱流行であり、新規感染者の約80%が既存の接触者監視網外から発生するなど国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生への深刻な影響が認められるため。
triage.notes: 新規感染者の約80%が既存の接触者追跡網の外で発生している点が、サーベイランスと封じ込めの重大な課題を示しており、継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: DR Congo death toll exceeds 5,000 as cases top 10,000
article.articleSummary: DR Congo reports an Ebola outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo strain, with 10,351 confirmed cases and 5,026 deaths as of 31 October 2026. Authorities logged 77 new confirmed cases and 34 additional deaths. Ituri Province remains the epicenter, accounting for 71% of cases and 36.4% of newly reported cases nationwide. The outbreak has spread to 67 of 178 health zones across eight of DR Congo’s 26 provinces, with a case fatality rate of 48.6%. About 1,101 patients are in treatment and isolation centers, and 2,788 have recovered. Insecurity in eastern DR Congo hampers response, with threats to health workers. There is no licensed vaccine specific to Bundibugyo; the Ervebo vaccine has been deployed to protect frontline responders. The WHO urges additional funding. Cases linked to the wider outbreak have been reported in Nigeria, with Uganda, Kenya and France also reporting related cases.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴ民主共和国で死者数5,000人超、症例数1万人突破
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.6%・症例1万人超・死者5,000人超という深刻な規模に加え、ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・ケニア・フランスへの国際拡大も報告されており、IHR基準を複数満たすためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株による大規模流行で、未承認ワクチンのみ使用可能な状況。治安悪化により対応が困難で、既に複数国へ感染拡大が確認されている。ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・ケニア・フランスは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: Kenia rechaza restricciones de viaje impuestas por Arabia Saudí tras detectar casos de ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kenya rejects travel restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia after detecting Ebola cases.
article.articleSummary: Kenya rejected Saudi Arabia’s travel restrictions after Ebola cases were detected, stating there is no community transmission and no new cases since October 19, 2026. The Health Ministry reported two deaths, including the index patient, and eight confirmed infections linked to the index case—four health workers and four close relatives. A total of 118 contacts were quarantined; all confirmed cases remained within this cluster. Seven patients are still undergoing care; five have a first negative test, with a second test due Monday. 46 contacts remain in quarantine, and 20 have been discharged. Saudi Arabia suspended travel to Kenya and barred visas for Kenyans; entry rules apply to travelers from Kenya or with recent contact within 21 days. The index patient was a 40-year-old Kenyan who had lived in the DRC, arrived Nairobi Oct 3, and died Oct 5. The DRC outbreak has 10,351 cases and 5,026 deaths; vaccines are in trials.

triage.headline_ja: ケニア、エボラ症例検出後のサウジアラビアによる渡航制限を拒否
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の国境を越えた伝播（DRC由来の指標症例がケニアで死亡、医療従事者を含む二次感染が発生）と、サウジアラビアによる渡航制限という国際的対応が生じており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: 主要な報道対象はケニアでの二次感染クラスター（対象国リスト外）だが、指標症例の渡航元であり継続的大規模流行が進行中のDRC（10,351例・5,026死亡）が記事中で具体的に言及されているため、verified_locationsにDRCを含めた。ケニア・サウジアラビアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: وفيات فيروس إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية تتجاوز 5000 حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola virus deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have surpassed 5,000. The health authorities report 5,026 fatalities among 10,351 confirmed Ebola cases, yielding a case fatality rate close to 50%. As of October 31, 2026, the outbreak remains severe, prompting warning from experts about health system capacity to contain transmission. The statistics indicate a deadly burden within the DRC and show the virus has spread to several African countries beyond the outbreak's origin, complicating containment efforts. Public health officials are monitoring progression, reinforcing surveillance, diagnostics, and response measures, as authorities work to identify infection clusters and prevent further amplification. The reported figures reflect ongoing, sustained transmission and highlight the urgent need for effective control strategies to reduce fatalities.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラウイルスによる死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%、感染者1万人超・死者5000人超という甚大な公衆衛生インパクトがあり、国境を越えた拡大も報告されているためIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事は他のアフリカ諸国への拡大に言及しているが、具体的な対象国名は明示されていないため、DRC以外は検証不能。続報で拡大先国の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola deixa mais de 5 mil mortos na República Democrática do Congo desde maio
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola leaves more than 5,000 dead in the Democratic Republic of the Congo since May.
article.articleSummary: As of October 31, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has caused 5,026 deaths since it began in May, with 10,351 infections and 2,788 recoveries. The case fatality rate is near 50%. The provinces of Ituri and North Kivu account for 4,792 deaths and more than 9,700 infections. Ebola is a viral hemorrhagic fever transmitted from animals to humans, with infection occurring through direct contact with blood or other fluids of infected people. Ongoing conflict and violence—including local forces, the M23 rebel group, and other militias—complicate response efforts. Rwanda has been accused of supporting the M23. Security disruptions hinder healthcare access, and WHO notes that about one third of deaths occurred without medical care.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、コンゴ民主共和国で5月以降5000人以上が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%の大規模エボラ出血熱アウトブレイクで、死者5,000人超・感染者1万人超と深刻な公衆衛生影響があり、紛争による対応困難も重なり国際的関心・支援が必要な事案。
triage.notes: ルワンダは紛争(M23)への関与の文脈で言及されているのみで、エボラ発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外。

article.articleHeadline: VSR e influenza estão entre os vírus associados a mortes por SRAG
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: RSV and influenza are among the viruses associated with deaths due to SARI.
article.articleSummary: Acre, Brazil, reports 2026 deaths from severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) linked to multiple respiratory viruses. The surveillance panel records 23 SRAG deaths with no identified agent and 80 additional cases under investigation. Among identified pathogens, influenza A caused three deaths (one linked to subtype H1N1, two unsubtyped); a single death was linked to adenovirus. Other detections include RSV, rhinovirus, metapneumovirus, and Covid-19. In the year’s SRAG data, 913 cases are classified as unspecified SRAG in Acre, with 65 cases of influenza A unsubtyped, 18 H1N1, 9 H3N2, and 2 influenza B. Adenovirus appears in 53 cases, plus one death. The findings underscore diverse respiratory etiologies contributing to severe infections and fatalities in Acre during 2026, with ongoing investigations and weekly surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: RSVとインフルエンザが、重症急性呼吸器感染症（SRAG）による死亡に関連するウイルスとして挙がる
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・アクレ州における季節性呼吸器ウイルス（インフルエンザ、RSV等）によるSRAGサーベイランス報告であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 複数の既知呼吸器病原体（インフルエンザA/B、RSV、アデノウイルス、メタニューモウイルス、COVID-19）による季節性サーベイランス報告であり、新興感染症や異常なクラスターではない。

article.articleHeadline: NCDC identifies two suspected Ebola cases in North-East | The ICIR- Latest News, Politics, Governance, Elections, Investigation, Factcheck, Covid-19
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola cases identified by Nigeria's NCDC in the North-East, with both individuals isolated as lab tests proceed; states involved not disclosed as of 2026-10-31. This follows Nigeria's first imported Ebola case, caused by Bundibugyo virus, confirmed in Abuja on 20 October 2026. The 42-year-old woman traveled from Uganda via Addis Ababa, arriving 3 October, developed symptoms 7 October, and sought care 11 October. Initial contact tracing identified 44 potential contacts, later rising to 62; all are under monitoring as of 29 October. The index patient was evacuated to Switzerland on 26 October. The outbreak is Bundibugyo Ebola, with the wider outbreak starting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in May 2026 and reaching Kenya. Nigeria has strengthened surveillance, laboratory testing, and infection prevention/control, while urging proper hygiene, adherence to advisories, and avoidance of misinformation.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリアCDC、北東部でエボラ出血熱の疑い症例2例を確認
triage.triage_reason: ナイジェリアでの輸入エボラ症例に続き新たな疑い例が発生し、DRC発のバンディブギョ型エボラ流行がケニア・ナイジェリアへ拡大するなど国際的拡大とヒト-ヒト感染リスクが明確であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべきシグナルと判断。

article.articleHeadline: DR Congo Ebola case: Wat next for DRC as Ebola deaths hit ova 5000 wit 10,351 cases for second deadliest outbreak - BBC News Pidgin
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: 10,351 confirmed cases, 5,026 deaths (CFR 48.6%) since onset. Ituri is epicenter (71% of confirmed, 36.4% of new), across 178 health zones 67 have reported cases; eight of 26 provinces affected. Currently 1,101 in care; 2,788 recovered. No licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo; Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus) deployed to protect frontline workers. article.articleHeadline: 多毒株活跃，今年流感季提前！最新提示→
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Multiple strains are active; this year's flu season is earlier than usual! Latest tips →.
article.articleSummary: Influenza activity in China shows co-circulation of multiple strains this year, with A(H3N2) and B Victoria lineage predominant since July and A(H1N1) on the rise; overall H3N2 is more prevalent. The season is starting earlier and, with cooler weather and indoor crowding, transmission risk increases in schools and offices. High‑risk groups for severe disease include children, adults ≥65, pregnant women, people with chronic conditions, and the immunocompromised. Warning signals of worsening illness include persistent high fever despite antipyretics, fever relapse after defervescence, symptoms lasting >5 days, severe cough or chest tightness, shortness of breath or pneumonia; children may become lethargic or irritable with vomiting; young adults may have chest pain or dizziness; elderly may show reduced appetite or apathy without high fever. Vaccination remains advised throughout the season; best window is September–October, with protection developing 2–4 weeks after. This year’s vaccines update three components: split inactivated, subunit inactivated (both for 6 months+), and live attenuated nasal spray (3–17 years; not for elderly or immunocompromised).

article.articleHeadline: La peligrosa complacencia mundial ante el ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The world's dangerous complacency in the face of Ebola
article.articleSummary: 10,193 Ebola cases and 4,960 deaths in the Democratic Republic of Congo as of 27 October 2026 mark the deadliest outbreak in its history, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus rather than the Zaire strain. With no fully authorized vaccines or antivirals proven effective, the response relies on a combination of multivalent vaccines and rapid clinical trials, plus basic containment, contact tracing, and isolation. The northeast DRC, long destabilized by conflict, hinders tracing to the 95% target needed to stop transmission. Global funding shortfalls and fragmented strategies undermine humanitarian operations and biosecurity. Africa CDC is coordinating a continental response—cross-border surveillance, harmonized protocols with neighbors, and community-centered containment—engaging religious leaders, youth advocates, and trusted health workers to combat misinformation. Donors should empower an Africa-led command to safeguard health security.

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو الديمقراطية: وفيات إيبولا تتجاوز (5) آلاف حالة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo: Ebola deaths exceed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has escalated with 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed infections, according to the Ministry of Health reporting on 31 October 2026. The case fatality rate stands at about 50%. A World Health Organization official noted that roughly one third of deaths occurred outside Ebola treatment centers and prior to diagnostic testing, complicating efforts to contain transmission. The figures reflect ongoing transmission within the DRC and highlight access barriers to care and timely testing as critical factors driving mortality. The data underscores the need for expanded surveillance, rapid isolation, and community engagement to reduce fatalities and curb the spread of Ebola within the country.

article.articleHeadline: Más de 5,000 muertes por brote de Ébola en República del Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 deaths from an Ebola outbreak in the Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 5,000 deaths with over 10,300 confirmed cases across eight of 26 provinces, begun in May and centered in Ituri in the northeast amid conflict. The current outbreak is due to Bundibugyo ebolavirus; no approved treatment or vaccine exists. Case fatality is 48.6%, making it the deadliest in DRC history and the second-largest on record after West Africa (2014–2016) with over 11,325 deaths. Transmission occurs via contact with infected bodily fluids; early symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, progressing to organ failure and hemorrhage. Response hampered by attacks on health workers; a nurse was killed and another seriously injured, and a politician was killed after promoting containment measures. Uganda reports 2 deaths and 20 cases; Kenya 9 cases and 2 deaths; Nigeria has 2 suspected cases under isolation. Europe’s risk is deemed very low by ECDC.

article.articleHeadline: Congo registra más de 10.000 casos de ébola y la epidemia continúa sin control
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo records more than 10,000 Ebola cases, and the outbreak remains out of control.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains uncontrolled as of Oct 29, with 10,351 confirmed cases and 5,026 deaths (case fatality rate 48.6%). There are 2,788 recoveries and 1,101 patients hospitalized or in isolation; contact tracing covers 84.5%, but roughly 80% of new infections occur in people not listed, hindering transmission-source identification. International agencies urge a coordinated continental response, prioritizing early case detection, contact tracing, and safe burials. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo strain; no specific vaccine or approved treatment exists. WHO is testing two vaccines in Phase 1; Congo began August vaccination with Ervebo (Zaire ebolavirus) despite not being strain-specific; animal data suggest possible cross-protection. The outbreak has surpassed the 2018–2020 toll in the region but remains below the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ感染者が1万人を超え、流行は依然として制御不能

triage.notes: 発生地域にUganda、Angolaが含まれるが記事サマリーではDRC国内の流行のみが主題であり、対象国リストにも含まれないため除外。Bundibugyo株によるアウトブレイクで2018-2020年の同地域の被害を上回る規模。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola en el Congo supera los 5,000 muertos y registra más de 10,000 contagios
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Congo surpasses 5,000 deaths and records more than 10,000 infections.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths and 10,000 infections as of 31 October 2026. Declared in May in the east, it spread to eight provinces and 67 health zones. The case fatality rate is 48.6%; 2,788 recovered and 1,101 remain hospitalized or in isolation. North Kivu (58.4%) and Ituri (36.4%) account for most new cases. Transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids and can cause hemorrhagic fever with vomiting and diarrhea. The WHO and African Union urge coordinated action, noting mortality exceeds the 2018–2020 regional outbreak but remains below Africa’s 2014–2016 crisis (about 11,000 deaths, 28,000 infections). Cases linked to Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria, and one in France; three infected in DRC evacuated to the Netherlands and Germany. Bundibugyo strain; no specific treatment. Ervebo vaccination began in August; two vaccines in Phase 1 with positive safety signals; animal data suggest possible efficacy against Bundibugyo.

article.articleHeadline: Ξεπέρασαν τους 5.000 οι νεκροί από την επιδημία Έμπολα στο Κονγκό - The Press Project - Ειδήσεις, Αναλύσεις, Ραδιόφωνο, Τηλεόραση
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The death toll from the Ebola epidemic in Congo has surpassed 5,000 - The Press Project - News, Analyses, Radio, Television
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed more than 5,000 people, spreading across eight provinces: Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Bas-Uele, Tshopo, Nord-Ubangi and Sud-Ubangi. It is the nation’s largest and deadliest Ebola epidemic and the second-largest globally after West Africa’s 2014–2016 outbreak. Africa CDC this week urged stronger protection for frontline health workers following the deaths of two young Congolese doctors in North Kivu and Ituri. Health authorities say key barriers to halting transmission are delays in detecting cases and tracing contacts. Only about 12% of confirmed cases have been identified among people already recorded as contacts, and many fatalities occur within the communities themselves. The article underscores the ongoing, sprawling nature of the outbreak and the critical need for enhanced surveillance and protective measures.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ流行による死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最大規模のエボラ流行が8州に拡大し死者5,000人超と深刻化しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断する。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCにおける国内最大規模のエボラ流行を報じており、Angolaは発生地域リストに含まれるが記事本文では言及なしのため除外した。感染追跡率の低さ（12%）や医療従事者の死亡など、拡大継続・管理困難性を示す情報あり。

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola en RDC supera los 5.000 fallecidos - teleSUR
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 5,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 10,351 confirmed infections and 5,026 deaths (case fatality rate 48.6%) as of October 29. The Bundibugyo strain currently has no specific treatments, so control relies on patient isolation and extensive contact tracing. Declared May 15, the outbreak spans 67 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, with Ituri accounting for 36.4% of new cases and North Kivu 58.4%. Of the infected, 2,788 have recovered while 1,101 remain hospitalized or in isolation, indicating ongoing transmission. The WHO and the African Union’s health agency held an emergency meeting, urging coordinated regional action as transmission persists. Secondary cases have been reported in Uganda, Kenya, and Nigeria, as well as France, the Netherlands, and Germany. The outbreak is the second deadliest and among the most contagious in global history; vaccines are in Phase 1 trials, and Ervebo has been used experimentally in DRC since August. Emphasis remains on early detection, 84.5% contact tracing, and safe burial protocols.

article.articleHeadline: NCDC Identifies Two Suspected Ebola Cases In Nigeria's North-East, Begins Contact Tracing
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola virus disease cases identified in Nigeria's North-East, with both individuals isolated as health authorities begin contact tracing and laboratory testing to confirm infection. The NCDC cautioned that designation as 'suspected' does not equate to a confirmed case; confirmation will depend on lab results. This follows ongoing Ebola surveillance after a patient was medically evacuated to Switzerland. WHO had noted that Nigeria could not yet be declared Ebola-free, with about 53 contacts under 21-day monitoring, then another 21 days of observation, totaling a 42-day surveillance window. The Swiss government-requested evacuation was not due to Nigerian deficiencies in case management. Nigerians were urged to maintain good hand hygiene and follow public health guidance while investigations continue. Ebola remains a public health concern in Africa, particularly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where the outbreak is described as very serious.

article.articleHeadline: Machado confirma sete casos de escabiose e Sul de Minas chega a 435 registros - BH 24 Horas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Machado confirms seven cases of scabies and Southern Minas Gerais reaches 435 records - BH 24 Horas
article.articleSummary: Machado, Minas Gerais, Brazil reports seven newly confirmed scabies cases among students across three local schools, bringing Southern Minas Gerais’ total to 435 cases across Alfenas (332, including a recent confirmation), Andradas (47), Paraguaçu (35), Poços de Caldas (9), Caldas (3), and Lavras (2). No school closures; cases are monitored individually by Epidemiological Surveillance with involvement from the School Health Program. Authorities provided treatment to all diagnosed students and have medications available for new suspected cases. Outbreaks began after the October school break, with initial preventive cleaning already completed. Transmission is mainly through prolonged direct skin contact and sharing personal items (clothes, towels, bed linens); intense nocturnal itching is a common symptom. Scabies is not on the state’s mandatory reporting list, so local tallies may diverge from SES-MG data, and data are not consolidated in a single database.

triage.notes: 疥癬は接触感染で重症度が低く、学校内での継続的な感染リスクはあるものの、当局により治療・監視体制が確立されている。国家報告義務対象外の疾患である点に留意。

article.articleHeadline: Alarma en Congo por el brote de ébola que ya causó más de 5.000 muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Alarm in Congo over the Ebola outbreak that has already killed more than 5,000 people.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has reached 10,351 confirmed infections and 5,026 deaths as of October 29, per the National Institute of Public Health (INSP). The case fatality rate is 48.6%, with 2,788 recoveries and 1,101 patients hospitalized or under strict isolation in affected provinces. Contact tracing coverage stands at 84.5%. Since the outbreak was declared in May, it remains one of Africa’s most severe public health emergencies, stressing regional healthcare systems. INSP urges strengthened early detection, expanded contact tracing, and safe, dignified burials as urgent response pillars, acknowledging logistical and cultural challenges. Africa CDC notes that approximately 80% of new cases originate outside the current contact-tracing network, underscoring the ongoing transmission risk and need for intensified control measures.

triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.6%、感染者1万人超、死者5千人超の大規模なエボラ流行であり、接触者追跡網外での新規感染が8割に上るなど国際的拡大リスクが高いため。
triage.notes: Africa CDCの指摘によれば新規感染の約80%が既存の接触者追跡網外で発生しており、流行制御の困難さと地域医療システムへの深刻な負荷が示唆される。

article.articleHeadline: Letošní epidemie eboly dosáhla dalšího smutného milníku
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: This year's Ebola epidemic has reached another sad milestone.
article.articleSummary: As of October 31, 2026, the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo (the outbreak’s epicenter) has 10,060 confirmed cases, with roughly half of the infected dying. It is the fastest-spreading outbreak in history and the deadliest in DR Congo, surpassed only by West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic (over 28,000 cases and 11,310 deaths). Cases have also been reported in Kenya and Nigeria, while Uganda and France currently report no active cases. Ebola, a hemorrhagic fever first identified in 1976 in Zaire (now the DRC), involves five strains: Bundibugyo, Sudan, Taï Forest, Reston, and Zaire; three are known to cause severe disease in humans. Transmission occurs via contact with blood, secretions, and bodily fluids, and healthcare workers are often affected due to limited protections.

triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ出血熱が1万例を超え致死率約50%、史上最速拡大で複数国への波及も報告されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大な公衆衛生イベントである。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリアでも症例報告ありとされるが対象国リストに含まれず、ウガンダ・フランスは現在活動性症例なしと明記。DRCが流行の震源地であり主題。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak death toll crosses 5,000, half the total infected
article.articleSummary: DRC's Ebola outbreak has reached 5,026 deaths from 10,351 infections, with 2,788 recoveries, as of 31 Oct 2026. The Bundibugyo virus has no vaccine or specific treatment; declared mid-May, it is the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record after 2014–2016 West Africa. The outbreak spans 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, concentrated in Ituri and North Kivu, which together report 9,782 confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths. Case fatality is about 50%. Fifty of the affected health zones remain active. Roughly 80% of new cases occur outside the monitored contact chain, and around one-third of deaths happen outside treatment centres before testing. Security in eastern Congo—fighting with armed groups including M23 and Islamist insurgents, plus ADF—hampers contact tracing, testing, and timely care. Some cases have been reported in other African nations.

triage.triage_reason: DRCのエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクは死者5,000人超・致死率約50%に達し、史上2番目に深刻な流行となっている。治安悪化による対応困難や他国への拡大報告もあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事では『他のアフリカ諸国でも一部症例が報告されている』とあるが、具体的な対象国名は不明のためverified_locationsにはDRCのみを記載。ブンディブギョウイルス型で既存ワクチン・特効薬がなく、治安悪化（M23・ADF等武装勢力）が対応を阻害している点も重大な懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Mehr als 5.000 Ebola-Tote im Kongo - Chronik | stol.it
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 Ebola deaths in the Congo - Chronicle | stol.it.
article.articleSummary: In the DR Congo, a Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak has caused 5,026 deaths and 10,351 cases since mid-May, with 1,101 patients currently in treatment or isolation and 2,788 recovered. Authorities warn the true toll may be higher, as transmission likely began before the May 15 outbreak declaration, possibly as early as February. The outbreak has extended to Kenya, linked to a Kenyan who stayed in Congo, and Nigeria reported its first Ebola case on October 20, tied to the wife of a Swiss diplomat after a Uganda visit. A European case involved a doctor deployed to eastern Congo who tested positive in France in June and recovered. Ebola virus spreads through close contact and bodily fluids, causing a life-threatening fever with diarrhea and bleeding.

article.articleHeadline: יותר מ-5,000 מתים: מגפת האבולה מתפשטת באפריקה
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 dead: The Ebola outbreak is spreading in Africa.
article.articleSummary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, as of 31 October 2026, shows 10,351 infections and 5,026 deaths (case fatality ~50%), driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no vaccine or specific treatment. It is the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak, after 2014–2016 West Africa (≈11,000 deaths). Recovered: 2,788. The epidemic spans 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu bearing the bulk (9,782 infections, 4,792 deaths). About 80% of new cases are among people not on contact-tracing lists; one-third of deaths occur outside treatment centers before diagnosis. Security challenges from armed groups (M23, ADF) and attacks on health workers, plus funding shortages and treatment-center strikes, hinder response. In October, cases were reported in Kenya (8 infections, 2 deaths) and Nigeria (1 patient flown to Switzerland), with earlier cases in Uganda.

triage.notes: ケニア、ナイジェリア、ウガンダ、スイスでの症例報告もあるが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないか（ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイス・ウガンダ）、または主要な発生地ではないため、verified_locationsにはDRCのみを記載。武装勢力による治安悪化・資金不足等で対応が困難化しており、国際支援の必要性が高い状況。

article.articleHeadline: Early diagnosis, timely treatment key to eliminate TB: Expert
article.articleSummary: Early diagnosis, timely treatment and greater public awareness are crucial to a TB-free India, said Prof Tariq Mahmood, at a four-day national conference in Kolkata (Oct 29–Nov 1). TB remains a major public health challenge, but the National Tuberculosis Elimination Programme (NTEP) has strengthened India's ability to diagnose and treat the disease. Government health centres provide free TB testing, medicines and treatment. He highlighted modern diagnostics—CBNAAT (GeneXpert) and Truenat—for early detection and drug-resistance identification. For drug-resistant TB, including MDR/RR-TB, the six-month BPaLM regimen has emerged as an advancement over earlier 18–20 month courses. Patients should not discontinue medicines without medical advice, and those with a persistent cough (>2 weeks) should be tested, with screening for high-risk groups. He urged greater support and an end to discrimination, calling for collaboration among government, healthcare professionals and citizens.

triage.headline_ja: 早期診断と適時の治療がTB撲滅の鍵：専門家
triage.triage_reason: 通常の啓発・教育的な専門家コメント記事であり、異常な流行や新規事象の報告ではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 内容はカンファレンスでの専門家発言に基づく一般的なTB啓発記事であり、新規の発生・急増等の報告ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Alerta por un brote de ébola que ya supera los 5 mil muertos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Warning about an Ebola outbreak that has already surpassed 5,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths as of October 31, 2026. The evolving epidemic strains the national health system, with hospital capacity stretched: more than 1,100 patients currently hospitalized, including 1,101 under strict isolation and monitoring, and 2,788 patients having recovered after specialized care. Despite high mortality, health facilities remain under pressure. The Institute National de Santé Publique (INSP) reports the contact-tracing rate at 84.5%, yet a sizeable fraction of transmission may occur outside identified transmission chains. Africa CDC notes that roughly 80% of new cases come from individuals not linked to monitored contact networks, hindering early case detection and raising urban and rural spread risk. Authorities emphasize strengthening prevention and control, including early detection, contact tracing, and dignified, safe burials, while maintaining surveillance and response in affected provinces.

triage.headline_ja: 5,000人以上の死者を出したエボラ出血熱の流行に対する警告
triage.triage_reason: DRCにおけるエボラ流行が5,000人以上の死者を出し、医療体制が逼迫、接触追跡の約80%が未確認の感染経路によるもので国際的拡大リスクも高く、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: Africa CDCの報告によれば新規症例の約80%が既知の接触者ネットワーク外から発生しており、感染拡大の制御が困難な状況。都市部・農村部双方への拡大リスクが指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Епідемія вірусу Еболи набирає обертів: у Конго вже зафіксовано понад п'ять тисяч смертей (відео)
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola virus epidemic is gaining momentum: in Congo more than five thousand deaths have already been recorded (video)
article.articleSummary: Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo accelerates: government data place fatalities above 5,000 and total infections over 10,000, with deaths continuing as cases rise. The outbreak is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus; there are no approved treatments or vaccines for this strain. Experts warn that delayed detection, ongoing armed conflict, and overstretched health services impede containment. Eight of Congo's 26 provinces have been affected, and many deaths have occurred outside medical facilities. Analysts caution that the virus could spread among more than 5 million displaced people in the eastern region. Earlier reports noted Ebola reaching Europe, where a doctor who treated patients in DRC contracted the virus. The situation highlights critical background factors and a need for intensified public health responses.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスの流行が勢いを増す：コンゴではすでに5000人以上の死者が記録されている（動画）
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で死者5,000人超・感染者10,000人超に達するエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）の大規模流行があり、治療薬・ワクチンが存在せず、既に欧州への感染者流出も報告されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し緊急のリスク評価が必要と判断。
triage.notes: 記事では欧州への感染者流出（DRCで患者を治療した医師が感染）が言及されているが、欧州は対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。治療薬・ワクチン未承認のブンディブギョ株による流行であり、武力紛争下での対応困難、500万人超の避難民への拡大懸念など深刻な状況。
