article.articleHeadline: Deadly Ebola outbreak spirals as death toll hits record high and fears grow over UK spread
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the current Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has killed 5,000 of 10,351 confirmed infections, making it the fastest-growing and second-deadliest Ebola event after 2014–2016. Initiated in May, the outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no vaccine. The outbreak has spread to Kenya (8 confirmed cases, 2 deaths) and Nigeria (1 confirmed case evacuated to Switzerland); Uganda and France have no current active cases. DR Congo faces undercounting due to tracing challenges in the eastern conflict zones amid distrust and attacks on health workers, including a nurse killed responding to an alert. UK risk remains low; UKHSA says readiness, monitoring, and the Returning Workers Scheme for those returning from affected areas (DRC, Central African Republic, South Sudan, Kenya, Nigeria, Uganda). Imported cases are rare; NHS centres are prepared for treatment.

triage.headline_ja: 致死的なエボラ出血熱の流行が拡大、死者数が過去最多を記録し英国への拡散懸念が高まる
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行は致死率約48%、感染者1万人超、ケニア・ナイジェリアへの国際的拡大が確認されており、IHR基準の複数（深刻性・異常性・国際拡大）に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイス・英国・フランスは発生地域として記載されているが対象国リストに含まれないため除外。主たる流行地であるDRCのみをverified_locationsに含めた。ブンディブギョウイルスにはワクチンがなく、東部紛争地域での追跡困難や保健従事者への攻撃により過小報告の懸念もある。

article.articleHeadline: Эпидемия вируса Эбола набирает обороты: в Конго уже зафиксировано более пяти тысяч смертей (видео)
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola virus epidemic is gaining momentum: in Congo, more than five thousand deaths have already been recorded (video).
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has surpassed 10,000 infections and more than 5,000 deaths, according to government data published on Friday. Eight of 26 provinces are affected, with many fatalities occurring outside treatment centers as civil conflict and shortages of clinicians hamper containment. There are no approved treatments or vaccines for this rare Bundibugyo variant. Delays in detection, ongoing armed conflict, and overwhelmed health services have accelerated spread, with more than 5 million people displaced in eastern Congo. The report also notes cross-border risk: Ebola was identified in Europe, in a doctor who treated patients in the DRC.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスの流行が拡大:コンゴで既に5000人以上の死者を記録(動画)
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ(ブンディブギョ株)が1万人超感染・5000人超死亡と大規模化し、国際的拡大(欧州への伝播)も確認されており、IHR基準に複数該当するためフルRRAに進むべき。
triage.notes: 承認された治療法・ワクチンがない希少なブンディブギョ株であること、武力紛争・大規模避難民(500万人超)が封じ込めを困難にしていること、欧州で治療医からの感染が確認されたことが国際拡大リスクを示す重要な要素。

article.articleHeadline: കോംഗോയിൽ എബോള മരണം 5,000 കടന്നു; ആഫ്രിക്കയിലാകെ പടരുമെന്ന് ആശങ്ക
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola deaths in Congo exceed 5,000; fears that it could spread across Africa.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease caused by Bundibugyo virus has claimed 5,026 lives out of 10,351 confirmed infections in the Democratic Republic of Congo as of 31 Oct 2026, according to the Congo health ministry. This is the country’s largest outbreak and the second-deadliest globally, surpassed only by the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic. The outbreak spans 8 of 26 provinces, with 178 health zones and 67 health areas reporting cases; Ituri and North Kivu in eastern DR Congo are the main transmission hubs. Many deaths occur before patients reach care, and authorities face difficulties with contact tracing and surveillance; around 80% of new infections arise outside monitored contact networks. Outside DR Congo, Kenya (8 cases, 2 deaths), Nigeria (1 case), and Uganda have reported cases; Uganda’s earlier spread is described as controlled. There is no licensed vaccine or targeted treatment; patients receive supportive care and fluids, while research on vaccines and therapies continues.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超える；アフリカ全土への拡大懸念
triage.triage_reason: DRCでの史上最大規模のエボラ流行（死者5,026人、感染者10,351人）がケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへ越境拡大しており、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高いためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダへの越境拡大が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在せず、接触者追跡の約80%が監視対象外で発生しているなど、制御困難な状況が継続している。

article.articleHeadline: BROTE DE ÉBOLA EN REPÚBLICA DEMOCRÁTICA DEL CONGO SUPERA LOS 5 MIL MUERTOS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo surpasses 5,000 deaths.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths, with 10,351 confirmed infections and a case fatality rate of 48.6% as of Oct 29, 2026. Recovered: 2,788; 1,101 patients are hospitalized or in isolation. North Kivu (58.4%) and Ituri (36.4%) are the most affected provinces, spanning 67 health zones across eight provinces. An immunization campaign with the Ervebo vaccine began in late August, though it targets Zaire ebolavirus; studies show favorable results against Bundibugyo in animals. There are no specific treatments for Bundibugyo; WHO and the African Union warn the outbreak is not under control and urge intensified surveillance, contact tracing (84.5%), and safe burials. The outbreak began May 15 in eastern DRC, with linked cases in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria, and France, and evacuees to the Netherlands and Germany. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids, causing fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and hemorrhages.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱アウトブレイク、死者数5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率48.6%、死者5000人超、8州67保健地区に拡大し、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランスへの関連症例も報告されており、WHOがアウトブレイクは制御下にないと警告していることから、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリア、フランス、オランダ、ドイツでの関連症例・避難者が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないか（ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア）、二次的な輸出症例（欧州）であるため、主要発生地であるDRCのみをverified_locationsに記載。Bundibugyo種はErvebo（Zaire種対象）の効果が不確実で、特異的治療法がない点もリスクを高めている。

article.articleHeadline: Nigeria: NCDC announces 2 new Ebola cases - Blueprint Newspapers Limited
article.articleSummary: Two additional suspected Ebola cases identified in Nigeria’s North-East as NCDC intensifies surveillance after an imported Bundibugyo virus case. Laboratory investigations are underway to confirm infection; contact tracing identifies and monitors potential exposures, with no identities or travel histories disclosed for the new cases. This follows Nigeria’s first case of the current outbreak, a 42-year-old woman from Uganda who arrived in Abuja (Oct 3); she developed symptoms Oct 7, was admitted Oct 11, confirmed Oct 20, and evacuated to Switzerland on Oct 26. As of Oct 29, 62 contacts were identified, with 18 samples tested: 1 positive and 17 negative; an Enugu suspected case tested negative. The link between the North-East suspects and the Abuja patient remains unconfirmed. Regional context: DRC has 9,704 cases and 4,687 deaths; Kenya reports nine cases (one death) as of Oct 20.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリア:NCDCがエボラ出血熱の新規2例を発表
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）がウガンダからナイジェリアへ越境し、スイスへの患者搬送も発生するなど国際的拡大の兆候があり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリア（対象国外）における輸入エボラ症例とその後の疑い例に関するもの。DRCは地域的な比較統計（累計症例数・死亡者数）として言及されているのみで、本イベントの発生国ではないため verified_locations には含めない。対象国リストに該当する国での発生は確認されなかった。

article.articleHeadline: Число жертв Эбола в ДР Конго превысило 5000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola death toll in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceeds 5,000.
article.articleSummary: As of October 31, 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has recorded a cumulative Ebola death toll exceeding 5,000 from a renewed outbreak since mid-May. Total confirmed deaths: 5,026, with 10,351 infections. Currently, 1,101 people are under treatment or in quarantine, and 2,788 recovered. Experts caution that the true burden may be higher, as the virus likely circulated undetected at least since February, months before the official outbreak declaration on May 15. The outbreak is driven by a rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, which initially eluded standard tests. The epidemic began in Ituri Province in the northeast and subsequently spread to remote northern and eastern areas affected by ongoing unrest. The article highlights the scale of the outbreak and the potential for undercounting due to testing challenges and conflict-affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴでのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 死者5,000人・感染者10,000人超の大規模アウトブレイクで、紛争地域での拡大や検査の課題により国際的拡大・公衆衛生への深刻な影響が懸念されるため。
triage.notes: まれなBundibugyo株によるアウトブレイクで、紛争地域における検査の遅れから実際の感染規模はさらに大きい可能性が指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Nigeria reports two suspected Ebola cases in northeast region
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola cases are under investigation in northeast Nigeria, with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention isolating the patients and conducting contact tracing and laboratory testing; confirmation awaits laboratory results as of Oct 31, 2026. The cases follow Nigeria’s confirmation of its first Ebola case in more than a decade last week—a Swiss woman who travelled to Uganda and returned to Abuja—who, along with her husband, was evacuated to Switzerland. Authorities have not said whether the two suspected cases are linked to the initial patient. If confirmed, the new cases could indicate local transmission within Nigeria, raising major public health concerns. The Congo outbreak epicenter remains the Democratic Republic of Congo, with more than 5,000 deaths since May; Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases. The Bundibugyo species behind the Congo outbreak has no approved treatments or vaccines.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリア北東部でエボラ出血熱の疑い例2件を報告
triage.triage_reason: ナイジェリアで10年以上ぶりに確認されたエボラ患者（スイスへ渡航後帰国）に続き、新たに疑い例が報告され国内伝播の可能性が懸念される。DRCでは5000人超の死者を出す大規模アウトブレイクが継続中であり、国際的拡大リスクも高い。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリアでの疑い例2件だが、ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCは震源地として実質的に発生が確認されている国であるため含めた。ナイジェリアの疑い例が確認された場合、さらなるリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: El ébola roza los 5.000 muertos en el Congo: casi la mitad de los infectados han fallecido
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola nears 5,000 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: nearly half of those infected have died.
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus has reached 4,992 deaths and 10,274 infections as of 28 October, with a case fatality rate around 48.6%. The outbreak spans multiple regions, including Ituri in the northeast and North Kivu and Haut-Uele, with 66 health zones affected across eight provinces. There is no licensed vaccine or antiviral specifically for Bundibugyo; existing Ebola vaccines target other strains and are not proven for Bundibugyo, though experimental vaccines and treatments are under investigation. The World Health Organization maintains an international response amid security, displacement, and access challenges, with many deaths occurring in communities and outside treatment centers. Internationally, cases linked to the DRC outbreak have been reported in Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths), Nigeria (1 case), Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths, plus a probable), and France (1 case recovered; no active cases noted).

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱が5,000人の死者に迫る：感染者のほぼ半数が死亡
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約48.6%、感染者1万人超・死者約5千人に達し、ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・フランスへの国際的拡大も確認されており、IHR基準の複数に該当する重大な公衆衛生事象。
triage.notes: ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリア・フランスへの波及症例が報告されているが、いずれも対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。主要発生国はDRCのみ。Bundibugyo株には認可済みワクチン・抗ウイルス薬が存在せず、治療アクセスにも課題があるため、フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola ultrapassa 5 mil mortes no Congo e chega a 50% de letalidade
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola surpasses 5,000 deaths in the Congo and reaches a 50% case fatality rate.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths, with 10,351 cases and 2,788 recoveries as of Oct 31, 2026, a case fatality rate near 50%. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus and has spread to eight of 26 provinces and 67 of 178 health zones, led by Ituri and North Kivu (9,782 infections and 4,792 deaths combined). Symptoms include fever, weakness, muscle pains, headache, vomiting, and diarrhea; severe cases may involve hemorrhage and organ failure. The WHO warns of persistent transmission and early identification challenges; about 80% of new cases lie outside monitored contact chains amid conflict and limited resources. There is no approved vaccine or specific treatment; care is supportive, with vaccines under study. Prevention focuses on avoiding contact with blood, bodily fluids, and contaminated objects; border controls advised.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱による死者が5000人を超え、致死率50%に達する
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ出血熱が大規模流行し致死率約50%、8州67保健区に拡大、新規症例の80%が接触者追跡圏外にあるなど、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する深刻な公衆衛生イベントであるため。
triage.notes: WHOも持続的な伝播と早期発見の課題を警告しており、ワクチン・特異的治療法が未承認である点も国際的懸念を高めている。

article.articleHeadline: Pancaroba Picu Risiko ISPA hingga DBD, Dokter Ingatkan Orang Tua Jaga Kesehatan Anak
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Seasonal transition increases the risk of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) and dengue fever, doctors remind parents to protect their children's health.
article.articleSummary: Seasonal transition to the rainy season in Indonesia heightens risks of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) including influenza A, with children being especially vulnerable. In Jakarta, pediatric specialist Dr. Mulki Angela urges basic hygiene (handwashing, bathing, clean clothing) and hydration, noting that smoke from forest and land fires can worsen respiratory symptoms. As rain begins, dengue fever risk rises due to conditions favoring mosquitoes; communities should eliminate standing water and apply the 3M Plus mosquito-control measures. Limited access to clean water may elevate gastrointestinal infections (diarrhea, vomiting) and fungal skin infections. The guidance, supported by Jakarta and Jember, East Java academics, emphasizes protecting children and the elderly, ensuring complete immunizations, and considering vitamin D supplementation when appropriate. Additional advice includes cough etiquette, mask use around the ill, and preparing rain gear to maintain children's health during pancaroba.

triage.headline_ja: 季節の変わり目がARI(急性呼吸器感染症)からデング熱までのリスクを高める、医師が保護者に子供の健康管理を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 季節性の一般的な健康注意喚起記事であり、特定のアウトブレイクや異常事態の報告ではないため、トリアージ基準に該当しない。
triage.notes: 本記事は季節性疾患（インフルエンザA、デング熱等）に関する一般的な予防啓発情報であり、具体的な症例数増加やアウトブレイクの報告は含まれていない。

article.articleHeadline: Власти Нигерии сообщили о выявлении двух случаев с подозрением на Эболу
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nigerian authorities report two suspected Ebola cases.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, two people in northeast Nigeria are in isolation with suspected Ebola virus infection; investigations and contact tracing are ongoing, with laboratory results pending to confirm or rule out infection. Earlier, a 42-year-old wife of a Swiss diplomat who had Ebola and had arrived in Nigeria from Uganda was evacuated to Switzerland. The global Ebola situation remains dominated by the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak, which has over 10,351 reported cases and more than 5,000 laboratory-confirmed deaths (case fatality 48.6%), since it began on 15 May in DRC and Uganda and has affected eight DRC provinces. Uganda announced containment on 28 July, confirmed by WHO on 25 August. Kenya reported its first Ebola case on 6 October, underscoring ongoing regional transmission concerns.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリア当局、エボラ疑いの2症例を確認したと発表
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラアウトブレイクは10,351症例・5,000人超の死亡（CFR48.6%）という深刻な規模であり、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・スイスへの波及が確認されるなど国際的拡大が継続しているため、IHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 記事の主たる発生地域はDRC（大規模アウトブレイクの中心）。ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・ケニア・スイスは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。スイス人外交官の妻の症例はウガンダ由来の輸入例であり、ナイジェリアの疑い例は未確定（検査結果待ち）。

article.articleHeadline: Farmers urged to get jabs amid fears over mutant flu 'super-virus'
article.articleSummary: Scotland urges thousands of animal workers—farmers, farm staff, vets, inspectors, transport drivers, and abattoir personnel—to take a free flu vaccine via the NHS to prevent a theoretical reassortment between animal (avian and swine) flu and human flu into a novel, highly contagious ‘super-virus.’ Public Health Scotland leaflets warn that simultaneous infection with bird flu and human flu could enable a new virus to spread easily and cause severe illness due to low immunity. The campaign is framed as a precaution to protect society, not only individuals. WHO surveillance published earlier this month reports high levels of swine and avian flu in animals globally. In the past month, several people in China and Cambodia contracted avian flu, and one Brazilian woman died after swine flu. The vaccine is offered to those working with cattle, pigs, and poultry to mitigate this risk.

triage.headline_ja: 変異型インフルエンザ『スーパーウイルス』への懸念の中、農業従事者にワクチン接種を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: 中国・カンボジアでのヒト鳥インフルエンザ感染、ブラジルでの豚インフルエンザによる死亡例が報告されており、動物由来インフルエンザの再集合体（リアソータント）による新型ウイルス出現への懸念から公衆衛生当局が予防的ワクチン接種キャンペーンを実施している点で、重大性・異常性の両面でIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事の主眼はスコットランドでの予防接種キャンペーンだが、背景として中国・カンボジアでのヒト鳥インフルエンザ感染例、ブラジルでの豚インフルエンザ死亡例が言及されている。カンボジアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。ヒト－ヒト感染や国際的拡大の実証的証拠はまだ無く、続報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Nigéria registra dois casos suspeitos de Ebola na região nordeste
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nigeria reports two suspected Ebola cases in the northeast region.
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola cases are being investigated in Nigeria's northeast, with individuals isolated as authorities conduct contact tracing and laboratory testing; confirmation is pending. This follows Nigeria's confirmation last week of its first Ebola case in more than a decade—a Swiss woman who had travelled to Uganda and returned to Abuja—who along with her husband was transported to Switzerland. If the two suspected cases are confirmed, Nigeria could face domestic spread, though authorities did not state whether they are linked to the first case. The Democratic Republic of Congo remains the outbreak epicenter, with more than 5,000 deaths since May; neighbouring Kenya and Uganda have also reported cases. There are no approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain involved.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリア北東部でエボラ出血熱の疑い例2件を確認
triage.triage_reason: ナイジェリアで10年以上ぶりの確定例に続き疑い例が発生し国内拡大の懸念があること、DRCでは5000人超の死者を出す大規模流行が継続中であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要と判断した。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はナイジェリアの疑い症例だが、ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。DRCは現在進行中の大規模流行地として実際に発生が確認されているため含めた。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Kisangani : désinfection d'une école primaire après un décès suspect - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Kisangani: disinfection of a primary school after a suspected death - ACP
article.articleSummary: In Kisangani, the Maleke primary school in Kabondo commune, Tshopo Province, was fully disinfected on Oct 31, 2026, two weeks after the death of a teacher at the school amid Ebola concerns. The provincial Ebola response team deemed disinfection necessary since the teacher worked there. The death occurred in the community after treatment in a private health center, and the family did not arrange a secure and dignified burial due to lack of risk awareness. The director said classes will not be suspended and urged students and staff to return on Monday. The public health intervention follows the teacher’s death on Oct 16 and the confirmation of two positive Ebola cases in his household, including his wife, highlighting the need for heightened vigilance against school-based transmission in Tshopo.

triage.headline_ja: キサンガニのエボラ: 疑い死亡後に小学校を消毒 - ACP
triage.triage_reason: DRCコンゴ・キサンガニで学校関係者のエボラ疑い死亡後、家族内で2例の陽性が確認されており、ヒト-ヒト感染と地域拡大の懸念がある。公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と異常事態としてIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: 教師の死亡（10/16）後、適切な安全な埋葬が行われず、家族内で2例の陽性が確認された。学校内での感染拡大防止のため消毒が実施されたが、授業は継続予定。地域内のエボラ対応チームが既に稼働しており、今後の感染者数や対応状況の続報を要確認。

article.articleHeadline: В Нигерии сообщили о выявлении двух случаев с подозрением на Эболу
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Two suspected Ebola cases identified in Nigeria.
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola cases identified in northeast Nigeria; both isolated, contact tracing initiated, and medical histories reviewed, with laboratory confirmation pending. On Oct 26, a 42-year-old woman, wife of a Swiss diplomat, with confirmed Ebola infection, was evacuated from Nigeria to Switzerland after arriving in Nigeria by plane from Uganda; Uganda reported no outbreak. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, lab-confirmed Ebola deaths exceeded 5,000, with 10,351 confirmed cases and a case fatality rate of 48.6%. The outbreak began May 15 in DR Congo and Uganda and has affected eight provinces. Uganda declared the outbreak over on July 28, with WHO confirming this on August 25. Kenya reported its first Ebola case on Oct 6.

triage.headline_ja: ナイジェリアでエボラ出血熱の疑い症例が2件確認
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国での大規模流行（確定症例10,351件、死亡5,000人超、致死率48.6%）に加え、スイス人外交官夫人の確定症例、ケニア初症例、ナイジェリアでの疑い症例など国際的拡大が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア、スイス、ケニア、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCでの流行が主要な発生地域として確認された。ナイジェリアの疑い症例はラボ確認待ちであり、続報の注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Εμπολα: Πάνω από 5.000 νεκροί στο φονικότερο ξέσπασμα στην ιστορία του Κονγκό
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: More than 5,000 dead in the deadliest outbreak in the history of Congo
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo reports over 5,000 deaths and more than 10,300 confirmed Ebola cases from the Bundibugyo strain, in the deadliest outbreak in the country’s history. Since May, the epidemic has spread to eight of 26 provinces, with the epicenter in Ituri’s northeast, a conflict zone complicating response. Cases have also appeared in Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths) and in Nigeria and Uganda, marking the outbreak’s regional reach. A confirmed case in early October involved a woman airlifted to Switzerland for treatment. The World Health Organization notes the death toll rising faster than in prior waves; there is no approved vaccine or specific therapy for Bundibugyo. Diagnostic testing, treatment trials, and vaccine studies are underway. Attacks on health workers and aid personnel have impeded control efforts; the 2018–2020 DRC outbreak caused 2,299 deaths. Global context includes West Africa’s 2014–2016 outbreak with over 11,325 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱:コンゴの歴史上最も死者数の多い流行で死者5,000人超
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行は死者5,000人超・症例10,300件超と同国史上最悪規模であり、複数国（ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ、さらにスイスへの搬送例）への拡大も確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当しフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ケニア・ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・スイスでも症例が報告されているが、対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ。紛争地域（イトゥリ州）での対応困難、ワクチン・治療薬未承認（ブンディブギョ株）が流行制御の障害となっている。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola ultrapassa 5.000 mortos na República Democrática do Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola surpasses 5,000 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) since May has reached 5,026 deaths among 10,351 confirmed cases, with data through Oct 29. The epicenter is Ituri, with North Kivu accounting for about 58% of new cases. The flare spans 67 health zones across eight provinces, including Ituri, North Kivu, Tshopo, Bas-Uélé, Haut-Uélé and South Kivu. Recovered 2,788; 1,101 hospitalized or in isolation; contact tracing covers 84.5% of identified contacts. On Oct 28, AU and WHO urged response after warning the outbreak was out of control. The pathogen is Bundibugyo Ebola virus; no approved vaccines or treatments exist. Ervebo vaccination began in August, but efficacy against Bundibugyo is unproven and used under research protocols. Outside DRC, Uganda reports 20 cases and 2 deaths (15 imported); Kenya 9 cases; Nigeria 1; France linked. Transmission via blood and bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea; severe cases may bleed.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、コンゴ民主共和国で死者5,000人を突破
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱がDRCで大規模流行し、複数国への越境拡大（ウガンダ、ケニア、ナイジェリア、フランス関連）が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランスへの関連症例も報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。AU・WHOが制御不能と警告し支援を要請している点も重要。

article.articleHeadline: Polícia investiga suspeita de gripe aviária após resgate de araras debilitadas no DF
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Police investigate suspected avian influenza after rescue of weakened macaws in the Federal District.
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza is suspected in the Federal District of Brazil after rescue of several weakened macaws in Vicente Pires, Planaltina, Asa Sul, and Sobradinho. As of 2026-10-31, the Environmental Military Police Battalion reported macaws with lethargy, ruffled feathers, and difficulty or inability to fly, without visible injuries. Multiple cases within a short period prompted suspicion, but the illness has not been confirmed. The birds were forwarded to Hospital da Fauna for veterinary evaluation and investigation of potential causes. The public is advised not to capture or handle debilitated wild birds and to contact authorities at 190. There are no confirmed human cases reported. Investigations aim to determine whether avian influenza is present and identify possible infection sources; results await laboratory confirmation. The incident highlights wildlife health surveillance in the Distrito Federal.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジル連邦直轄区で衰弱したコンゴウインコ救助後、鳥インフルエンザ疑いを警察が調査
triage.triage_reason: 野生鳥類での鳥インフルエンザ疑い事例だが、検査未確定でヒト感染例もなく、情報不足のため続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: 野生のコンゴウインコ（野鳥）における鳥インフルエンザ疑い事例であり、検査結果待ち。ヒト感染例の報告はなし。環境軍警察が調査中。

article.articleHeadline: Vietnam: Ho Chi Minh City reports rise in dengue
article.articleSummary: Between Oct 19 and 25, Ho Chi Minh City reported 1,785 dengue cases, 9.7% above the four-week average, indicating high transmission with potential increases in coming weeks. Since the start of the year, the city has recorded more than 42,500 dengue cases and 11 deaths. Rainy-season conditions are boosting mosquito breeding; prevention focuses on removing breeding sites, eliminating larvae, and addressing high-risk areas in residential communities. Households should spend 10–15 minutes weekly checking and cleaning surroundings, keep water containers tightly covered, and remove bottles and other objects that collect stagnant water, with regular checks of areas where mosquitoes may breed. Residents should seek medical attention if dengue symptoms arise; fever should be assessed at a healthcare facility rather than self-medicating. Dengue can become severe after fever subsides; warning signs include severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding, lethargy, or cold extremities requiring immediate care.

triage.headline_ja: ベトナム:ホーチミン市でデング熱が増加
triage.triage_reason: デング熱は流行地での季節性増加であり異常性は低いが、症例数増加と死亡例があるため経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: ホーチミン市における季節性デング熱の増加で、地元当局による予防啓発が中心。国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは示唆されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Bagpat News: मौसम बदलते ही वायरल ने पकड़ ली रफ्तार
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bagpat News: As the weather changes, the virus has gained momentum.
article.articleSummary: Bagpat, India — Amid seasonal weather shifts, viral infections have surged in Bagpat. The district hospital's outpatient department (OPD) logged over 800 patients on Saturday, with roughly 70–80% suffering from flu, viral fever, cold, or respiratory infections. Children and the elderly are the hardest hit, and the pediatric wards are densely crowded. Similar crowding is reported at CHCs, PHCs, and private hospitals across the district. The changing climate has coincided with rising cases of pneumonia and gastrointestinal infections among children, with many seriously ill youngsters requiring daily emergency admissions. Doctors warn against laxity and against taking antibiotics without medical consultation, urging adherence to proper medical guidance to prevent inappropriate antibiotic use and complications.

triage.headline_ja: バグパットニュース：季節の変わり目にウイルス感染が急増
triage.triage_reason: 季節性のインフルエンザ・ウイルス性感染症の通常の季節的増加であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 地域ローカル紙による季節性ウイルス感染症（インフルエンザ・風邪等）の増加報告であり、通常の気候変動に伴う現象として報道されている。

article.articleHeadline: Stray dogs bite at least 20 commuters at Chennai Central in two months
article.articleSummary: Chennai Central has recorded at least 20 dog-bite cases at the emergency care unit run by Apollo Hospitals in the past two months; railway officials report four to five weekly complaints. About 25 stray dogs roam the premises, with bites reported near Gates 6. The station handles one lakh daily. In a 1:45am incident, Anandh was bitten after three stray dogs chased him near the station entrance. The emergency unit lacked anti-rabies vaccine; patients receive wound care, a tetanus shot, and are referred to Govt General Hospital. A senior medical officer warned that sterilisation alone does not protect against rabies, and vaccination must occur within a prescribed window. In Nov 2025, the Supreme Court ordered removal of stray dogs from public places with an eight-week deadline; nearly a year later, dogs remain. Greater Chennai Corporation commissioner G S Sameeran says a special drive will be organised and relocated community dogs.

triage.headline_ja: チェンナイ・セントラル駅で野良犬が過去2か月に少なくとも20人の通勤客を襲う
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病ワクチン不足と野良犬による咬傷の継続的発生が報告されているが、実際の狂犬病感染例の報告はなく、現時点では個別の公衆衛生インフラ問題にとどまる。
triage.notes: 狂犬病ワクチンの供給不足が救急医療施設で報告されている点は公衆衛生上の懸念だが、記事は野良犬対策の行政対応の遅れが主題であり、狂犬病感染の確定例は言及されていない。

article.articleHeadline: Έμπολα: Ξεπέρασαν τους 5.000 οι νεκροί στη ΛΔ Κονγκό
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: The death toll in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed over 5,000 people, the deadliest outbreak there and the second-largest globally. Since May, more than 10,300 cases have been confirmed in eight of the DRC's provinces, with a case-fatality rate about 48.6%. The outbreak is spreading fastest in Ituri province, where armed conflict hinders access. It has surpassed the 2018–2020 outbreak (2,299 deaths) and trails only West Africa’s 2014–2016 outbreak (over 11,300). Attacks on health workers complicate response; a nurse was killed and another worker seriously injured, and locals accuse responders of polluting water. Outside DRC, Uganda has 20 cases and 2 deaths; Kenya 9 cases and 2 deaths; Nigeria 1 case with two suspected. Bundibugyo ebolavirus; no approved vaccine or specific therapy yet, though trials are underway and care is supportive. Transmission is via direct contact with blood or bodily fluids; Europe risk remains very low per ECDC.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：コンゴ民主共和国での死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: DRCで過去最悪規模のエボラ流行（死者5,000人超、致死率48.6%）が発生し、ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの国際拡大も確認されているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: 記事内ではウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの感染拡大も報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。発生地域にAngolaが含まれていたが本文中で言及がないため除外した。武装勢力による医療従事者への攻撃や水質汚染の訴えなど対応の困難さも報告されている。

article.articleHeadline: Kolhapur's Seva Hospital gets MRI, CT scan facilities, yellow fever centre
article.articleSummary: Kolhapur's Seva Rugnalaya (Services Hospital) in Kasba Bawada opened MRI and CT imaging facilities, an Integrated Public Health Laboratory (IPHL), and a yellow fever vaccination centre. Inaugurated by state health minister Prakash Abitkar, the event highlighted efforts to provide free or affordable care at public hospitals and to boost trust in Maharashtra's public-health system. Attendees included State Planning Commission head Rajesh Kshirsagar, MP Shahu Chhatrapati, mayor Rouparani Nikam, district collector Vijay Rathod, and ZP CEO Jasmine. Abitkar announced an 'Arogya Samvad Yatra' to review health services and a dedicated mobile app to lodge online complaints about deficiencies. Kolhapur aims to become a medical hub, with Seva and CPR Hospitals serving western Maharashtra; priority treatment is anticipated for residents of Line Bazaar, Kasba Bawada, and Kadamwadi. Seva Hospital, once Victoria Diamond Jubilee Hospital, traces back to 1897.

triage.headline_ja: コルハープールのセヴァ病院にMRI・CTスキャン設備と黄熱病センターが新設
triage.triage_reason: 記事は病院の設備拡充（MRI・CT・黄熱病予防接種センター開設）に関する行政的な話題であり、実際の黄熱病の発生や症例報告ではない。
triage.notes: 記事は病院のインフラ整備（黄熱病ワクチン接種センター開設含む）に関する報道であり、黄熱病の発生事例や患者情報は記載されていない。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يتوسع في الكونغو.. 5 آلاف وفاة منذ مايو الماضي
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola spreads in Congo... 5,000 deaths since last May.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues, with 5,026 deaths and 10,351 confirmed cases since mid-May, health authorities told AFP. About 1,101 people remain in treatment or under quarantine, and 2,788 have recovered. Officials caution the true toll may be higher, noting evidence the virus has circulated since February. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo strain. Abroad, Kenya reports cases connected to a Kenyan infected in Congo who later died. Nigeria records its first Ebola case on Oct 20—a Swiss woman who developed symptoms days after returning from a weeks-long trip to Uganda. Europe has one case, a doctor in France in June after a humanitarian mission in eastern Congo, who subsequently recovered. The developments underscore ongoing cross-border transmission risks from eastern Congo.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱がコンゴで拡大…昨年5月以降5,000人超が死亡
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ流行が5,000人超の死亡者を出し、ケニア・ナイジェリア・フランスへの越境感染も確認されており、IHR基準の複数（重大な公衆衛生影響・異常性・国際拡大）に該当するためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断する。
triage.notes: 発生地域にフランス・ケニア・ナイジェリアが含まれるが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。主たる発生地はDRC東部であり、同国からの越境感染事例として他国症例が報告されている。

article.articleHeadline: Újabb országban szabadulhatott el a halálos kór: hosszú évek után üthette fel a vírus a fejét
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In yet another country, the deadly disease could break loose: after many years, the virus has reared its head.
article.articleSummary: Two new Ebola-suspected cases are under investigation in northeast Nigeria, with both isolated and contact tracing underway as laboratory tests are conducted to confirm infection. A decision will await test results. This follows Nigeria’s first confirmed Ebola case in more than a decade last week—a Swiss woman who had been in Uganda and later returned to Abuja; she and her husband were moved to Switzerland. If the two new cases are confirmed, Nigeria could have intra-country transmission. The Africa outbreak focus remains the Democratic Republic of Congo, where since May the Bundibugyo strain has killed more than 5,000 people; Kenya and Uganda have reported cases. No approved drug or vaccine exists for Bundibugyo Ebola.

triage.headline_ja: またも新たな国で死の病が拡大か：長年を経てウイルスが再び頭をもたげた
triage.triage_reason: ナイジェリアで10年以上ぶりにエボラ確定例が発生し国内伝播の疑いがある新規2例も調査中であり、さらにDRCでは5月以降ブンディブギョ株により5000人超が死亡するなど深刻な越境拡大が続いているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・ケニア・スイスでの事例が記事の主題だが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。DRCは対象国かつ実際の主要発生国として含めた。ブンディブギョ株には承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しない点も要注視。

article.articleHeadline: Kongo DR Ebolas upuru skaits pārsniedz 5000
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo Ebola death toll exceeds 5,000.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reported 10,351 Ebola infections and 5,026 deaths since the outbreak was first detected in mid-May. Currently 1,101 people are receiving treatment or in quarantine, and 2,788 have recovered. The official toll likely undercounts, as experts say the virus may have circulated undetected since February, months before the 15 May outbreak declaration. The outbreak is driven by the rare Bundibugyo variant and was not initially detected by conventional tests. It began in Ituri Province in northeastern DRC and then spread to northern and eastern districts. Ebola has appeared in other African countries: Kenya has reported several cases and deaths since early October, and a Swiss citizen infected in Nigeria was evacuated to Switzerland on 26 October, Nigeria's first confirmed case in this outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ出血熱による死者数が5000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱が大規模流行し、複数国（ケニア、ナイジェリア、スイス）に拡大しているため、IHR基準を複数満たしフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ナイジェリア・ケニア・スイスでも症例が確認されているが、対象国リストにはDRCのみ該当。ナイジェリアは対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。感染は2月から未検出のまま拡大していた可能性があり、過小報告の懸念あり。

article.articleHeadline: Apollo Foundation Screens 11,000 People For TB In High-Risk Areas Of Chittoor
article.articleSummary: Chittoor district, Aragonda, Andhra Pradesh, sees TB screening expansion through Apollo Foundation’s Total Health initiative with the state government. In the last year, over 11,000 people in 10 mandals were screened, yielding 90 suspected TB cases. Sushela, 45, from Aragonda reported chest burning and cough during center waiting. High-risk groups—over 60, diabetics, smokers, alcohol users, people living with HIV, TB contacts, BMI<18.5—are prioritized; 100–150 people are screened daily free of cost. Mobile teams use chest X-rays, with images transmitted to Hyderabad for radiologist review via teleradiology; an AI-assisted system estimates TB probability, but specialists validate findings and the algorithm does not confirm diagnosis. Abnormal X-rays prompt sputum testing by TruNat to detect TB and drug resistance. Government teams confirm cases, register on Nikshay, and start treatment; MDR TB can be identified within an hour. Apollo also provides nutrition kits to support treatment and follow-up.

triage.headline_ja: アポロ財団、チットール県の高リスク地域で11,000人を対象に結核スクリーニングを実施
triage.triage_reason: 通常の結核スクリーニング活動の報告であり、異常発生や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す内容はなく、IHR・WPRO基準のいずれにも該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: My girl, 25, died after docs said don't worry about flu - it was hideous disease
article.articleSummary: Daisy, 25, of Cirencester, UK, fell ill in January 2025 with flu-like symptoms and swollen glands that doctors dismissed as a viral infection. Her condition escalated into haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH), a rare immune disorder triggered by infection, with over-activation of T-cells and macrophages causing inflammation and damage to liver, spleen and bone marrow. She developed a rash, high temperature, swollen organs, anaemia, and kidney failure requiring dialysis, ultimately needing an induced coma. After a trip to Cambodia and Vietnam, then the Philippines, she deteriorated upon returning to the UK. A bone marrow biopsy confirmed HLH, and she died on February 22, 2025, at 9am. HLH is extremely rare in the UK, with estimates of about 1.2 cases per million children and roughly one in 50,000 births; urgent specialist treatment is required.

triage.headline_ja: 25歳の娘、医師に『インフルエンザは心配ない』と言われた後に死亡 ― 恐ろしい病気だった
triage.triage_reason: 英国在住の一個人の稀少疾患（HLH）による死亡例の human interest記事であり、公衆衛生上の集団発生や国際的拡大のリスクを示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 個人の症例報告（英国在住者）であり、カンボジア・ベトナム・フィリピンへの渡航歴は言及されているが、これらの国での感染症発生や集団事例を示すものではない。対象国での発生とは認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Deaths in Democratic Republic of the Congo Exceed 5,000
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, Ebola deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have surpassed 5,000. The figure was reported from Kinshasa in October by the Saudi Press Agency. A World Health Organization official stated that about one-third of these fatalities occurred outside treatment centers, before patients could be tested, complicating efforts to contain the outbreak. The disclosure highlights a critical obstacle in outbreak response: deaths occurring in the community prior to diagnosis hinder surveillance, case finding, and timely isolation. The report underscores the ongoing severity of the Ebola outbreak in the DRC and the persistent challenge of managing transmission when patients die outside of care settings.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ死者数が5,000人を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱による死者数が5,000人を超え、地域社会内での未診断死亡が多発し感染拡大・サーベイランスの深刻な障害となっているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大イベントと判断。

article.articleHeadline: Cavalos detectam vírus que ameaçam saúde humana
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Horses detect viruses that threaten human health.
article.articleSummary: Rabies concerns rise after seven horses die at a Goiás farm in September 2026, with laboratory confirmation in one animal and three workers monitored, illustrating how horses serve as sentinels and trigger One Health responses in Brazil. The case underscores rabies vaccination for domestic animals and pre‑exposure prophylaxis for high‑risk workers, though coverage remains incomplete. Beyond rabies, horses can indicate circulation of West Nile virus and Eastern/Western equine encephalitis in a region, guiding public health actions. In 2026, Brazil reported four human West Nile cases (two in Santa Catarina, two in São Paulo). In 2025, three human Venezuelan equine encephalitis cases were recorded in Tabatinga, Amazonas. West Nile was first isolated in Espírito Santo in 2018. Separately, research on bumped kinase inhibitors in horses, including BKI-1708 against Sarcocystis neurona, informs development for equine myeloencephalitis and potential human applications, though CNS penetration was subtherapeutic in this study.

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية: 5026 وفاة وأكثر من 10 آلاف إصابة
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: 5,026 deaths and more than 10,000 infections.
article.articleSummary: as of October 31, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 5,026 deaths and over 10,351 infections since mid-May. About 1,101 patients are under treatment or in isolation, with 2,788 recovered; authorities warn the true toll may be higher. The outbreak is linked to Bundibugyo ebolavirus and may have circulated since February before the May 15 declaration. Exported/imported cases include Kenya (a Kenyan infected in DRC who later died); Nigeria (first case on October 20 in a woman who developed symptoms after a weeks-long trip to Uganda); and Europe (a doctor infected in France during a June humanitarian mission in eastern DRC, who recovered). The data reflect confirmed cases/deaths to date, with ongoing transmission within the DRC remaining a concern.

article.articleHeadline: Costa Rica registra 6,285 casos de dengue y 974 de chikungunya en lo que va de 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Costa Rica records 6,285 dengue cases and 974 chikungunya cases so far in 2026.
article.articleSummary: Dengue infections in Costa Rica rose 36% in 2026, totaling 6,285 cases by epidemiological week 41, with 98 dengue patients presenting warning signs. The outbreak is concentrated in Alajuela province (2,724 cases), notably in Orotina canton (2,249.1 per 100,000; 572 total) and Grecia (704 cases, 865 per 100,000). Central Alajuela canton has 627 cases; La Cruz, Guanacaste, 233. Concurrently, a chikungunya outbreak totals 974 notifications, with 847 PCR-confirmed and 127 probable cases. The Chorotega region accounts for over 59% of chikungunya (576 cases), led by La Cruz canton with 390; Alajuela 114; Carrillo 83; San José 65; Santa Cruz 59. Vector-control actions include 501,113 household visits, over 3.1 million breeding sites treated/destroyed (1.7 million deposits treated, 1.3 million containers destroyed), and 783,751 house fumigations. PAHO regional alerts and cross-border cooperation accompany these efforts.

article.articleHeadline: في الكونغو.. "أرقام مرعبة" تخص وفيات فيروس إيبولا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Congo, "Harrowing numbers" pertain to deaths from the Ebola virus.
article.articleSummary: As of Oct 31, 2026, Democratic Republic of Congo health authorities report Ebola deaths surpassing 5,000, with 5,026 confirmed deaths and 10,351 infections since the outbreak began in mid-May. About 1,101 people remain in treatment or under isolation, while 2,788 have recovered. Officials warn the true toll may be higher than official counts. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, with transmission intensifying within Congo and linked cases reported in other countries, including Kenya, where a Kenyan national infected in Congo died. Health authorities estimate that the actual mortality and incidence could be higher than reported. Suspected circulation of the virus dates back to February, months before the May 15 official declaration. The evolution underscores ongoing, high-risk transmission and cross-border spillovers.

article.articleHeadline: Le nombre de décès attribubale à l'Ebola au Congo dépasse les 5000 | L'actualité
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of deaths attributable to Ebola in the Congo exceeds 5,000 | L'actualité.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 5,026 deaths among 10,351 infections (case fatality ~50%), caused by Bundibugyo virus. Declared mid-May, the eastern provinces of Ituri and North Kivu are the epicenters with 9,782 confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths. The outbreak has spread to 67 of 178 health zones across 8 of 26 provinces; 50 zones report active transmission. No vaccine or specific antiviral exists; treatment is supportive. About 2,788 people have recovered. Approximately 80% of new cases stem from transmission chains outside known contact tracing; one-third of deaths occurred outside care centers before testing. Insecurity and distrust hinder response, with armed conflict (including M23), attacks on health workers, and strikes over unpaid salaries at treatment centers such as Tchomia in Ituri (five confirmed, ten suspected). The figures echo the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak (11,000 deaths).

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent-wide spread mounts
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, Congo's Ebola outbreak (Bundibugyo virus) has 5,026 deaths from 10,351 infections, with 2,788 recoveries; no vaccine or specific therapy exists, so care is supportive. Declared mid-May, the outbreak spans 67 of 178 health zones across eight of 26 provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu as epicenters: 9,782 confirmed cases and 4,792 deaths there. About 80% of new cases stem from transmission chains outside monitored contacts, and roughly one-third of deaths occur outside treatment centers, hindering containment. Ongoing conflict, tracing/testing gaps, distrust, and unpaid health workers impede response, including strikes at Tchomia in Ituri (5 confirmed, 10 suspected). Cross-border cases have appeared: Kenya (8 cases, 2 deaths) and Nigeria (1 case evacuated to Switzerland); earlier Uganda reported cases. The outbreak is the second-deadliest in history, after West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic (≈11,000 deaths).

article.articleHeadline: 剛果埃博拉疫情喪生破5千人 蔓延多國 | 非洲
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo Ebola outbreak death toll surpasses 5,000 as it spreads to multiple countries | Africa
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola outbreak has surpassed 5,000 deaths with over 10,000 infections as of Oct 31, 2026, spreading to Kenya and Nigeria in October after Uganda previously reported cases. Eight provinces are affected, with Ituri and North Kivu in the east the hardest hit. The case-fatality rate is about 50% (5,026 deaths among 10,000+ infections). About one-third of deaths occurred outside testing and treatment centers, and roughly 80% of new cases are not on the original contact-tracing lists, indicating widespread undetected transmission. The outbreak began mid-May and is the second-deadliest Ebola outbreak in history. Healthcare workers face security challenges and wage arrears, including attacks on staff and shuttered treatment centers; a nurse was killed responding to alerts. Ongoing armed conflict and strained health capacity hinder containment and response, with the virus spreading to multiple neighboring countries.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱、死者5000人超え 複数国に拡大 | アフリカ
triage.triage_reason: 致死率約50%、死者5000人超・感染者1万人超の大規模アウトブレイクが複数国（ケニア、ナイジェリア、ウガンダ）に拡大しており、IHR基準の複数該当とWPRO基準の全項目該当が認められるため、フルRRAへ進むべき事案。
triage.notes: 発生地域にナイジェリア、ウガンダ、ケニアが含まれるが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。コンゴ国内の東部（イトゥリ、北キブ）が最も深刻で、紛争による対応困難、約80%の新規症例が接触者追跡リスト外という点から、検知されていない感染拡大が懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Más de 5,000 muertos por brote de ébola: la enfermedad se sigue propagando en África
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 5,000 dead from an Ebola outbreak: the disease continues to spread in Africa.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has claimed 5,026 lives and infected 10,351 people, yielding a case-fatality rate of about 50%. The outbreak continues to spread in the DRC, with reports of cases in other African nations according to official data published on Saturday. The most recent flare of hemorrhagic fever linked to Bundibugyo virus was declared in mid-May, and health authorities have faced difficulties in containing it since. The figures indicate sustained transmission and a heavy mortality burden, underscoring ongoing public health challenges in surveillance, containment, and healthcare capacity across affected regions. The report provides no details on which neighboring countries are affected.

triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ(ブンディブギョウイルス)流行が死者5,000人超・感染者10,000人超と深刻な公衆衛生インパクトがあり、周辺国への拡大も報じられているためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 記事では近隣国への拡大が示唆されているが具体国名は不明。致死率約50%と非常に高く、5月から継続する大規模流行。

article.articleHeadline: தாராபுரம்: டெங்கு காய்ச்சலுக்கு 6 வயதுச் சிறுமி உயிரிழப்பு
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dharapuram: Six-year-old girl dies of dengue fever.
article.articleSummary: Six-year-old Jayasree from Dharapuram, Tiruppur district, died of dengue fever on Friday after rapid clinical decline. She had been admitted to Palani Government Hospital in severe fever, then transferred to Dharapuram Government Hospital where intensive care was provided. Laboratory findings indicated rapid leukopenia (decline in white blood cells). Six additional patients with dengue-like symptoms were admitted to the Dharapuram hospital's ICU. The family hails from Vathambacheri village in Coimbatore district. With dengue concerns rising in Dharapuram and surrounding areas, the Tamil Nadu government is urged to deploy special health surveillance teams to monitor fever patients in government and private hospitals and ensure requisite tests and treatments.

triage.headline_ja: タラプラム：デング熱で6歳の少女が死亡
triage.triage_reason: インドの一地域（タミル・ナードゥ州）における散発的なデング熱死亡例・ICU入院例の報告であり、単一地域の流行拡大懸念はあるが国際的拡大やIHR通報相当の基準には達していないため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドの流行地域で季節的に発生する既知の疾患であり、本記事は地域的な症例クラスターと死亡例の報告。地方政府へのサーベイランス強化要請があるが、国際的な影響は現時点で不明。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : 129 cas de choléra et 14 décès enregistrés à Mbandaka
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: 129 cholera cases and 14 deaths recorded in Mbandaka.
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak in Mbandaka, Democratic Republic of Congo (Équateur province) with 129 cases and 14 deaths (as of 30 October 2026), and 68 recoveries. Bolenge health zone accounts for 104 cases (epicenter); Wangata health zone 77 cases. Of the 14 deaths, 11 occurred in the community and 3 in cholera treatment centers (CTCs) at Wangata and Bolenge. Sixteen Bolenge patients were transferred to Wangata, which is treating 41 patients; Bolenge CTC has observed 47 recoveries and Wangata CTC 21. Seven new cases were admitted to both centers. Bolenge CTC is about 9 km from Mbandaka. Outbreak likely linked to docking of three boats from Kinshasa (Maluku, Kingabwa) toward Kisangani, Mbandaka, Basankusu; HB Hanawa arrived a week ago, with ~800 passengers and ~100 symptomatic. Response includes enhanced community/media awareness (PNCPS/ACSA), preventive measures (handwashing, avoiding physical greetings, disinfecting motor-taxis, boiling drinking water), and port controls at Iyonda (Bolenge) and Ex-Onatra (Mbandaka) to screen and isolate suspected cases.

triage.headline_ja: DRC：マバンダカで129件のコレラ症例と14人の死亡を記録
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国マバンダカで129例・死者14名（致死率約10.8%）のコレラ集団発生が継続中で、複数保健ゾーンに拡大し船舶を介した感染拡大の懸念があるため、フルリスク評価への移行が妥当と判断。
triage.notes: コレラはDRCで風土病的に発生するが、今回はキンシャサ発の船舶（HB Hanawa号、乗客約800人中約100人が有症状）を介した複数都市間の感染拡大リスクが指摘されており、水系感染症としての拡大可能性に注意が必要。致死率が高い点も懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RD Congo : Plus de 5 000 personnes meurent d'Ebola lors de l'épidémie la plus meurtrière qu'ait connue la RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: More than 5,000 people die from Ebola during the deadliest outbreak the DRC has ever seen
article.articleSummary: More than 5,000 people have died from the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), with over 10,300 confirmed cases across eight of its 26 provinces. The outbreak began in May and, by August, became the deadliest in the DRC, with a case fatality rate of 48.6%. The epicenter is Ituri province in the northeast, a conflict zone complicating containment. Cases have been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda. This is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC and the second deadliest globally; the UN notes it is spreading at a faster pace. The Bundibugyo strain is responsible; there is no approved treatment or vaccine. WHO Africa urges stronger control measures, better access to affected areas, and community outreach, with ongoing tests, treatments, and vaccine trials. Uganda reports 2 deaths and 20 cases (no new cases since August) with travel restrictions for entrants from DRC; Kenya 9 cases and 2 deaths; Nigeria 2 suspected cases.

article.articleHeadline: Muertes por ébola en Congo superan las 5.000 mientras crece preocupación por propagación en África
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Deaths from Ebola in Congo exceed 5,000 as concern grows over its spread in Africa.
article.articleSummary: Death toll from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000, with 5,026 fatalities among 10,351 confirmed infections, a case-fatality rate near 50%, according to the Congolese Ministry of Health. The data, reported from Bunia, reflect the persistence of a hemorrhagic fever outbreak caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. The latest outbreak episode was declared in mid‑May 2026, and authorities have struggled to contain transmission since. Beyond the DRC, authorities report cases in other African nations, underscoring regional concern about spread. The article notes government data published on a Saturday but provides no detailed laboratory confirmation, transmission chains, or infection source. The ongoing situation calls for sustained public health measures to curb further morbidity and prevent exportation of cases.

article.articleHeadline: Ébola supera las 5,000 muertes y aumenta la alerta en África - ABRIENDO BRECHA
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola surpasses 5,000 deaths and raises the alert in Africa
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths, with 10,351 cases reported as of 31 October 2026. Declared in May 2026, it is the most deadly Ebola outbreak in DRC history and the second deadliest globally after 2014–2016 West Africa (about 11,000 deaths). The Bundibugyo virus variant is responsible; there is no vaccine or approved specific treatment, with care limited to supportive measures. Eight provinces are affected: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo, Haut-Uele, Bas-Uele, Sud Ubangi, and Nord Ubangi, with Ituri bearing a large share of cases and deaths. Challenges include under-detection outside treatment centers, weak health systems, insecurity, attacks on health workers, and misinformation. Kenya, Nigeria, and Uganda have reported linked cases. WHO emphasizes surveillance, contact tracing, and cross-border cooperation to curb further spread.

article.articleHeadline: El ébola deja más de 5.000 muertos en el Congo y se abre paso hacia otros países
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola leaves more than 5,000 dead in the Congo and is making its way to other countries.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has surpassed 5,000 deaths with 10,351 confirmed cases as of Oct 29, 2026. Case fatality rate stands at 48.6% with 2,788 recoveries and 1,101 patients still hospitalized or in isolation. The surge centers in Ituri and North Kivu, where conflict, limited access, and diagnostic delays hinder response. No approved vaccines or treatments exist for the Bundibugyo variant. A notable transmission case traveled from Buta through Aketi, Likati, Bondo, Kisangani, and Beni in DRC, then Uganda (Kampala) and Kenya (Entebbe Airport) before dying in Nairobi on Oct 5; WHO maps a 14-stage itinerary of the journey. Kenya tallied nine cases (eight linked to the index patient) and two deaths by Oct 26; Uganda reported 20 cases (including 15 imported) and two deaths; Nigeria confirmed a related case in October. Emphasis on border surveillance, contact tracing, isolation, and exploratory vaccines; many deaths occur outside treatment centers.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ出血熱による死者5,000人超、他国への拡大進む
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）大規模流行が5,000人超の死者を出し、ワクチン・治療薬未承認のままウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへ越境拡大しており、IHR基準の複数該当とWPRO基準も複数該当するため即時フルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダ・ケニア・ナイジェリアへの越境症例が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。DRC国内（イトゥリ、北キブ、ブタ等）が主発生地である。

article.articleHeadline: Acre registra 1.440 casos de covid-19 em 2026, com concentração de 74% no segundo semestre
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Acre records 1,440 COVID-19 cases in 2026, with 74% concentrated in the second half of the year.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in Acre, Brazil totaled 1,440 confirmed cases in 2026, with 1,068 (about 74%) in Aug–Sep and 96 in Oct so far, per the Ministry of Health’s Covid-19 Influenza-like Illness panel. August: 591; September: 477; earlier months were low (Jan 102, Feb 53, Mar 39, Apr 30, May 18, Jun 17, Jul 17). Women account for 68% of infections; ages 20–39 lead with 491 cases, followed by 40–59 with 476 (together ~67%). Elderly: 60–70 has 161 cases; 71+ has 99. Adolescents and younger children contribute fewer cases. Race: pardos 59.65%; white 16.60%; yellow 13.75%; unknown 7.22%; black 2.22%; Indigenous 0.56%. Health professionals 63; pregnant/puerperal 5; essential workers 1. Incidence rate 40.93. A sharp rise since August signals ongoing circulation, especially among young adults and women; authorities urge vaccination, masking in risk settings, and seeking medical care for persistent flu-like symptoms.

triage.notes: 既知の疾患（COVID-19）に関する定例の統計報告であり、死亡数や重症例の急増、医療逼迫等の記載はない。

article.articleHeadline: ▷ Ministerio de Salud reporta repunte del 36,6 % en casos de neumonía y alerta sobre virus respiratorios #31Oct
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health reports a 36.6% uptick in pneumonia cases and issues an alert about respiratory viruses #31Oct.
article.articleSummary: Venezuela reported a 36.7% rise in pneumonia in week 40 (4–10 Oct) with 2,638 cases nationwide, up from 1,920 in week 39. Infants under one year are most affected, incidence 438.33 per 100,000. Children aged 1–4 show high case concentration, with Amazonas state reporting 34.10 per 100k, Zulia 15.20, and Trujillo 12.40. Acute respiratory infections totalled 54,301 in week 40, up 23.2% week-on-week, impacting especially children 1–5 years in Amazonas, Trujillo and Yaracuy. Influenza accounted for 441 positive cases, 52% in ages 5–39; circulating subtypes include A(H1N1)pdm09, A(H3N2), and B Victoria lineage. Yellow fever remains under strict surveillance; through week 40 Venezuela has 12 confirmed cases and 4 deaths, CFR 33.3%. OPS/OMS alerts drive nationwide monitoring. Keywords: vaccination, outbreak, public health measures.

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يتوسع في الكونغو.. 5 آلاف وفاة منذ مايو الماضي
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola spreads in the Congo... 5,000 deaths since last May.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Bundibugyo strain) has killed at least 5,026 people and infected over 10,351 since the mid-May start of the outbreak, health authorities say. About 1,101 patients remain in treatment or under quarantine, with 2,788 recoveries reported. Officials warn the true toll may be higher, with evidence of viral circulation as early as February, before the May 15 official announcement. The outbreak has spilled beyond Congo, with cases in Kenya linked to a Kenyan infected in Congo who died; Nigeria reporting its first case on Oct 20 in a Swiss woman who developed symptoms after a trip to Uganda; Europe’s single case in France involving a doctor who recovered after a humanitarian mission in eastern Congo. The Bundibugyo strain continues to drive transmission; monitoring and containment are ongoing.

article.articleHeadline: More than 5,000 die from Ebola in DR Congo's deadliest outbreak
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has claimed over 5,000 lives and surpassed its previous deadliest epidemic as of this week. Initiated in May, the Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak has recorded more than 10,300 confirmed cases across eight of 26 provinces, with Ituri province in the northeast remaining the epicenter. The case fatality rate is 48.6%. There is currently no approved treatment or vaccine for Bundibugyo Ebola. Ongoing violence and attacks in the conflict zone hinder containment; a nurse was killed and another health worker seriously wounded, and residents have blamed responders for water contamination. Cases have crossed borders to Kenya (9 cases, 2 deaths) and Uganda (20 cases, 2 deaths), with Uganda maintaining border travel restrictions; Nigeria reports two suspected cases, one confirmed, in October. Europe assesses very low infection risk. The outbreak underscores the need for expanded controls, access, and community engagement.

triage.headline_ja: DRコンゴで5,000人超がエボラで死亡、過去最悪の流行に
triage.triage_reason: 死者5,000人超・致死率48.6%の大規模流行で、国境を越えてケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリアに拡大しており、IHR基準の複数該当と高い社会的関心が確認される。
triage.notes: ケニア・ウガンダ・ナイジェリアへの越境感染が報告されているが、これらは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。紛争地域での治安悪化により対応が困難、承認済み治療薬・ワクチンも存在しない点が特筆される。

article.articleHeadline: Residents burn Ebola treatment center in north-central DR Congo
article.articleSummary: Two rooms for suspected Ebola cases were burned in Bafwasende, a rural town in north-central DR Congo’s Tsopo province, as residents set fire to an Ebola treatment center before guards extinguished the blaze in the early morning. Medical director Marcel Likilo said responders fled to Kisangani and suspected patients were transferred to Nia-Nia in neighboring Ituri province. The incident underscores persistent community resistance amid an outbreak caused by the Bundibugyo virus, coming one week after a health worker was lynched during an Ebola alert. Ongoing transmission is reflected in Health Ministry figures: confirmed Ebola cases surpass 10,000 with more than 5,000 deaths since mid-May, highlighting containment challenges in the region."

article.articleHeadline: Nigeria investigates two suspected Ebola cases as outbreak spreads across Africa | News.az
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola cases in Nigeria’s northeastern region are in isolation as the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) awaits laboratory confirmation and conducts contact tracing after Nigeria reported its first infection in more than a decade last week. Authorities say results will determine if the two suspected cases represent new infections; tracing is underway to assess exposure and prevent transmission. It remains unclear whether the suspected cases are linked to the imported infection of a Swiss woman who travelled to Uganda and returned to Abuja; she and her husband were evacuated to Switzerland on Oct 26. If confirmed, the cases could signal onward transmission within Nigeria. The broader outbreak in Africa centers on the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with over 5,000 deaths since May; Uganda and Kenya have reported infections. The Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain has no approved vaccines or specific treatments.

triage.triage_reason: DRCを中心に5000人以上の死者を出すエボラ流行が複数国に拡大しており、ナイジェリアでも10年ぶりの感染例に続き疑い例が発生するなど、IHR基準・WPRO基準の双方で複数該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はDRCを震源とするエボラ流行とその波及（ナイジェリア、ウガンダ、ケニア、スイス）。対象国リストに該当するのはDRCのみ。ナイジェリア・ウガンダ・ケニアは対象国リスト外のため除外。

article.articleHeadline: Attempted Fire at Ebola Center Under Construction in DRC | EconoTimes
article.articleSummary: Attempted arson at an Ebola treatment center under construction in Bafwasende health zone, Tshopo province, DRC, where two rooms for suspected Ebola patients reportedly burned; the facility had not yet opened. Guards intervened; other reports describe an attempted attack with stones, with no damage assessment communicated. The center is being built by International Medical Corps and was planned to have 20 beds (8 suspected, 12 confirmed). Health workers reportedly left Bafwasende, with suspected patients being taken to Nia-Nia; local youths expressed resistance, linking Ebola spread to medical staff. World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus noted a nurse was killed and another health worker seriously injured during an Ebola-alert response in Bafwasende on Oct 24. INSP SitRep No. 168 (dated Oct 29) lists 77 new confirmed Ebola cases nationwide. MSF reported last confirmed-diagnosis patients had left the Mongbwalu center.

The article highlights ongoing outbreak dynamics and cross-border transmission risks.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Death Toll Surpasses 5,000 in Congo as Deadly Outbreak Spreads Across Africa - [your]NEWS
article.articleSummary: DR Congo's ongoing Ebola outbreak has killed 5,026 people and infected 10,351 as of Oct 31, 2026, with a case fatality rate around 49%. The outbreak, caused by Bundibugyo virus and declared in mid-May, has spread beyond the DRC into eight provinces and neighboring countries, with Ituri and North Kivu accounting for the majority (9,782 cases, 4,792 deaths) across 67 health zones. There is no approved vaccine or virus-specific therapy; care relies on supportive management. About 2,788 patients have recovered. Roughly 80% of newly identified cases are not linked to known contacts, indicating transmission chains remain unidentified. Around one-third of deaths occurred outside treatment centers, as insecurity, attacks on health workers, and distrust impede response. Ongoing conflict in eastern regions complicates surveillance and delivery of vital care.

article.articleHeadline: Minsa atiende brote de dengue con 35 casos confirmados en Miramar, Colón
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health addresses dengue outbreak with 35 confirmed cases in Miramar, Colón.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, approximately 35 confirmed dengue cases are reported in Miramar, Santa Isabel district, on Colón’s Costa Arriba in Panama. The Ministry of Health (Minsa) deployed a multidisciplinary response team—physicians, nurses, vector-control technicians, environmental sanitation, laboratory, health promotion, pharmacy, and epidemiology—to manage the outbreak and reinforce prevention and vector-control measures. Actions are coordinated through the Colón Health Region with support from the Nombre de Dios Health Center, and ambulance transfers remain available for affected individuals. Inspections identified dengue mosquito breeding sites inside homes and in surrounding areas. Residents are urged to eliminate containers and any spaces where water can accumulate to prevent Aedes aegypti proliferation and curb transmission. No deaths reported; ongoing surveillance and preventive interventions are in place.

article.articleHeadline: 甲流併發休克 7歲長期病女童危殆 - 20261101
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza A (H1N1) infection complicated by shock; a 7-year-old girl with a chronic illness in critical condition - 20261101.
article.articleSummary: As of 31 October 2026, a case of Influenza A (H1N1) infection with septic shock in a 7-year-old girl with a chronic illness is in critical condition in Hong Kong. On 29 September she developed runny nose, diarrhea and abdominal pain; the next day fever and seizures led to admission at Tuen Mun Hospital, later transferred to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit. Respiratory samples tested positive for Influenza A (H1N1). Preliminary CHP investigation: no travel during incubation; not vaccinated for the 2026/27 seasonal flu vaccine; household contacts asymptomatic; three classmates with mild flu. School infection control measures were advised; investigation ongoing. Hong Kong’s flu season began in late June and has persisted ~4 months, still above baseline. This season there have been 28 severe pediatric influenza cases: 20 recovered, 2 stable, 4 critical, 2 deaths. Vaccine protection wanes after ~9 months; vaccination urged.

article.articleHeadline: Health authorities probe two suspected Ebola cases in northeast Nigeria
article.articleSummary: Two suspected Ebola cases identified in Nigeria's northeast are isolated as contact tracing and laboratory testing proceed, following Nigeria's Oct 20 declaration of its first Ebola case in over a decade. The cases relate to the Bundibugyo strain circulating in the region; a Swiss woman who traveled from Uganda tested positive and was evacuated to Switzerland with her husband, a Swiss diplomat. The Democratic Republic of the Congo outbreak, which began in May, is the largest on record there, with more than 10,300 confirmed cases and over 5,000 deaths across eight provinces; no approved treatment or vaccine exists for Bundibugyo Ebola, though vaccine trials are underway. Africa CDC cites weaknesses in early detection and contact tracing, noting only about 12% of confirmed DRC cases were identified from known contacts. Since May, Bundibugyo cases have appeared in DRC, Uganda, France, Kenya, and Nigeria.

article.articleHeadline: Mãe pede ajuda para garantir suplementos nutricionais ao filho após grave infecção cerebral
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mother seeks help to secure nutritional supplements for her son after a severe brain infection.
article.articleSummary: Valmir Rodrigo da Silva, 37, from Campo Grande, Brazil, suffers mobility-limiting sequelae after a severe brain infection and now depends on constant care, requiring daily caloric and protein nutritional supplementation. He was admitted to Hospital Universitário Maria Aparecida Pedrossian on May 29 in a coma due to suspected brain infection; after six months in coma, he was discharged in early September and returned home under pallative care. Valmir is treated at Hospital São Julião, with his mother Maria Aparecida, a retiree who stopped working to care for him. The family, residents of the São Jorge da Lagoa neighborhood, reports financial hardship and has not yet received INSS assistance. A raffle to raise funds was organized but failed; donations can be made via Pix key 44834179168 to help cover supplements and care.
